title: Epic: CI and build foundation
description:
No CI exists in this repo: no .github/, no workflow file, no CI configuration of any kind. Build, cargo fmt, cargo clippy and all 83 test suites are manual steps enforced only by CLAUDE.md.

The codebase is already written for a CI that does not exist. machines/tests/input_contract_test.rs:11 explains that the suite avoids MachineEntry::create because 'CI does not have' ROMs — the design accommodation was made, the runner never was.

Deliberately small and first, so every later epic is checked automatically from here on.

Baseline measured at 89c1b92: 3,165 tests passing across 83 suites, plus one environment-only failure covered by child .2.
close_reason:
All three children closed; the project now has automated verification it did not have before.

.1 CI workflow (b90dcc1, refined in a8e3085) — .github/workflows/ci.yml with three jobs: 'check' (fmt, clippy -D warnings, workspace tests, pinned to the flake's rustc 1.95.0) gating every push and PR; 'future' (same lints on current stable, continue-on-error) as an early-warning signal; 'validate' (submodules, generated M6800/M6809 vectors, all 7.1M) weekly plus workflow_dispatch. Verified green on GitHub, and 'validate' verified to genuinely validate rather than skip — 2,577,000 I8088, 1,604,000 Z80 and 1,000,058 M68000 vectors passed in a 6-minute job, with the explicit presence check confirming all six vector sets present.

.2 Validator skip (dfca3be) — scope proved wider than filed: cpu-validation/test_data is gitignored in full, so ALL six validators panicked on a fresh checkout, not just i8088. Added require_test_data() and converted all six.

.3 Release profile (72ac233) — lto = 'fat', codegen-units = 1, kept on measured evidence: +15.0% joust, +9.4% pacman, +8.3% galaga, +4.7% marble against a ~1.7% noise floor.

Two things this epic surfaced that are tracked elsewhere rather than left implicit: the vector generators write relative to CWD so the documented command silently misfires (contained-fidelity-np9x.7, currently worked around in the validate job by working-directory plus a presence check), and the toolchain pin now lives in both flake.lock and the workflow with nothing enforcing agreement — noted in the workflow comment, to revisit if it drifts.

title: CI: run fmt, clippy and the workspace test suite on push and PR
description:
Add .github/workflows/ci.yml running, in order: cargo fmt --all --check; cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -D warnings; cargo test --workspace.

Notes:
- flake.nix already pins the toolchain (cargo, rustc, clang, SDL2, pkg-config, libGL). Either use the Nix shell in CI or install SDL2 via apt — phosphor-frontend is the only crate needing system packages, so core/machines/macros/harness can build on a plain toolchain if a split job is preferred.
- Do NOT check out the cpu-validation submodules in the default job: the single-step suites are designed to skip without them (see sibling .2). A separate scheduled job can init submodules and run the full 7.1M-vector validation.
- ROM-gated tests (frameshot parity, future golden frames) already skip cleanly when PHOSPHOR_ROMS is unset.

Acceptance: a red CI on a deliberately introduced clippy warning and on a failing test; green on 89c1b92 as-is.
close_reason: Implemented in b90dcc1 as .github/workflows/ci.yml. Two jobs: 'check' (fmt --check, clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test --workspace, all --locked) on push to main + PRs, with SDL2/GL installed via apt since --workspace builds phosphor-frontend; and 'validate' (submodules: true, generate M6800/M6809 vectors, run all 7.1M) on a weekly cron plus workflow_dispatch. The split keeps per-push CI fast while still validating the CPUs regularly. Two hazards handled explicitly: the generators write relative to CWD so they run under working-directory: cpu-validation (underlying bug filed as contained-fidelity-np9x.7), and 'validate' asserts every vector directory exists before running, because a skipped validator reports success and libtest captures its skip message. Baseline verified green before landing: fmt exit 0, clippy no warnings, 3165 tests passing. Not yet exercised on GitHub — first real run happens on push.

title: All six single-step validators should skip, not panic, without vector data
description:
In a checkout without submodules the M6502, M6800, M6809, Z80 and M68000 single-step tests each report '0 passed' and move on. The I8088 one panics:

  cpu-validation/tests/i8088_single_step_test.rs:189
  'No SingleStepTests data. Run: git submodule update --init cpu-validation/test_data/8088'

It is the one test that turns a fresh CI run red for an environment reason rather than a code one. Reproduced at HEAD in a clean worktree.

Fix: match the five siblings — eprintln! the hint and return, rather than panic.

Acceptance: cargo test --workspace passes in a submodule-free checkout.
close_reason: Fixed in dfca3be. Scope was wider than filed: cpu-validation/test_data is gitignored in full, so a fresh checkout has neither the four SingleStepTests submodules nor the generated M6800/M6809 sets — all six validators panicked, not just i8088. (The earlier 'five skip gracefully' reading was wrong: cargo stops after the first failing test binary, so the other three submodule-backed validators were never reached, and the '0 passed' lines were the lib and gen_* bin targets.) Added require_test_data() to the cpu-validation lib and converted all six to return early through it. Verified in a submodule-free worktree: six ok/1-passed results, zero panics, message visible under --nocapture. Noted in the doc comment that libtest captures the message for a passing test, so the real guard against a permanently-skipping validator is the scheduled full-validation job, not the eprintln.

title: Tune the release profile: fat LTO and codegen-units=1
description:
Cargo.toml:6-13 raises dev builds to opt-level 2 for real-time emulation and then never mentions [profile.release], so release ships stock: no LTO, 16 codegen units.

The workload is one hot loop calling across three crate boundaries per emulated cycle (machines -> core CPU -> core devices), which is exactly the case cross-crate inlining serves.

  [profile.release]
  lto = 'fat'
  codegen-units = 1

Acceptance: measured against the benchmark harness. Record before/after frames-per-second in a comment; keep the change only if it helps. Blocked on the benchmark issue only for the measurement, not for the edit.
close_reason:
Landed in 72ac233. [profile.release] lto = 'fat', codegen-units = 1.

Kept because it measurably helps, per the issue's own acceptance criterion. Measured with phosphor-bench (600 frames, 120 warmup, 5 reps, best of two full runs each side; tool noise floor ~1.7%):

  machine   emul ms/f before -> after   fps change
  joust           0.746 -> 0.648           +15.0%
  pacman          0.845 -> 0.772            +9.4%
  galaga          1.021 -> 0.935            +8.3%
  marble          2.473 -> 2.355            +4.7%
  tempest         1.146 -> 1.131            +1.3%  (within noise)

Four of five boards improve well clear of the noise floor. Tempest is flat, consistent with it spending proportionally more time inside phosphor-core's AVG and Mathbox devices, where calls were already intra-crate and inlinable — i.e. the win really is cross-crate inlining, which is the mechanism the issue predicted.

Cost is release build time only. CI's gating 'check' job runs the test suite under the dev profile and is unaffected; the scheduled 'validate' job builds release and trades a slower build for a faster 7.1M-vector run. Observed ~50s to rebuild the bench binary's dependency chain after the change.

Side note worth carrying forward: this is the first use of phosphor-bench in anger, and it did the job — the effect was large enough to be unambiguous against the noise floor, which is evidence the tool is sensitive enough for the concrete-bus-dispatch A/B it was built for.

title: M6809 reset sequence costs 0 emulated cycles
description: Cpu::reset for the M6809 (core/src/cpu/m6809/mod.rs:616) reads the FFFE/FFFF vector outside the tick loop, so the reset sequence consumes no emulated cycles. MAME's cycle-stepped core spends 4 (base6x09.lst INTERRUPT_VECTOR: dummy_vma, vector hi, vector lo, dummy_vma). Measured on esb: our first instruction begins at machine cycle 2, MAME's at 7 — 4 cycles of vector fetch plus 1 because ORCC #imm costs 3 on MAME and 2 on ours. Not the cause of j63p (verified inert: correcting it leaves the first divergence, the bank-change counts and the derail cycle all bit-identical), but it is a real fidelity gap and probably applies to every CPU whose reset() fetches vectors outside the clock. Also check ORCC/ANDCC #imm timing against the datasheet — 3 cycles is the documented figure.
close_reason: Fixed in b9942fa. RESET_SEQUENCE_CYCLES = 4, burned in execute_cycle before the first fetch; at_instruction_boundary is false while they run. The correct figure is 4, not the 5 the raw measurement suggested: MAME's INTERRUPT_VECTOR is 4 cycles (base6x09.lst:51) and the extra 1 was our trace's labelling convention (it tags an instruction with the cycle the previous one finished). +5 was tried first and overshot by one instruction. ORCC #imm was NOT wrong at 2 cycles as first suspected — it is 3, matching MAME; that reading came from misreading a held-CPU trace. Verified: first divergence from MAME moves 454,189 -> 463,991 and the run-wide cycle offset drops to the -1 of the labelling convention. Does not fix j63p on its own.

title: Epic: Concrete bus dispatch (remove the per-access vtable)
description:
README.md:264 describes the Bus trait as 'compile-time polymorphism with no vtable overhead'. That is the design intent and not what ships.

core/src/core/bus.rs:96 — bus_split! coerces the machine to &mut dyn Bus, and all 91 execute_cycle call sites across machines/src pass a trait object (264 bus_split! sites in total). So every memory read, opcode fetch and device write in every running machine goes through a vtable — millions per second per CPU — and, more costly than the indirect call itself, the optimiser cannot inline bus dispatch into the CPU inner loop or keep board state in registers across it.

Largest single structural performance item in the codebase.

Root cause: the trait object exists only to work around the borrow split, because CPU and bus state live in one struct. Separating them (struct X { cpu: Z80, bus: XBus }) makes self.cpu.execute_cycle(&mut self.bus, ..) borrow-check natively at a concrete type, monomorphising the whole loop and deleting the unsafe as a side effect.

Sweeping — roughly 40 machine files — so this epic is deliberately prototype-first. The design doc is written from prototype results, not before them.

Blocked by the benchmark harness (nothing here is arguable without it) and by golden frames (this is exactly the change most likely to move pixels).

title: Correct the README's vtable claim
description:
README.md:264 states the Bus trait gives 'compile-time polymorphism with no vtable overhead'. Every shipped machine dispatches through &mut dyn Bus, so the claim is false today regardless of what the rest of this epic concludes.

Fix now, independently of the refactor: describe what actually happens and why (the borrow split), and reference this epic as the intended direction. If the refactor lands later, update again.

Trivial, unblocked, and worth doing immediately so the document stops misleading.
close_reason: README.md:311 now describes the actual dispatch (bus_split! -> &mut dyn Bus, virtual call per access, unsafe reborrow because CPU and bus state share a struct) and points at this epic. Commit 66a4f84.

title: Prototype: convert Pac-Man to concrete-typed bus dispatch and measure
description:
First prototype — chosen for the cleanest signal: single Z80, one AddressSpace16, one board struct.

Split NamcoPacBoard so CPU state and bus state are separate fields of the wrapper, then call self.cpu.execute_cycle(&mut self.bus, BusMaster::Cpu(0)) directly with a concrete bus type. Remove the bus_split! use and its unsafe on this path only.

Report:
- frames/sec before and after, from the benchmark harness
- whether the generated inner loop actually inlines bus dispatch (cargo asm or perf)
- how much of the board had to move, and what fought back

Do not generalise yet. The point is a number and a shape, not coverage.

Blocked by the benchmark harness.
close_reason:
Converted in 498374b. Shape: the board keeps everything the Z80 talks to, the CPU moves up into the game wrapper, and the two are disjoint fields, so cpu.execute_cycle(&mut board, ..) borrow-checks natively. Base decoding (A15 mirror, IM2 vector latch) became 'impl Bus for NamcoPacBoard'; Ms. Pac-Man's daughter card became MsPacmanBus, a view struct built from disjoint field borrows (split()), since its state is not board state. bus_split! and its unsafe are gone from this hardware.

Codegen: the Pac-Man Z80 cycle instantiation has 0 indirect calls vs 48 in the dyn one -- the vtable really is gone. But bus dispatch became a *direct call* to bus_read_common/bus_write_common (29+17 sites), not an inlined access: those functions are too big to inline (page lookup, watchpoint check, trace check).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 12 alternating runs of both binaries, host under load ~12): pacman emul 0.756 -> 0.737 ms/f, -2.5%. Core-pinned rounds with +/-0.5-1.7% spread: 1.733 -> 1.704, -1.7%. mspacman similar. So the vtable is worth ~2%, not the 'largest structural item' the epic assumed.

What fought back:
1. The BusDebug derive. With the CPU out of the board, the board loses cpus() and its debug read/write arms. Fixed generally in 057a13d: #[debug_bus] merges a nested BusDebug, and map-driven read/write arms no longer require a local #[debug_cpu].
2. Cpu::reset takes '&mut dyn Bus + 'static', which a borrowed view struct cannot satisfy. Worked around for Z80 (reset ignores the bus) by resetting against the board. CPUs that fetch a reset vector -- 6502, 6809, 68000 -- will need Cpu::reset generic over the bus before their boards can convert.
3. MachineDebug::debug_tick assumed bus_split! + board.tick(bus); added a split_cpu arm calling the machine's inherent step_cycle().

Golden frames unchanged for all 39 machines.

title: Prototype: convert Galaga (3x Z80) and measure
description:
Second prototype — confirms whether the win scales to a multi-CPU board, where vtable dispatch should cost most: three Z80s sharing NamcoGalagaBoard, plus the 06XX/51XX devices ticking per cycle.

This is also where the borrow split is genuinely harder: three CPUs and the board all want to move independently, and namco_galaga.rs:461 mutates board state (namco51 LLE, interrupt latches) around each CPU tick.

Report the same three things as the Pac-Man prototype, plus: whether a shared-bus-with-multiple-CPUs shape needs a different pattern than the single-CPU case.

Blocked by the Pac-Man prototype.
close_reason:
Converted in 3d8886b (galaga + digdug + xevious together -- they share NamcoGalagaBoard).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 8 alternating runs, idle host):
  galaga  0.887 -> 0.759 ms/f  -14.5%
  xevious 1.164 -> 1.037       -10.9%
  digdug  2.091 -> 1.956        -6.5%
  pacman  0.748 -> 0.706        -5.6%  (unchanged binary, re-measured idle: the -2.5% in .2 was taken under load average 12)

So the win is real and scales with CPU count on a shared bus, as the epic expected -- galaga (3 Z80s) gains 2.5x what pacman does.

Shape for multi-CPU: the CPUs group into one GalagaCpus field beside the bus; the board's tick splits into begin_cycle/latch_pc/end_cycle and the per-cycle sequence becomes a free generic fn over a NamcoGalagaBus trait. Each game's bus is a view struct of disjoint field borrows (board + that game's bus-visible state). No new pattern was needed for multiple CPUs -- the same split works, because the three CPUs are stepped by one generic tick that holds the bus.

The load-bearing finding: WHERE the split happens decides whether the change wins at all. Splitting per cycle (the obvious translation of the old per-cycle tick) made galaga 6% SLOWER than the trait object (0.883 -> 0.938) -- a multi-pointer view rebuilt 50,688 times a frame costs more than the indirect call it removes. Hoisting the split to once per frame-boundary run turned that into -14.5%. Pac-Man, whose bus needs no view at all (the board *is* the bus), never had this problem.

Also: SAVE_VERSION 4 -> 5, since the CPU block now precedes the RAM block in these machines' state. Golden frames unchanged for all 39 machines.

title: Decision and design doc from the prototype results
description:
With two measured data points, decide: roll out across roughly 40 machine files, apply selectively to the hot boards, or abandon.

If proceeding, write docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md covering the target struct shape, what happens to bus_split! and its three arms (u16, u32, u32-word), how multi-bus-master boards (blitter, DMA, DmaVram) fit, the migration order, and the mechanical ast-grep pattern for the bulk of the work.

Then decompose the rollout into per-board-family child issues under this epic.

Blocked by both prototypes.
close_reason:
Decision: PROCEED with the full rollout. Design doc written at docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md (commit 23f89d7) from the two prototypes' measured results.

Numbers that decided it (idle host, best of 8 alternating A/B runs): galaga -14.5%, xevious -10.9%, digdug -6.5%, pacman -5.6% emulation ms/frame. Codegen confirms the mechanism: 0 indirect calls in the converted Z80 cycle instantiation vs 48 in the dyn one. The win scales with how much of a frame is CPU cycles, so multi-CPU boards gain most.

The doc covers: the two target shapes (board-is-the-bus, preferred; bus view of disjoint field borrows where the game interposes state), the per-family generic tick, frame-boundary renders, what the BusDebug derive needed (#[debug_bus]), the SAVE_VERSION bump rule, and the load-bearing constraint -- split once per run, never per cycle, since a per-cycle split measured 6% SLOWER than the trait object.

Open problems recorded: Cpu::reset takes '&mut dyn Bus + 'static' and blocks every reset-vector CPU (6502/6809/68000); Williams' blitter as a second bus master; the two wide-bus bus_split! arms (which are not width-specific work -- they vanish with the trait object).

Rollout decomposed into child issues, ordered by payoff per unit of risk:
  bek7 (P1) Cpu::reset generic over the bus  <- blocks the four below
  129w      TKG-04 (Donkey Kong, DK Jr, Mario Bros)
  hwd9      Galaxian + MCR II
  ra3r      Do Castle family
  8v1a      Williams (blocked by bek7)
  hv5p      Atari DVG/AVG family (blocked by bek7)
  3hnp      Atari System 1 + Gottlieb System 80 (blocked by bek7)
  642d (P3) standalone machines, then delete bus_split! (blocked by bek7)
Plus icym (related): an inlinable fast path for backed-memory reads -- the next lever, available only because dispatch is now concrete.

CLAUDE.md (machines + core) and the README were updated to describe the mixed state rather than the old advice.

title: Invert run_frame to scanline-outer / cycle-inner
description:
Every board's tick() opens with clock % cycles_per_frame, a scanline-boundary divisibility test, and a ladder of frame-position comparisons — VBLANK, sound NMI scanlines, watchpoint context latching — all evaluated on every one of the roughly 50,000 cycles in a frame to be true on a few hundred of them. Galaga runs this ladder three times per cycle, once per Z80.

  machines/src/namco_pac.rs:451-492
  machines/src/williams.rs:465
  machines/src/namco_galaga.rs:461

The divisions themselves are likely folded to multiplies since the timing constants are const, so this is about branch volume and instruction cache rather than division cost — but the structure is doing per-frame work at per-cycle frequency.

Fix: run_frame iterates scanlines outer, cycles inner. Boundary work then happens 264 times per frame instead of 50,688, and the inner loop shrinks to CPU-plus-device ticks.

Independent of the dispatch change but touches the same loops, so sequence them together. Blocked by the benchmark harness and by golden frames — this reorders when board state is observed relative to CPU execution, which can legitimately move pixels.
close_reason:
Done for the Namco boards in 2b1667f (namco_pac + namco_galaga). Williams was deliberately left out: it still dispatches through bus_split!, so its inversion is folded into its conversion issue (8v1a), whose notes now carry the pointer.

Shape: the board's per-cycle work splits into begin_scanline (render, VBLANK, 51XX TC pin, sound-NMI scanline timer -- all of which fire on scanline boundaries) and begin_cycle_inner (no frame-position test at all). run_scanlines iterates scanlines outer / cycles inner; run_frame and run_cycles route whole scanlines through it and any partial scanline through the per-cycle tick, so a clock the debugger left off-phase still runs the identical cycle sequence. tick remains the debugger's single-cycle path. Both paths call the same pieces of work, so they can only differ in how often the frame position is tested.

Measured (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, idle host) -- this change, and cumulative against the dyn baseline the epic started from:
  galaga  0.759 -> 0.646  -14.9%  (-27.2% cumulative)
  xevious 1.037 -> 0.850  -18.0%  (-27.0%)
  pacman  0.706 -> 0.611  -13.5%  (-18.3%)
  digdug  1.956 -> 1.826   -6.6%  (-12.7%)
Dig Dug gains least because much of its frame is the background tilemap renderer, which neither change touches.

Golden frames unchanged for all 39 machines.

title: Epic: Contained fidelity and coverage fixes
description:
Six independent, well-scoped items from the codebase review. No shared design, no ordering between them — take them as appetite allows. Grouped only so they do not get lost between the large structural epics.

Three are hardware-fidelity gaps (68000 byte strobes, 6522 timers, x86 disassembler); three are coverage gaps (MB88xx/I8035 validators, untested devices, frontend logic).

title: 68000 byte writes should be a single half-word transaction, not a word RMW
description:
core/src/cpu/m68000/README.md, 'Word bus' section: a byte write is implemented as read-word / patch-byte / write-word. Correct for RAM and it passes state-only validation, but it is wrong against any side-effecting memory-mapped register — the read half triggers a phantom access the hardware never performs, and the write half puts a stale value back into the neighbouring byte.

The README already flags this as 'not faithful for side-effecting memory-mapped registers'. Four shipped boards drive 68000-class hardware through it (foodf, quantum, marble, roadrunner), so this is a latent bug class: the symptom would be an intermittent, hard-to-localise device misbehaviour.

Fix: carry UDS/LDS strobe width in the bus contract so a byte write is one half-word transaction. Then audit the four boards for registers currently absorbing a phantom read.

Note the interaction with the cycle-accurate M68000 epic — that work will touch the same bus interface, so sequence them deliberately rather than in parallel.

Acceptance: a write-only device register on a 68000 board sees exactly one access for a byte write, and no read.

title: MOS 6522 VIA: implement T1/T2 timers and the IFR/IER interrupt path
description:
core/src/device/via6522.rs:1 describes itself as a 'register-file stub'; :92 notes it 'emulates no interrupt sources (no timers/SR/CxN)'. It stores port and direction registers and nothing else.

It sits on Road Runner's speech board, where a real 6522 times the TMS5220 handshake. Speech works today because the surrounding code does not depend on the timer; the next board that needs one will find nothing there.

Fix: implement T1 (one-shot and free-run), T2 (one-shot and pulse counting), the interrupt flag/enable registers, and CA1/CA2/CB1/CB2 edge handling. Well-specified chip, contained job.

Acceptance: unit tests for both timer modes and the IRQ assert/clear path; Road Runner speech unchanged or improved.

title: Real I8088 disassembler to replace the DB $xx stub
description:
core/src/cpu/i8088/mod.rs:452 — 'Stub disassembler: show raw opcode byte. Full x86 disassembly TBD.' It returns the opcode as a define-byte pseudo-op.

Every other core has a real disassembler with its own test file (m6809, m6800, m6502, z80, m68000, i8035). This one blanks the debugger disassembly pane and the standalone disasm tool for the whole Gottlieb System 80 family — precisely where you would most want to read the code, with Reactor and Mad Planets on the roadmap.

Fix: the ModR/M decoder already exists in core/src/cpu/i8088/addressing.rs; reuse it rather than reimplementing the operand grammar. Intel syntax, matching the register naming already in registers.rs.

Acceptance: an i8088_disasm_test.rs in the shape of the other five; disasm --machine qbert --region main produces readable output.

title: MB88xx and I8035 single-step validators in cargo test
description:
MB88xx is the only CPU with no tests of any kind: no test file in core/tests/, no inline #[test] in core/src/cpu/mb88xx/, and no validator in cpu-validation/tests/. It drives core/src/device/namco51_lle.rs — the low-level Namco 51XX handling input for Galaga and Xevious.

Both MB88xx and I8035 have vector generators (cpu-validation/src/bin/gen_mb88xx_tests.rs, gen_i8035_tests.rs) but no matching tests/ validator, so cross-validation runs through the manual C++ make path outside cargo test entirely. I8035 at least has five unit-test files behind it; MB88xx has nothing.

Fix: add mb88xx_single_step_test.rs and i8035_single_step_test.rs alongside the other six, so cross-validation is a suite gate rather than a remembered ritual. Follow the skip-without-data convention (see the i8088 skip fix in the CI epic).

Acceptance: cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation covers all eight CPUs when data is present, skips cleanly when not.

title: Tests for the six untested devices, Namco WSG first
description:
Device coverage is better than it first appears — 26 of 41 device files carry inline tests, Votrax alone has 60. The untested set is: namco_wsg, namco06, namco53, namco51_lle, output_latch, dac.

Namco WSG is the odd one out and should come first: it is the sound chip for Pac-Man, Ms. Pac-Man, Galaga, Dig Dug and Xevious, it is 261 lines, and it has no test at all.

Directly assertable without a running machine: waveform-ROM decode, frequency accumulator stepping, per-voice volume, and the sound-enable gate.

Acceptance: each of the six has at least the register-contract and reset-behaviour tests the other devices carry.

title: Testable seam for frontend logic, starting with state.toml migration
description:
frontend/tests/ exists and is empty. There is genuinely testable SDL-free logic in the crate: binding resolution (input.rs), host-key conflict detection (host_keys.rs), and state.toml migration of the legacy top-level input_bindings/dip_switches maps into the per-machine [machines.<name>] section (state.rs).

The migration path matters most: it silently rewrites user config, and a bug there loses someone's rebinds.

frontend/src/emulator.rs:1366 shows the inline-test pattern already works for the pure helpers (presentation, fit_aspect).

Acceptance: migration is covered by round-trip tests over legacy and current state.toml shapes, including the both-present and neither-present cases.

title: Vector generators write relative to CWD, so the documented command silently misfires
description:
cpu-validation/src/bin/gen_m6800_tests.rs:425 (and the i8035/m6809/mb88xx siblings) do:

  let out_dir = Path::new("test_data/m6800");

That is relative to the current directory. The validators read the same relative path with CWD = the crate root, because that is where cargo runs integration tests.

So the command the validators themselves print on a missing-data skip —

  cargo run -p phosphor-cpu-validation --bin gen_m6800_tests -- all

writes to <repo>/test_data/m6800 when run from the repo root, while the test looks in <repo>/cpu-validation/test_data/m6800. It only works if you happen to cd into cpu-validation first, which the message does not say.

The failure is silent in the worst way: the generator reports success, the validator then finds no data and skips, and libtest captures the skip message for a passing test — so the suite goes green having validated nothing.

Found while writing the CI validate job, which works around it with working-directory: cpu-validation plus an explicit directory check (.github/workflows/ci.yml). The workaround is correct but the underlying footgun should go.

Fix: resolve the output directory against env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") in all four generators so the documented command works from anywhere, and update the hint text in require_test_data call sites if the command changes.

Acceptance: running the printed command from the repo root produces vectors the validator then finds.

title: Epic: Control handling — closing the input architecture gaps
description:
Close seven gaps in the input path between the typed input model (InputControl/InputEvent, core/src/core/machine.rs:160-394) and the SDL dispatch layer that feeds it. Design: ~/control-handling.md.

The model is sound: machines declare stable logical controls and consume typed InputEvents; the frontend owns physical binding and persists overrides by stable name. The dispatch layer is unfinished, and ~7 machines have each hand-rolled the analog conditioning core never provided.

Verified against code before filing:
- No InputEvent::Absolute producer exists in frontend/ — the only non-test emitter in the repo is tools/script/src/session.rs:406, so the pad-analog receivers in starwars.rs:1579 and irobot.rs:1338 are reachable only from Rhai scripts, never from a gamepad.
- InputEvent::Relative is produced ONLY by frontend/src/emulator.rs:681,685. Neither the harness nor the Rhai session emits it, so five trackball/spinner games (marble, ccastles, missile_command, quantum, tempest) have input paths no headless test can drive.
- InputBinding::scale is hardcoded 1.0 at all three construction sites (input.rs:238,290,319); deadzone is always STICK_DEADZONE_NORM. Neither round-trips through SerializedBinding.
- MouseButtonUp (emulator.rs:696) is gated on mouse_grabbed while KeyUp (:626) is deliberately NOT — the file carries a six-line comment at :619-625 explaining exactly why releases must not be gated. Same bug class, one path guarded, the other not.
- No Event::Window arm exists anywhere in emulator.rs (no focus-loss handling); ControllerDeviceRemoved (:667) only retains, sends no releases.
- MachineEntry (registry.rs:13-20) has exactly three fields; input_controls() uniformly returns &static [InputControl] across all machines, so hoisting the slice into the registry is mechanically sound. 94 sites dispatch via `id.0 as u8`.

Sequencing note (diverges from the design doc): Area 3 does NOT depend on Area 1. The doc claims it does via set_velocity, but that only covers binding trackballs to pad sticks. Area 3s headline win — analog yoke on Star Wars, analog stick on I, Robot — is Family B and touches none of Area 1s RelativeCounter work. Area 1 completes Area 3s trackball half rather than blocking it.

Ordering: headless Relative path first (unblocks five games for frameshot regression, depends on nothing), then Area 2 (four stuck-input bugs), Area 5 (extraction + test double), Area 6 (mechanical contract test), Areas 3+4 (the user-visible analog work), Area 1 (largest cleanup, only medium-risk area), Area 7 last.
close_reason:
All 8 areas shipped. ~40 commits.

.1 headless Relative input path (script + harness + disasm trace --move)
.3 Area 5 — dispatch() extracted from run(), with tests
.2 Area 2 — resync + release_all_inputs, four stuck-input bugs fixed
.5 Area 3 — PadControl::FullAxis, Absolute reaches machines from a gamepad
.4 Area 6 — MachineEntry::controls + registry-wide contract tests
.6 Area 4 — per-game analog sensitivity and deadzone, persisted and tunable
.7 Area 1 — RelativeCounter/AnalogAxis, all 8 analog machines migrated
.8 Area 7 — player-scoped pad routing + rebindable frontend hotkeys

BEYOND THE DESIGN, from a bug reported mid-epic: a gamepad axis resting off-center re-asserted "released" on every motion event, killing left/right in every game while up/down worked. Fixed by latching pad-axis state and dispatching only on change (86e3d9c). A second, related defect was found in the code this epic added: resync emitted one event per binding, so an absent pad's bindings overwrote a held key. Both are regression-tested.

WHERE THE DESIGN WAS WRONG (each recorded on its issue):
- InputBinding::analog, called Area 3's deliverable and Area 4's prerequisite, has no consumer at all — every call site holds the control table already. Added and removed twice before being dropped.
- register_machine! cannot fill MachineEntry::controls automatically; the const name tracks neither type nor CLI name, and an associated const would break the registry's dyn-compatibility.
- Area 6's two per-control assertions contradicted an established convention (~11 machines deliberately leave coin2 unbound; two-player analog cabinets leave P2's axes unbound). Narrowed to per-machine invariants rather than changing the tables.
- Area 1's save-state break is per-machine, not universal: 5 of 8 machines kept their formats intact.
- Area 1's drain policies differ in how they treat held keys, which the design's table did not capture.
- starwars must not use set_absolute, roadrunner must not use reversed() — both off by one against the hardware.
- Area 7's slot None must mean "any slot", not "no slot".

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND anywhere in this epic: no second gamepad and no live egui session were available. The stuck-input paths (alt-tab, F11-while-firing, pad unplug), the sensitivity/deadzone sliders, the hotkey capture UI, and two-pad routing are all unit-tested but unplayed. The analog machines' rendering is proven byte-identical; the *feel* is unchanged by construction but unconfirmed.

~/control-handling.md is now substantially out of date. phosphor-emulator-dry-refactors-0lhx.8 already tracks correcting the DRY doc; this one deserves the same treatment.

title: headless: emit InputEvent::Relative from script/harness (unblocks trackball frameshots)
description:
InputEvent::Relative is produced by exactly two lines in the entire repo — frontend/src/emulator.rs:681 and :685, both inside the SDL MouseMotion arm. Neither phosphor-harness nor the Rhai session (tools/script/src/session.rs) can emit it.

Consequence: marble, ccastles, missile_command, quantum and tempest accept only Relative for their trackball/spinner axes, so their primary input path is unreachable from any headless test, script, or frameshot capture. Five games have zero regression coverage on the control that actually plays them.

Work:
- Add DebugSession::input_relative(control, delta) alongside the existing input_button/input_absolute (session.rs:391-408), exposed to Rhai.
- Add a relative form of ScheduledPress in harness/src/harness.rs:99-140 (currently produces only Button).
- Frameshot smoke test for at least marble and ccastles driving the trackball via script.

Depends on nothing. Filed first because it is small, and because it is the prerequisite for cheap before/after frame verification on Area 1 — which is otherwise the riskiest item in the epic.

Note: this is listed in the design doc only as "a small follow-on to Area 3" in the Sequencing section. It does not depend on Area 3.
close_reason: Shipped in 3 commits on control-handling: DebugSession::input_relative + Rhai binding (4e4fcf2); harness MotionSpec/ScheduledMotion + Harness::schedule_motion (a8964a1); disasm trace --move (94467b1). Relative is now producible from the script session and the CLI trace path, so trackball/spinner games (marble, ccastles, missile_command, quantum, tempest) are drivable headlessly for the first time. Verified end-to-end against marble: two 400-frame traces differing only by --move diverge at frame 247, inside the motion window. Not done: frameshot still has neither --press nor --move (pre-existing gap, filed separately if wanted).

title: Area 2: input resync + release_all_inputs (fixes four stuck-input bugs)
description:
There is no "forget every held input" operation anywhere in the stack. Four confirmed bugs follow from that one missing primitive:

1. MouseButtonUp (emulator.rs:696) is gated on mouse_grabbed. Press mouse-fire on Gridlee, press F11 to ungrab (:568-570) -> the release never dispatches and fire sticks on. The keyboard path already documents this exact hazard at :619-625 and deliberately dispatches KeyUp unconditionally; the mouse path just was not given the same treatment.
2. No focus-loss handling — there is no Event::Window arm anywhere in emulator.rs. Alt-tab with a direction held and the machine sees it held forever.
3. ControllerDeviceRemoved (:667-670) only does controllers.retain(...) and sends no releases — unplug a pad mid-deflection and the direction latches.
4. load_state does not reconcile with physical state. Port bits are inside the snapshot (joust.rs:247 p1_controls and friends), so F7 restores a machine whose input state can contradict what is physically held. reset() (F5, :424) has the mirror problem: the machine clears its ports but a key held across the reset produces no new KeyDown, so the input is lost until the user releases and re-presses.

Cases 1-3 want release-all; case 4 wants the stronger "re-assert true physical state". Build resync and derive release-all from it.

Core: default method on InputConfigurable (core/src/core/machine.rs:386) sending Button{pressed:false} for each declared control — idempotent, and the borrow works because input_controls() returns &static [InputControl]. Analog controls deliberately get no synthetic Absolute{0.0}: a trackball has no center, and a self-centering stick is already driven back by the release of its digital directions.

Frontend: input::resync(bindings, machine, keyboard, controllers, mouse_grabbed) reading live SDL state via is_scancode_pressed / GameController::button / axis. Mouse axes are relative and have no resyncable state — skip them.

Call sites: FocusLost -> release_all_inputs; FocusGained -> resync; F11 ungrab (:568) -> release_all_inputs; ControllerDeviceRemoved (:667) -> release_all then resync; after reset() (:424) -> resync; after successful load_state() (:450) -> resync.

Risk low — release_all_inputs is idempotent by construction. The one subtlety: resync must run AFTER the machine mutation it reconciles, not before.

Fixes 1-3 are a few lines each and do not strictly require the Area 5 extraction; the extraction is what makes them testable, hence the dependency.
close_reason:
Shipped in 2 commits on control-handling: InputConfigurable::release_all_inputs (7d45a44) and the frontend reconciliation (ec739ae). All four bugs addressed: MouseButtonUp no longer gated on mouse_grabbed; Event::Window FocusLost/FocusGained arms added (none existed); ControllerDeviceRemoved now releases then re-syncs; reset (F5) and load_state (F7) re-sync.

input::resync re-asserts each binding's live value rather than only clearing, which is what makes the reset/load cases work rather than merely not-stick.

DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN: resync takes a DeviceState trait instead of raw SDL types (KeyboardState/GameController), and InputConfigurable instead of FrontendMachine. Both narrowings exist so the logic is unit-testable now without an SDL context or a 300-line machine stub — the reason this issue was originally sequenced behind dyvs.3. 6 tests total (2 core, 4 frontend). The dyvs.3 dep was downgraded blocks -> related on that basis; dyvs.3 is still worth doing for the dispatch-arm tests, which this does not cover.

NOT DONE: per-machine release_all_inputs overrides that clear conditioned analog state (accumulated trackball motion). The default handles every digital control, which is what the four bugs needed; the analog overrides become one-liners once Area 1 (dyvs.7) lands the RelativeCounter/AnalogAxis components with their release_all().

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND: the alt-tab and F11-while-firing paths need an interactive session (SDL window, physical pad). Verified by construction, unit tests, workspace build, clippy and fmt clean, and full test suites across core/machines/frontend/harness/script/disasm.

title: Area 5: extract dispatch() out of run() + recording test double
description:
pub fn run spans emulator.rs:56-1032 (file is 1159 lines): SDL event loop, all frontend hotkeys, input dispatch, frame execution, audio draining and egui presentation in one function. The #[cfg(test)] block at :1108 tests only fit_aspect. frontend/src/input.rs has good unit tests for BindingSet construction/serialization/override semantics (:430-622) but NOTHING tests event -> InputEvent dispatch — which is exactly where Areas 2 and 3 and all four stuck-input bugs live.

Move the eight input arms (emulator.rs:608-700) into frontend/src/input.rs behind:

  pub struct DispatchCtx { pub egui_wants_keyboard: bool, pub mouse_grabbed: bool }
  pub fn dispatch(event: &Event, bindings: &BindingSet, machine: &mut dyn FrontendMachine, ctx: DispatchCtx) -> bool

runs match collapses to one delegating arm, placed AFTER the hotkey arms so hotkey precedence is unchanged.

Test double: a recording machine in input.rs #[cfg(test)] implementing MachineCore + capability traits, capturing Vec<InputEvent>. tools/script/src/test_support.rs has an equivalent but it is a private mod; making it pub to cross a crate boundary for one test is worse than ~50 lines of local double.

Tests to write, each pinning a bug or currently-unverified behavior:
- Key release dispatches even when egui_wants_keyboard (pins the reasoning at :619-625, currently only a comment).
- Key press does not dispatch when egui_wants_keyboard.
- MouseButtonUp dispatches regardless of mouse_grabbed — EXPECTED TO FAIL until Area 2 lands. Write it red.
- Pad axis crossing the deadzone produces exactly one Button{pressed:true}.
- Pad axis bound to an analog control produces Absolute, deadzone-rescaled to 0.0 exactly at the edge (Area 3).
- Mouse motion applies scale to the Relative delta (Area 4).
- release_all_inputs emits one release per declared control and nothing else (Area 2).

Pure code motion plus tests. The one hazard is reordering match arms and changing hotkey precedence — move the input arms as a block and keep them last.
close_reason:
Shipped in 60056d8 on control-handling. input::dispatch(event, bindings, machine, DispatchCtx) -> bool holds all eight input arms; run's match ends in one delegating arm kept last, so hotkey precedence is unchanged. emulator.rs drops ~100 lines.

DEVIATION FROM THE DESIGN — no recording machine stub was needed. The issue budgeted ~50 lines for a local double implementing MachineCore + every capability trait. Instead dispatch takes InputConfigurable (the only trait it uses) rather than FrontendMachine, so the 20-line Recorder added for resync in dyvs.2 covers it. Same narrowing dyvs.2 applied for the same reason.

6 tests: key press suppressed under egui focus; key release dispatched anyway; mouse release dispatched regardless of grab (pins the dyvs.2 fix); pad axis pressing only the direction crossing the deadzone; mouse motion applying scale and requiring the grab; unrelated events not consumed.

NOT DONE, as filed: the 'pad axis bound to an analog control produces Absolute' test belongs to Area 3 (dyvs.5) — the analog dispatch path does not exist yet. The 'release_all_inputs emits one release per control' test already landed in core with dyvs.2.

Hotplug and Event::Window arms deliberately stay in run: they mutate frontend state (controller list, needs_resync), not the machine, so they are not dispatch's business.

Gate: workspace build, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, and tests across frontend/core/machines all clean. 35 frontend tests pass.

title: Area 6: MachineEntry::controls + registry-wide input contract test
description:
Nothing verifies the invariants the whole typed input model rests on. InputIds must be unique within a machine (they are the handle_input dispatch key); stable_names must be unique (they are the persistence key — a duplicate silently makes one controls bindings unrecoverable). Only 6 of ~40 machines have a test file at all. The DIP side already has the equivalent guard: assert_dip_banks_valid in machines/src/lib.rs:437-469. Input has no counterpart.

Obstacle: MachineEntry::create (registry.rs:19) needs a RomSet, so a test cannot instantiate machines without ROMs, which CI does not have. Fix by making the control table reachable statically — add `pub controls: &static [InputControl]` to MachineEntry (currently exactly three fields, registry.rs:13-20). VERIFIED: input_controls() returns &static [InputControl] uniformly across every machine, so the hoist is mechanically sound and the compiler finds every registration site.

machines/tests/input_contract_test.rs asserts per machine: non-empty control table; no duplicate InputId; no duplicate stable_name; no empty name/label; every control either InputKind::Action (role supplies defaults) or has its own default_bindings; and control.id.0 < 256.

The id.0 < 256 assertion is worth spelling out: 94 sites in machines/src dispatch via `match id.0 as u8`, so the u16 InputId is silently truncated. No machine currently exceeds 100, so this passes today and pins a latent footgun.

A second test — every machines default bindings survive BindingSet::from_controls -> to_serialized -> apply_overrides unchanged — belongs in frontend/src/input.rs (where BindingSet lives), iterating phosphor_machines::registry::all().

INTERACTION WITH ~/dry-refactors.md 5a (register_machine!) — the control-handling doc claims that macro "would fill controls in automatically". It cannot, and this was verified:
- register_machine!(JoustSystem, "joust", &["joust"]) receives only the type, CLI name and rom_names.
- Every machine stores its table in a separately-named const, and the prefix does not track the type or CLI name: JOUST_CONTROLS but also CONGO_CONTROLS (congo_bongo.rs:1426), DKONG_CONTROLS (donkey_kong.rs:255). Deriving the ident with paste! would be fragile and wrong in at least those two cases.
- An associated const on InputConfigurable is NOT an option: InputConfigurable is a supertrait of FrontendMachine (machine.rs:687-695) which is used as Box<dyn FrontendMachine> in registry.rs:19. An associated const makes a trait non-dyn-compatible, and unlike methods there is no `where Self: Sized` escape hatch for consts. It would break the registry.

So the macro needs a fourth argument naming the const: register_machine!(JoustSystem, "joust", &["joust"], JOUST_CONTROLS). The consts are mostly private but register_machine! expands in the same module, so visibility is fine.

Consequence for sequencing: Areas 6 and dry-refactors 5a still want to land together — one pass over the ~18-31 registration sites instead of two — but the per-site hand-work is NOT eliminated by the macro. Do not defer this issue waiting for a macro that will not remove the work.

The control-handling doc also contradicts itself on this area — Risk says "passes today", Testing says "expected to surface real violations on first run". Run the assertions against the current registry early to find out which; if violations exist, fix the tables, do not relax the assertions.
close_reason:
Shipped in 2 commits on control-handling: MachineEntry::controls + machines contract test (3a486eb), frontend persistence round-trip (f5cc2db).

MachineEntry gained a `controls` field holding the machine's static InputControl slice; 40 registration sites updated mechanically across 35 files. 9 tests in machines/tests/input_contract_test.rs plus 2 in frontend/src/input.rs.

THE DESIGN'S TWO CONTRADICTORY PREDICTIONS, RESOLVED. Its Risk section said "passes today"; its Testing section said "expected to surface real violations". Both were half right. Every mechanical invariant (unique InputIds, unique stable_names, non-empty names/labels, id < 256) passes unchanged. Two proposed per-control assertions failed — but against an established convention, not a defect, so the assertions were narrowed rather than the tables changed:

- "every control has a default binding" failed on ccastles coin2. A survey showed ~11 machines deliberately leave coin2/coin3 unbound (burgertime binds Num6, starwars reuses P2_START, the rest leave it empty): a second cabinet coin slot has no natural key and is rebindable when wanted. Narrowed to "every machine has at least one BOUND coin control", so a machine that cannot be coined at all still fails.
- "analog controls bind something analog" failed on foodf p2_stick_x. Same shape: there is one mouse, so two-player analog cabinets (foodf P2 stick, marble P2 trackball) leave the second player's axes unbound by design. Narrowed to per-machine: a machine whose analog controls are ALL unreachable fails.

This is not relaxing assertions to reach green. The per-control forms encoded an assumption the codebase consistently contradicts across many machines. The reasoning is recorded in the commit message.

VERIFIED THE TESTS HAVE TEETH: duplicated a stable_name in joust, confirmed the uniqueness test fails naming the machine, then restored.

ADDED BEYOND THE DESIGN: a registry-non-empty guard in both suites. Every test iterates registry::all(), so an empty registry would make all of them pass while checking nothing.

NOT DONE: the design suggests sequencing with the register_machine! macro in the DRY doc, section 5a, so the field is filled in by the macro. Established earlier that the macro cannot derive the const name (it tracks neither the type nor the CLI name — CONGO_CONTROLS, DKONG_CONTROLS) and that an associated const on InputConfigurable would break dyn-compatibility for the registry. If 5a lands it takes a fourth argument; the per-site work here is not wasted. See phosphor-emulator-dry-refactors-0lhx.2.

Gate: workspace build, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, and tests across core/machines/frontend/harness/script/disasm all clean.

title: Area 3: close the Absolute path (PadControl::FullAxis + analog dispatch)
description:
emulator.rs:648-657 handles ControllerAxisMotion by looking up pad_axis_targets(axis) and emitting a Button — a threshold comparison against the deadzone. There is no analog lookup and no Absolute emission anywhere in the frontend. VERIFIED: the only non-test InputEvent::Absolute emitter in the repo is tools/script/src/session.rs:406.

Consequences: starwars.rs:1579 ("Pad stick sets an absolute yoke position") and irobot.rs:1338 (set_stick_abs) are reachable only from Rhai scripts and their own unit tests — never from a gamepad. Ten machines declaring InputKind::AnalogAxis are mouse-or-keyboard only; eight explicitly discard Absolute with `InputEvent::Absolute { .. } => {}`. And DefaultBinding::Pad(PadControl::Axis(axis, sign)) carries a sign, which is meaningful for "deflection stands in for a D-pad direction" but meaningless for a full analog axis — there is no way to express "bind the whole LeftX axis to this analog control".

Core: add PadControl::FullAxis(PadAxis) (machine.rs:320-323). Purely additive; existing Axis(..) bindings and their digital behavior are untouched. Do NOT remove PadControl::Axis — twin-stick fire (input_defaults.rs:54-69) legitimately wants signed-deflection-as-digital.

Frontend: PhysicalInput gains PadFullAxis(Axis) with token padfullaxis:<axis> (input.rs:59-149 round-trip, covered by the existing token test at :440). InputBinding gains `pub analog: bool`, set from matches!(control.kind, InputKind::AnalogAxis{..}) at construction — from_controls (:215), apply_overrides (:267) and rebind (:308) all already receive or can receive &[InputControl]. This field is also the prerequisite for Area 4.

New lookup pad_analog_targets(axis) -> impl Iterator<Item = (InputId, f32, f32)>. Dispatch replaces the single arm at :648-657 with both loops (an axis may drive digital and analog targets), the analog one deadzone-rescaled so the value ramps from 0 at the deadzone edge rather than jumping to it.

Machines: add DefaultBinding::Pad(PadControl::FullAxis(..)) to the analog controls that want it — starwars.rs:171-190, irobot.rs:391-410.

IMPORTANT — this does NOT depend on Area 1, contrary to the design docs sequencing. The Family B win (yoke on Star Wars, stick on I, Robot) touches none of Area 1s RelativeCounter work. Only the trackball half — giving RelativeCounter a set_velocity so a deflected stick rolls the ball continuously — needs Area 1, and that can land with Area 1 or after it. Ship the Family B half first.
close_reason:
Shipped in 2 commits on control-handling: the plumbing (093a30a) and machine defaults (48b7c32).

- core: PadControl::FullAxis(PadAxis), additive; PadControl::Axis kept for twin-stick fire.
- frontend: PhysicalInput::PadFullAxis + token padfullaxis:<axis>, BindingSet::pad_analog_targets, analog loop in dispatch running alongside the digital one, deadzone-rescaled via a shared analog_value() helper. resync re-asserts full axes as Absolute so a stick held across a reset/load stays deflected. Also folded the deadzone derivation triplicated across from_controls/apply_overrides/rebind into one make_binding().
- 5 new frontend tests (39 total in the crate).

DEVIATION 1 — machines bind the RIGHT stick, not the left as the design implied. input_defaults::P1_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN already bind LeftX/LeftY as signed digital directions, and both starwars (set_stick) and irobot (update_stick) assign their axis ABSOLUTELY from those. Binding FullAxis(LeftX) as well would put one physical stick on both paths, with the digital one snapping to full deflection or center and overriding the analog value. Right stick is purely additive and conflicts with nothing. Freeing the left stick would mean per-machine overrides of the four direction controls' defaults — a default-binding change that deserves its own commit, and which fits naturally with Area 7a (dyvs.8) where default bindings are already being revisited.

DEVIATION 2 — InputBinding::analog was NOT added. The design calls it the prerequisite for Area 4, but nothing in Area 3 reads it: pad_analog_targets filters on PhysicalInput::PadFullAxis, which already encodes the intent. Adding it here meant a dead field behind an #[allow(dead_code)]. dyvs.6 should add it together with its consumers (the sensitivity slider and capture_physical's analog_target argument). The control_is_analog helper it needs is a 4-line lookup.

NOT DONE, as filed: the trackball velocity path (RelativeCounter::set_velocity, and FullAxis defaults for the trackball machines) belongs with Area 1 (dyvs.7), which owns the component.

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND: no physical gamepad in this environment, so the starwars/irobot analog feel is unverified. The event path is unit-tested end to end (control table -> BindingSet -> pad_analog_targets -> Absolute).

Gate: workspace build, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, tests across core/machines/frontend all clean.

title: Area 4: persist scale + deadzone, expose per-game sensitivity UI
description:
InputBinding::scale (input.rs:167) is threaded correctly through mouse_axis_targets (:207-212) into InputEvent::Relative, but is VERIFIED hardcoded 1.0 at all three construction sites (:238, :290, :319). deadzone is always the single global STICK_DEADZONE_NORM (:21). SerializedBinding (:155-159) carries only {control, input}, so neither round-trips.

Result: no per-game analog sensitivity across seven trackball/spinner games whose hardware counters differ by a factor of sixteen in width (4-bit missile_command/quantum/tempest vs 8-bit ccastles/marble). Machines compensate internally by hand-tuning drain cadences — ccastles every 200 cycles, missile_command every 1000 (:396-398) — which is the right place for the hardware rate but leaves the players pointing-device sensitivity untunable.

Persistence: SerializedBinding gains Option<f32> scale and deadzone with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")], so existing state.toml files load unchanged and unchanged bindings still write two keys — matching the diff-only philosophy MachineSettings::is_empty (state.rs:55-67) already enforces. to_serialized emits Some(..) only when the value differs from default; apply_overrides fills via unwrap_or. bindings_eq (:327-337) sorts by (control, input) — extend the key to include both new fields, or a sensitivity-only change is not detected as differing from defaults and never gets saved.

UI: settings_ui.rs:79-85 currently renders analog controls as a dead row ("not rebindable here"). Replace with a logarithmic sensitivity Slider over 0.1..=5.0 labelled with the bound physical input from physical_for (:298), plus a deadzone slider for PadFullAxis bindings. Needs BindingSet::set_scale/set_deadzone.

Once Area 3 lands, analog controls are genuinely rebindable, which capture_physical (emulator.rs:42-53) cannot support — it only matches KeyDown/ControllerButtonDown/MouseButtonDown, so PadAxis, PadFullAxis and MouseAxis can be loaded from state.toml but never produced by the UI. Extend it with an axis-deflection arm (threshold ~24000, well above the digital deadzone so a resting stick never captures) and a mouse-motion arm. The mouse-motion arm MUST be gated on mouse_grabbed, or the cursor travelling toward the Rebind button captures itself.

Constraint: scale defaults stay 1.0 for every machine. Do not bake per-machine scale defaults into the tables to normalize sensitivity — the machines already compensate at the hardware drain rate and a second correction factor makes both untraceable. This is a user preference knob.

Needs Area 3s `analog` flag on InputBinding. Worth a state.toml round-trip test alongside the existing one at state.rs:234-247, plus a manual check that an old state.toml without the new keys still loads.
close_reason:
Shipped in 21c6f2f on control-handling.

Persistence: SerializedBinding gained Option<f32> scale/deadzone with serde(default) + skip_serializing_if, so existing state.toml files load unchanged and untouched bindings still write a two-key table. to_serialized emits a value only when it differs from the default. bindings_eq folds the tuning into its sort key — without that a sensitivity-only change compares equal to defaults and is never written at all.

UI: analog controls trade their dead "not rebindable here" row for a logarithmic sensitivity slider; any control bound to a pad axis also gets a deadzone slider. Edits are recorded as PendingTuning and applied by the emulator loop after the frame, following the existing PendingDipChange pattern rather than handing the panel a mutable BindingSet. capture_physical learned axis and mouse-motion capture, so analog controls are finally rebindable.

DEVIATION 1 — the deadzone slider reaches DIGITAL direction bindings, not just PadFullAxis as the design specified. This was driven by a field report during this epic: a gamepad whose stick rests off-center held left/right permanently in every game, because the resting deflection exceeded STICK_DEADZONE_NORM. Those are PadAxis bindings on digital directions, so a PadFullAxis-only knob would not have reached the actual failure. set_deadzone is scoped to axis bindings so a key never diverges from its default and gets needlessly persisted.

DEVIATION 2 — InputBinding::analog was NOT added, again. The design calls it Area 4's prerequisite (and Area 3 deferred it here for that reason), but it has no consumer: the settings panel and the capture site both already hold the control table and read control.kind directly. It was added during this work, flagged dead by clippy, and removed. The design's premise — "BindingSet has no access to control metadata later" — does not hold for any actual call site. Worth correcting in ~/control-handling.md.

PROCESS NOTE: this initially landed as two commits, the first of which left dead-code warnings because the API had no consumer until the UI arrived. That violates the project standard that clippy passes with no warnings, so the two were squashed into one before finishing. Unpushed history only.

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND: the sliders have not been exercised in a live egui session — no gamepad here and the panel needs a window. The persistence and tuning logic are unit-tested; the rendering is not.

Gate: workspace clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, and tests across core/machines/frontend all clean. 48 frontend tests.

title: Area 1: RelativeCounter + AnalogAxis conditioning components, migrate 7 machines
description:
Two distinct analog-conditioning state machines are reimplemented across seven machines, each with its own fields, its own Saveable entries and its own reset handling.

Family A — relative motion into a wrapping N-bit counter (trackballs, spinners): ccastles (state :445-450, keys :884-895, drain :896-908), missile_command (:316-319, :399-413, :414-427), marble (:456, :545-556, :558-564), quantum (:324-325, drain :467-475), tempest (:248-253, :328-334, :336-350). They differ in four parameters, all real hardware facts worth keeping: counter width (8-bit wrapping for ccastles/marble vs 4-bit masked & 0x0F for the rest); drain cadence/policy (Unit +-1 per call from a cycle divider; ClampCarry +-max_step remainder retained, marble; ClampDrop +-max_step remainder discarded so the player stops when the mouse does, tempest/quantum both +-7, documented at tempest.rs:337-345 as anti-aliasing for the 4-bit read); key step; and axis orientation (marble negates X at apply time :561, ccastles/missile_command negate Y at input time, quantum does a full axis crossover AND an inversion :661-670).

Family B — clamped absolute position, spring-centered (flight sticks, yokes): irobot (:722-739, :764-768, :752-761, ADC0809), starwars (:1020-1034, :1037-1040, :1043-1047, pot inputs), roadrunner (:557-568, :759, absolute ignored at :771, ADC0809). The spring-center closure is byte-identical between roadrunner.rs:557-567 and starwars.rs:1021-1029 and differs only in u8 vs i32 typing in irobot.rs:724-737. The one genuine difference is irobots asymmetric span (separate scale either side of center, :753-757) because its X and Y channels have different ranges.

New module core/src/core/input.rs exporting DrainPolicy, RelativeCounter, AxisRange, AnalogAxis. These are conditioners, not chips — they derive Saveable but NOT Device (Device requires a name() chip designation and Debuggable, a category error here). Precedent for a small shared helper carrying its own derived Saveable: core/src/device/output_latch.rs. All config fields (mask, key_step, invert, policy, range) take #[save_skip] — macros/src/lib.rs:666-684 supports it. Machines keep their push_stick()/update_adc_inputs() call after mutating: when the ADC sees a new value is machine-specific timing the component must not own.

Constraints:
- ZERO behavior change is the bar. Reproduce every quirk: marble carries its remainder while tempest/quantum drop theirs; quantums axis crossover stays in handle_input (bus wiring, not conditioning); marble negates at apply while ccastles negates at input — normalize both onto RelativeCounter::invert only after confirming the sign works out.
- Preserve key-vs-analog precedence exactly. Today, releasing a direction key on a Family B machine snaps the axis to center even if the mouse had moved it (update_stick assigns absolutely). That is arguably wrong but it is current behavior — reproduce it and file the improvement separately. Changing it inside a no-behavior-change refactor would hide a real gameplay change.
- Save states break for all seven machines. These are user-local quick-saves with no compatibility guarantee: bump each machines #[save_version] and update the per-machine round-trip tests (ccastles.rs:1405-1428, missile_command.rs:1211-1243) rather than writing migration code. Call it out in the commit message.

Also add RelativeCounter::set_velocity(f32) here — treating a stick deflection as velocity (update() adds value * key_step while held off-center) is the natural reading for a trackball and is the same mechanism the direction keys already use, with a continuous magnitude instead of a boolean. That completes Area 3s trackball half.

Only medium-risk area in the epic, entirely concentrated in migration transcription. Gate on cargo test -p phosphor-machines plus before/after frameshot diffs for marble, ccastles, missile_command, tempest and quantum — the frames must be byte-identical. Capture the BEFORE frames first; dyvs.1 (headless Relative path) is what makes driving these trackballs from a script possible at all.
close_reason:
Shipped in 10 commits on control-handling. All 8 analog machines migrated onto the shared components.

ee1f6dd components (DrainPolicy, RelativeCounter, AxisRange, AnalogAxis + 12 unit tests, incl. set_velocity deferred here from Area 3)
82878f9 quantum   | 4389122 tempest  | 2a60c77 missile
0f463a1 ccastles  | 879a3b1 marble   | 4591294 roadrunner
b194404 starwars  | 57da69f irobot   | 41974f0 release_all_inputs overrides

VERIFICATION: byte-identical frames after EVERY migration, not just at the end. A scripted probe per machine drives relative motion both directions, absolute deflection, and held direction keys, then screenshots; hashes compared against a pre-refactor baseline. The probe was confirmed deterministic across repeated runs before being trusted. Note the design asked for frameshot diffs, but frameshot cannot drive input — this was only possible because dyvs.1 added the headless Relative path first.

DESIGN CORRECTIONS FOUND DURING THE WORK:

1. The drain policies differ in how they treat held keys, which the design's table does not capture. Unit (ccastles, missile) applies the key step DIRECTLY to the counter and drains pending separately, so a key and buffered motion can both land in one tick. ClampCarry/ClampDrop fold keys into the accumulator first. Collapsing these into one path would silently change ccastles.

2. The save-state break is per-machine, not universal. The design budgeted a version bump for all of them. Actual: quantum, marble, roadrunner, starwars and irobot hand-write Saveable and only ever persisted the counter/position, so routing through counter()/set_counter() and position()/set_position() kept their formats intact — no bump needed. Only tempest (derived Saveable, bumped to save_version 2), ccastles and missile (hand-written but persisted the accumulators and key flags) actually break.

3. starwars must NOT use AnalogAxis::set_absolute. It scales both directions by its upper half-span (MAX - CENTER = 0x7F) even though center 0x80 is not the midpoint of 0x00..=0xFF; the component scales each side by its own span, which would move full-left deflection from 0x01 to 0x00. It computes its own value and assigns via the new set_position. irobot, the machine that motivated the asymmetric AxisRange in the first place, does use set_absolute directly.

4. roadrunner must NOT use AnalogAxis::reversed(). The hardware complements the byte (0xFF - position); reversed() mirrors about min + max, which is 0x100 there — off by one.

5. AnalogAxis rounds rather than truncates in set_absolute/move_relative, matching irobot's existing .round(). Safe for roadrunner and starwars, which convert deltas to integers before calling in — confirmed by the frame check.

ALSO DONE: the per-machine release_all_inputs overrides that dyvs.2 deferred here. Added core::machine::release_all_controls as a free function so an overriding machine gets the digital half without restating the loop.

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND: the release_all path is not exercised by the probe (which never loses focus), and analog feel has not been checked in a live session.

PROCESS NOTE: the quantum commit initially landed with a broken test build (its own tests still compared the old u8 fields), caught and amended. Scripted splices twice cut the wrong brace boundary in marble and ccastles; both caught by the compiler immediately.

Gate: workspace build, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, and tests across core/machines/frontend/harness/script/disasm all clean.

title: Area 7: multi-pad player routing + rebindable frontend hotkeys
description:
Two independent sub-features, both deliberately sequenced last. Larger and lower-value than Areas 1-6.

7a — player-scoped controller routing (medium-high risk). Event::ControllerButtonDown { button, .. } (emulator.rs:635) discards `which`; the instance id is used only for hotplug bookkeeping (:660-670). Two plugged-in pads both drive player 1. input_defaults.rs:41-51 documents the current workaround — P2 is keyboard-only (WASD, no pad) — and ActionRole::default_bindings hardcodes it at machine.rs:227 ((Primary, Some(2)) => &[Key(KeyId::RShift)]).

Design: the frontend maintains pad_slot: Vec<InstanceId> assigning connected controllers to slots 1..N in connection order, stable across hotplug. Dispatch resolves which -> slot and matches a binding only when the bindings player_slot is None (any pad) or equals that slot. InputBinding gains player_slot: Option<u8>, defaulted from the target InputControl::player — which the tables already declare correctly everywhere. ActionRole::default_bindings then stops special-casing player 2: P2 Primary becomes RShift PLUS gamepad A on slot 2.

That is a default-binding change, so it needs its own commit and a note that saved P2 bindings are unaffected (apply_overrides only replaces controls it names). It also interacts with Area 2 — resync must become slot-aware. Hence the dependency on dyvs.2.

7b — rebindable frontend hotkeys (low risk, high surface). Escape, F1, F5-F12, Num0/7/8/9, Tab, backtick, Ctrl+backtick and P are hardcoded Scancode arms at :342-606, all matched BEFORE the game-input arm, so they are unconditionally stolen from the machine. Tab and P are both in KeyId, so a machine binding either is silently shadowed. Escape quits with no confirmation.

Design: a HostAction enum (Quit, Reset, QuickSave, QuickLoad, TogglePause, ToggleDebug, Screenshot, ...) with a HostBindings map persisted in State (global, not per-machine), rendered in the settings panel alongside game controls. Dispatch consults HostBindings first, then falls through to BindingSet. A conflict check at machine load warns when a host binding shadows a machine controls default.

The payoff is real but narrow — it mostly matters for P and Tab, and only for machines that want those keys. The cost is a second binding system with its own persistence and UI. 7a and 7b are independently shippable; split into separate issues if either is picked up on its own.
close_reason:
Shipped in 3 commits on main: d26c56b (7a slot routing), a33df7f (7a default bindings), 5efb699 (7b hotkeys).

7a — PLAYER-SCOPED PAD ROUTING. InputBinding gains player_slot, defaulted from the target control's declared player, and set only on pad bindings (a keyboard binding for player 2 is still just a key; scoping it would make it unreachable). Slots follow connection order, 1-based to match InputControl::player. dispatch resolves instance id -> slot in the caller and passes it via DispatchCtx; resync became slot-aware too, so re-asserting a player 2 binding reads player 2's pad rather than "any pad pushing hardest".

DESIGN CORRECTION: the first cut had slot None mean "no slot", which excluded every slot-scoped binding from the settings UI and all non-pad lookups. None must mean "any slot". Controls with no owning player (coin, service) stay unscoped and work from whichever pad is nearest.

The default-binding change is a separate commit as the design required: ActionRole::Primary for player 2 becomes RShift PLUS gamepad A (same button as player 1, routed to slot 2), and P2_LEFT/RIGHT/UP/DOWN gain the D-pad and left stick. Player 2 keeps RShift rather than LShift so two players can still share a keyboard — that half was never about the pad. Saved bindings are unaffected: apply_overrides only replaces controls a state.toml names.

7b — REBINDABLE HOTKEYS. host_keys.rs holds a HostAction enum with a factory key table and a HostBindings storing only overrides, persisted globally in state.toml (these are emulator properties, not cabinet ones). The hotkey match arms keep their bodies and ordering; only their patterns changed, from literal Scancodes to a HostBindings lookup, so existing guards compose with it. Rebinding an action frees its old key, which is what makes a machine's P or Tab reachable. Rebinding onto a taken key displaces the other action rather than firing both. Settings panel gained a hotkey section with click-to-capture; capture runs before the hotkey arms or binding F5 would reset instead.

SCOPE DECISIONS:
- Ctrl+Grave (console) stays a fixed combo. Modifiers are not modelled, and one key with two actions is exactly what rebind() prevents.
- Debugger step keys (Num0/7/8/9) are in the table and rebindable, but excluded from conflict warnings: they only claim the key while the debugger is open, so a machine binding Num7 still gets it the rest of the time.
- The conflict check warns rather than auto-yielding. Silently handing F5 to a machine that binds it would be a worse surprise than a log line.

NOT VERIFIED BY HAND: no second gamepad here, so two-pad routing is unit-tested but not played. The hotkey UI and capture flow need a live egui session. Both are the parts most likely to need adjustment.

Gate: workspace build, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check, tests across core/machines/frontend/harness/script/disasm all clean. 56 frontend tests. The 8 analog machines' frames re-verified byte-identical against the Area 1 baseline — this touches no machine code, so that confirms nothing drifted.
