title: Epic: Cycle-accurate I8088
description:
The I8088 is instruction-level, not cycle-accurate (core/src/cpu/i8088/README.md, 'Timing: Instruction-level (not cycle-accurate)'), while five of the seven cores are true per-cycle state machines. Same stated-goal gap as the M68000 epic.

Smaller blast radius: Q*bert is the only shipped board on it today, with Reactor and Mad Planets on the roadmap. Its existing decode/execute split (decode.rs, execute.rs, addressing.rs) and BIU-oriented structure are closer to per-cycle than the M68000's atomic model, so this should be the lighter of the two.

Sequenced after the M68000 epic so the harder core sets the pattern — revisit if the M68000 design turns out to be board-specific enough not to transfer.

First child is the design doc. Blocked by the benchmark harness.

title: Design doc: cycle-accurate I8088
description:
Write docs/designs/cycle-accurate-i8088.md before any code. It must resolve:

- BIU prefetch queue: the 8088 has a four-byte queue whose refill timing is the main source of real cycle counts and is observable through bus ordering. Decide whether to model it.
- Bus cycle model: the 8088 bus cycle is four T-states plus wait states; decide what one tick() means.
- Validation: SingleStepTests/8088 supplies cycle-by-cycle bus activity, unlike the 680x0 suite. Confirm the vectors carry what is needed and make them the per-cycle oracle — this may make the I8088 the easier core to prove, which is an argument for doing it first after all.
- Reuse: how much of the M68000 design transfers, and whether a shared per-cycle scaffolding is worth extracting.
- Migration order by instruction class, keeping the 2,577,000-vector gate green throughout.

Acceptance: as for the M68000 doc.

title: Epic: Cycle-accurate M68000
description:
The M68000 decodes and applies an instruction's full effect on cycle 0, then burns the remaining documented cycles as bus-idle waits (core/src/cpu/m68000/README.md, 'Execution model: atomic, not per-cycle'). No per-cycle bus traces, no prefetch queue. Every 8-bit core in the workspace is a true per-cycle state machine where one tick() is one bus transaction.

Design priority #1 for this project is cycle-accurate hardware matching, so this is a stated-goal gap rather than a preference. It caps what the whole 68000 branch can be: foodf, quantum, marble and roadrunner run on approximate timing today, and any future board needing DMA contention, a mid-instruction bus grant, or video timing derived from bus phase hits this wall.

Larger blast radius than the I8088 (four boards vs one) and the harder of the two, so doing this first de-risks the other.

First child is the design doc — the shape depends on decisions not yet made (prefetch queue modelling, how the existing state-only SingleStepTests gate coexists with per-cycle bus traces, and how this interacts with the concrete-bus-dispatch epic, which changes the same inner loop).

Blocked by the benchmark harness: converting an atomic core to per-cycle will cost throughput and we should know how much.

title: Design doc: cycle-accurate M68000
description:
Write docs/designs/cycle-accurate-m68000.md before any code. It must resolve:

- Bus cycle model: the 68000 bus cycle is four clock states (S0-S7 in half-clocks); decide whether tick() is one clock or one bus cycle, and how that squares with Bus<Address=u32, Data=u16> being one word transaction today.
- Prefetch: the two-word prefetch queue is the main observable difference and drives the documented cycle counts. Decide whether to model it, since without it 'cycle-accurate' is only half true.
- Validation: SingleStepTests/680x0 is state-only and already passes 1,000,058 vectors. Per-cycle work needs a bus-trace oracle it does not provide — decide what replaces or supplements it, and whether the existing gate is preserved unchanged as a regression net.
- Interaction with the byte-strobe fix (contained-fidelity epic) which touches the same bus interface.
- Interaction with the concrete-bus-dispatch epic, which changes the same inner loop.
- 68010 differences, since Atari System 1 uses the 68010 variant.
- Migration order by instruction class, and how to keep the tree green throughout.

Reference the existing docs/designs/m68000-emulator.md rather than restating it.

Acceptance: the doc answers each of the above concretely enough that the follow-on issues can be written from it.

title: Show a running frame counter in the F10 debug overlay
description:
Keep a monotonic count of emulated frames and surface it on the F10 debug overlay, alongside the existing FPS and per-machine overlay_stats() lines. Useful for debugging: pinpointing/reproducing a glitch at a specific frame, correlating with logs, and comparing against a reference emulator's frame number.

Mechanism (frontend): the F10 overlay is gated by show_fps in frontend/src/emulator.rs (~lines 597-658). It draws fps_text plus machine.overlay_stats() through crate::overlay::draw_overlay(...) for raster machines and an egui window (present_vectors_with_overlay) for vector machines.

Proposed implementation (machine-agnostic, frontend-side):
- Add a frame counter (u64) to the main loop, incremented once per run_frame() call (per emulated frame, not per rendered frame).
- Render it on the overlay as a line like 'Frame: N' in both the raster path (crate::overlay::draw_overlay) and the vector egui path. Simplest: add it to fps_text, or add a dedicated line.
- Keep it a frontend/session counter independent of machine save state (so it works for every machine without touching MachineCore). Decide reset semantics: zero it on machine.reset(); leave it running across quick save/load (F6/F7), or restore alongside state if that's more useful for debugging (document the choice).

Acceptance: with F10 on, a frame-count line appears and increments each frame for both raster and vector machines; off when the overlay is hidden.

Consider whether it belongs next to the FPS readout permanently vs only in the overlay, and whether a per-machine current-scanline/beam readout would be a useful adjacent addition (out of scope here).
close_reason: Frame counter implemented and shown on the F10 overlay (fps line: 'fps: X  frame: N'). Unified into DebugState.frame_count so it also drives the new Step Frame control and the frame breakpoint. Increments per completed frame (debugger open or not), zeroes on F5 reset.

Design doc docs/designs/debug-observability.md fully implemented for the 16-bit surface; u16->u32 widening remains with the addr32 epic (hqy) as designed.

title: debug-obs: memory peek semantics (DebugRead) + BusDebug::peek + viewer
description: Add BusDebug::peek returning the canonical DebugRead (backed/io/unmapped); teach AddressSpace16/32 to return it; update memory viewer to stop showing FF for missing bytes.

AddressSpace32 doesn't exist yet (hqy epic) — its peek lands there. 3 commits, tests + clippy clean.

description: Expose per-device reset + register-write in the UI via existing reset_device/write_device_register. Defer semantic DebugAction list until tracing shows repeated needs.
close_reason: Device debug controls exposed in UI: per-device Reset button + hex offset/value register write, queued as DeviceAction and applied via existing BusDebug reset_device/write_device_register with immediate panel refresh. DevicePanel now carries its devices()-order index for correct dispatch past CPU filtering. Added previously-missing tests pinning the derived dispatch (indexing, write reaching device, reset isolation, CPU/out-of-range no-ops). Semantic DebugAction list deferred per design. 2 commits, tests + clippy clean.

title: debug-obs: broaden instrumentation (Namco Pac, TKG-04, Atari vector, Galaga/DigDug)
description: Instrument more boards by priority; give manual-BusDebug machines (Galaga/DigDug) reusable Watchpoints support they lack today.
close_reason: All four board families instrumented: Namco Pac (I/O latch/WSG/sprite/watchdog events + VBLANK IRQ), TKG-04 (sound latch/IRQ, NMI mask, i8257 sprite DMA with byte counts), Atari DVG+AVG (vector generator start/reset, watchdog, periodic NMI/IRQ), and Galaga/Dig Dug — which also gained the Watchpoints support they lacked: board-level Watchpoints set with per-CPU PC latching across 3 Z80s, BusDebug watchpoint overrides, and 06XX/51XX/53XX custom-chip transaction events. 9 wrappers now delegate DebugTrace. 4 commits, 20 new tests, clippy clean.

title: Debug panel unsupported on 24-bit-bus (MC68000) machines
description:
The egui debug panel (F1 / --debug) is gated on MachineDebug::debug_bus() returning Some, and the debugger's memory inspector is 16-bit-addressed. The MC68000 machines (Food Fight, Quantum) run on a 24-bit AddressSpace32 bus and return None for debug_bus, so --debug silently does nothing for them (the frontend computes has_debug = machine.debug_bus().is_some() in frontend/src/emulator.rs and disables the panel).

Cycle/instruction stepping still works internally via MachineDebug::debug_tick; only the interactive panel (register view + memory inspector) is unavailable.

To support it, the debugger's BusDebug trait and the egui memory inspector / disassembly view in frontend/src/debug_ui.rs need to handle 32-bit addresses (currently u16-addressed). The #[derive(BusDebug)] macro and AddressSpace32 wiring would also need a 32-bit debug path.

Affects: foodf.rs, quantum.rs (both note this limitation in their MachineDebug impls).
close_reason: Debug panel now works on 24-bit-bus MC68000 machines. AddressSpace32 already had the full debug surface (debug_read/peek/poke/watchpoints, all u32) and the frontend memory viewer + disassembly were already u32-aware; the gap was that foodf/quantum exposed no BusDebug. Extended #[derive(BusDebug)] to infer address width from the map field type (AddressSpace16 vs AddressSpace32 — 32-bit routes addresses untruncated) and to expand #[debug_device] on [T; N] arrays into per-element entries; added AddressSpace32::debug_write parity wrapper. Wired foodf + quantum via derive + impl_standalone_debug!. memory_map() stays 16-bit-only (its return type is &AddressSpace16 and it's unused by the frontend, which reads via peek).

title: Discrete sound device framework (v1: Asteroids, Lunar Lander, Donkey Kong)
description:
Reusable framework for discrete / board-level analog sound paths, per docs/designs/discrete-sound-framework.md.

Replaces ad-hoc per-board discrete sound (currently: DkongDiscrete synthesizes finished 44.1kHz PCM and is mixed AFTER resampling, bypassing the board analog path; Asteroids and Lunar Lander discrete writes are stubbed under no_audio) with a typed Rust circuit graph: contiguous Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges for feedback, per-component clock domains, AudioResampler output, Saveable/Debuggable integration.

v1 scope = framework + three migrations. Order (Asteroids first to de-risk the framework on simpler latch/data-driven Atari boards before DK's harder shared-analog mixer):
  1. Framework skeleton + evaluation model
  2. Mixer and filter primitives
  3. Asteroids migration (first real consumer)
  4. Lunar Lander migration
  5. Donkey Kong migration

Follow-ons (DK Jr., Mario Bros., Asteroids Deluxe, Namco 54XX) are out of v1 scope and tracked separately.
close_reason: v1 complete. Built a reusable discrete-sound framework (core/src/device/discrete/: typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted eval with one-step back-edges, per-component clock domains, mixer/filter primitives) and migrated all three v1 boards onto it, each verified against MAME 0.287 with a capture-and-compare rig (tools/sound-reference): Asteroids (l7o.3), Lunar Lander (l7o.4), Donkey Kong (l7o.5). The rig + case study (docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md) caught multiple bugs ears missed (write_d7 latch, XNOR DC-lock, level/balance/headroom). Follow-ups tracked separately: hm4 (MAME output post-processing / thrust rumble); DK fidelity + DK Jr. reuse noted in l7o.5.

title: Discrete sound: framework skeleton + evaluation model
description:
Phase 1. Add core/src/device/discrete/.

- DiscreteCircuitBuilder + typed handles (LogicInputId/DataInputId/PulseInputId/ExternalSourceId/NodeId).
- DiscreteCircuit runtime: contiguous Vec<Node> enum over the v1 primitive set + a single Node::Custom(Box<dyn CustomComponent>) escape-hatch variant. Static dispatch for common primitives; box fat per-variant state.
- Evaluation model: topological sort at build(); per-node output-slot value array (Vec<f64>); cycle detection (DFS) cutting back-edges read with one-step delay; same held-slot mechanism provides cross-clock-domain sample-and-hold.
- DiscreteScheduler with per-component clock domains (BoardCycle / FixedFrequency / OutputSample / EventOnly); dt-based analog state.
- Basic input/source/math primitives (logic/data/pulse inputs, edge detector, fixed/variable square, LFSR noise, gain/add/multiply/clamp).
- AudioResampler integration to mono i16.
- Saveable: include node output slots (held + back-edge state); versioned.
- Unit tests for deterministic primitives (LFSR, square phase/freq, save/load round-trip).

No board migration in this phase.
close_reason: Implemented in core/src/device/discrete/ (mod.rs, node.rs, tests.rs): typed-handle builder -> DiscreteCircuit, Vec<Node> enum + Node::Custom escape hatch, topo-sorted evaluation with one-step-delay back-edges, per-component clock domains, input/source/math primitives + LFSR noise, AudioResampler<i16> output, versioned Saveable with node output slots. 14 unit tests pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: Discrete sound: mixer and filter primitives
description:
Phase 2. Analog approximation primitives on top of the skeleton.

- RC charge/discharge (envelope), RC low-pass, RC high-pass / coupling cap.
- First-order and second-order filters (band-pass, Sallen-Key-style approximation).
- Resistor mixer (with optional pull-up/down/load), diode mixer (configurable forward drop/threshold), DAC / resistor ladder.
- External source input node (accept samples from existing chip/DAC devices).
- Per-primitive unit tests: RC approaches target within tolerance, filter step-response sanity, mixer scaling, diode threshold, DAC monotonicity/endpoints, external-source sample handling, save/load.
close_reason: Implemented analog primitives in core/src/device/discrete/: RC low-pass, RC high-pass/coupling, asymmetric RC envelope (charge/discharge), Chamberlin state-variable 2nd-order filter (low/band/high-pass), passive resistor mixer (weighted-average + optional load), diode-OR mixer (max minus forward drop), and R-2R/weighted DAC ladder. External-source node already present from skeleton; added builder methods, eval/reset/save-load, and FilterMode. 10 new unit tests (24 total in module); clippy + fmt clean.

title: Asteroids: migrate discrete sound to the framework (first consumer)
description:
Phase 3. First real migration — validates latch-driven + data-driven inputs and de-risks the framework before DK.

Add AsteroidsDiscreteSound (circuit + AsteroidsDiscreteInputs) and wire the currently-stubbed bus writes:
- 0x3600 explosion: bits 2-5 volume/data; bits 6-7 pitch divider (MAME-observed 00->12, 01->6, 10->3, 11->5 — verify against schematic).
- 0x3A00 thump: bit 4 enable; low nibble DAC data.
- 0x3C00..=0x3C07 addressable audio latch: saucer enable/fire/select, thrust, ship fire, life.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Signal paths: thump DAC ladder->555/filter; saucer VCO/warble/filter; fire decay-square/filter; thrust LFSR->band/low-pass; explosion sampled-noise->RC; life 3kHz square -> output mix -> gain.

Remove no_audio from AsteroidsSystem; route AudioSource through the device. Saveable + Debuggable (SAUCER/THRUST/THUMP_DATA/EXPLODE_PITCH/NOISE_LFSR ...). Tests: mapping of each write, noise reset pulse, audio drains after a frame, save/load.
close_reason: Asteroids migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287 ground truth. Built machines/src/asteroids_sound.rs (AsteroidsDiscreteSound) modeling all 7 asteroid_a.cpp paths; wired bus writes 0x3600/0x3A00/0x3C00-07(write_d7)/0x3E00; replaced no_audio with a hand AudioSource; Saveable+Debuggable; ticked per frame. Added a triangle-wave primitive to the framework for the saucer. Built a MAME-capture-vs-Phosphor comparison rig (tools/sound-reference/ + machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs) which caught two bugs the ear missed (explosion DC-locked on XNOR all-ones seed; thump 4x too high) — now every effect matches MAME within tolerance. Documented in docs/debugging-asteroids-discrete-sound.md. Remaining low-end-rumble polish tracked in phosphor-emulator-asteroids-sound-postprocessing-hm4. Tests/clippy/fmt green.

title: Lunar Lander: migrate discrete sound to the framework
description:
Phase 4. Compact register-driven circuit; reuses Atari noise/latch primitives established by the Asteroids migration.

Add LunarLanderDiscreteSound and wire stubs:
- 0x3C00 sound register: bits 0-2 thrust volume; bit 3 explosion enable; bit 4 3kHz tone enable; bit 5 6kHz tone enable.
- 0x3E00 noise reset pulse.

Circuit: 12kHz LFSR noise -> RC filter -> thrust gain (3-bit) -> band/low-pass; explosion gate; 3kHz and 6kHz fixed tones; final mix + output filter/gain.

Remove no_audio from LunarLanderSystem. Saveable + Debuggable. Tests: register mapping, noise reset, tone-only deterministic non-silent output, thrust/explosion non-silent, save/load.
close_reason: Lunar Lander migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287. New machines/src/llander_sound.rs (LunarLanderDiscreteSound) models MAME's llander_discrete netlist: a shared resettable 12kHz XNOR LFSR (Custom LanderNoise) -> RC LP -> band-passed thrust + unfiltered explosion (which reuses the 3-bit thrust value as its volume) -> 560Hz LP, plus fixed 3kHz/6kHz alert tones. Wired 0x3C00 sound register + 0x3E00 noise reset in llander.rs; replaced no_audio with a hand AudioSource; tick per frame; reset; Saveable+Debuggable; 5 tests. Extended the capture rig (drive_llander_sound.lua + llander_capture.rs + analyzer --llander); tuned gains to MAME's measured RMS balance (thrust 161~158, tones 21~21, explosion 1280~1712). Explosion's ~75% level + lower centroid is the same MAME output post-processing gap tracked in hm4. Tests/clippy/fmt green.

title: Donkey Kong: migrate DkongDiscrete to the framework
description:
Phase 5. Hardest migration: shared analog mixer + DAC-into-analog + discharge. Needs the diode/resistor mixers and DAC ladder from the primitives phase, plus a Node::Custom for DK's 555 control-voltage mixer.

Replace DkongDiscrete with DkongDiscreteSound:
- Tkg04Board::write_sound_control_bit feeds named circuit inputs (walk/jump/stomp).
- I8035 DAC writes feed the circuit DAC input; discharge/control lines feed inputs.
- Circuit owns stomp/jump/walk/DAC -> shared resistor mixer -> amp/filter -> resampler (replaces the current late post-resample PCM mix).
- Tkg04Board::fill_audio drains from the device.

Update TKG-04 audio, save-state, reset, and debug integration; preserve the frontend-facing machine API. Extend existing TKG-04 save-state tests. Debug registers: LATCH/WALK/JUMP/STOMP/DAC/DISCHARGE/MIX_OUT. (DK Jr. reuse is the cheap generalization check — share primitives, different topology.)
close_reason: Donkey Kong migrated to the discrete sound framework and verified against MAME 0.287 captures. New machines/src/dkong_sound.rs (DkongDiscreteSound): the I8035 DAC enters as an external source and is summed in-circuit with walk/jump/stomp (Custom components: 555 VCO + RC envelopes + LFSR), replacing the post-resample PCM add. Wired tkg04.rs (feed_dac steps the circuit per box-filtered DAC sample; write_sound_bit; fill_audio; save/load; reset; #[debug_device]); removed core DkongDiscrete. Built the MAME-vs-Phosphor comparison rig for DK (drive_dkong_sound.lua halts the Z80 to isolate the discrete effects; dkong_capture.rs; analyzer --dkong) — caught that the effects were ~135x too loud and ~5kHz too bright vs MAME. Fixed with per-effect 2nd-order low-passes (darken to MAME's ~300-1000Hz centroids) + MAME relative balance (walk subtle/jump/stomp prominent), and a DAC attenuation (~0.55, like MAME's VR2) to give output headroom so the effects are audible without clipping the full-scale music. User-confirmed audible. Tests/clippy/fmt green. title: Missile Command: emulate + expose the R8 game-options DIP bank

title: Epic: DRY cleanup — boilerplate reduction across core/frontend/machines
description:
Remove mechanical copy-paste boilerplate that the existing abstractions (core::cpu::flags, M68xxAlu, Disassemble, the machines delegation-macro layer) do not yet cover. Per-instance DATA (opcode->operation mappings, DIP tables, per-button input maps, circuit models) stays exactly where it is. No cycle-accuracy contract is touched: timing lives in the perform_*/alu_* helpers and the per-cycle state machines, not in the wrappers being collapsed. Design: ~/dry-refactors.md.

Scope differs from the design doc in three ways, all verified against the tree:

1. AREA 4a IS DROPPED — already done, and done better than proposed. The doc describes tools/disasm/src/main.rs:330-386 carrying a copy of frontend/src/rom_path.rs. Neither side exists: frontend/src/rom_path.rs is gone, there is no load_rom_set/load_from_zip/zip_err anywhere under tools/, and the canonical implementation now lives at harness/src/rom_path.rs:13 — matching what frontend/CLAUDE.md and the root CLAUDE.md describe. The docs proposed destination (machines/src/rom_loader.rs) was also the wrong layer; phosphor-machines has no business owning filesystem and ZIP I/O. No issue filed.

2. AREA 5d IS DROPPED on policy grounds. It proposes impl_board_input! to generate handle_input, but machines/CLAUDE.md:52 names handle_input explicitly in the list of machine-specific behavior that must stay in normal trait impls ("run_frame, reset, handle_input, NVRAM mapping, profiling ... dont widen the macro option language to hide it"). The doc catches this hazard for 5e and misses it for 5d despite quoting the same sentence. Four call sites is not worth relitigating the boundary. No issue filed.

3. AREAS 5e and 5f are not filed — the doc already scopes them to skip/confirm-first and that is the right call.

Two count corrections, both in the direction of MORE value (estimates fixed in the child issues):
- Area 1 undercounts M6809 by ~2.4x. Actual pub(crate) fn op_ counts: M6800 = 116 (binary 72, unary 24, shift 20); M6809 = 169 (binary 73, unary 34, shift 25, word 37). Doc says ~130 and ~70. Real total ~285 wrappers, not ~200, so the ~1,200 LOC estimate is conservative.
- Area 5a undercounts by >2x: ~40 MachineEntry::new registrations across 35 files, not "~18 copies". Several files register 2-3 variants.

Doc-hygiene note: Area 4as staleness and Area 5s line-reference drift (~10-20 lines; pacman handle_input is at :244-248 not :223-233, DipSwitches starts at :251 not :235) mean the references should be re-verified at the start of each area rather than trusted at face value. Areas 1-4 refs that were checked were accurate.

Recommended order: Area 1 (biggest win, zero timing risk) and 5a first, then 5b/5c, then 2, 3, 4. Land each as its own refactor: commit so any regression bisects cleanly.
close_reason:
All nine children closed; branch dry is 53 files changed, +1772/-3966 (net -2194 lines).

WHAT LANDED
.1 M68xx ALU wrapper macros — m68xx_alu_acc!/m68xx_alu_rmw!/m68xx_alu_inherent!; 243 wrappers (M6800 116, M6809 127) collapsed to table rows.
.2 register_machine! — 36 of 40 machine registrations to one line across 33 files.
.3 impl_dip_switches! — 22 of 26 DipSwitches impls, incl. a masked-arm family (galaxian/mooncresta/frogger/scramble/scobra) the issue had not scoped.
.4 assert_dip_banks_valid migration + dip_test_suite! — the generated suite ADDS coverage (every choice of every option, vs one hand-picked choice before).
.5 Z80 flag helpers + rotate_a.
.6 debug-UI entry-field helpers + fmt_hex_value.
.7 cpu::flags::parity + cpu::disasm::hex_bytes.
.8 doc corrections — closed as not worth doing; Area 5d recorded there as REJECTED (it would generate handle_input, which machines/CLAUDE.md fences).
.9 Z80 flag helpers extended to bit/block/load_store, incl. block_xy_flags for the bit-1 Y rule.

ONE INTENDED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, isolated in its own commit (fe6e7bf): the debug register grid now zero-pads 32-bit registers ({:08X}, was a bare {:X}), affecting every M68000 and i8088 machine. The epic's 'no behaviour change' framing was wrong about this, and the issue's framing ('unexpected widths') was too: 32 is a live width.

THE SCOPE CORRECTIONS IN THIS EPIC'S OWN DESCRIPTION HELD UP — 4a was already done (re-verified in .7), 5d is rejected on policy, 5e/5f rightly unfiled, and both count corrections were accurate.

WHAT THE EPIC TAUGHT, beyond the code: the doc-hygiene note was the most valuable line in it, and understated. Line references drifted in every area, but three areas also had substantively WRONG claims that only re-verification caught — the debug memory viewer was not a third hex_bytes caller; 32-bit was not an 'unexpected' register width; block.rs was not a drop-in for xy_flags (its Y comes from bit 1). One of those was in an issue I wrote myself, and .9 turned up two more of my own errors (a missed 20th site, and CB rotates taking X/Y from the result not the operand).

METHOD WORTH REUSING: for anything without existing vectors, build a temporary exhaustive differential digest, require it byte-identical across the refactor, and mutation-check the digest itself so a false 'no change' is impossible. Used in .1 (266k m6809 vectors), .2 (registry), .3 (DIP probes), .5 and .9 (Z80 flag digests, mutation-checked on both sides), .7 (3259-line disasm output). Every one of them was deleted afterwards.

FOLLOW-UPS FILED: phosphor-emulator-m6809-tst-vma-cycle-2kaj (pre-existing TST dummy-VMA-cycle failure that blocks the cpu-validation suite from covering opcodes past 0x0D).

title: DRY 1: M68xx op_* ALU wrapper macros (m68xx_alu_mem! / m68xx_alu_inherent!)
description:
Every M6800/M6809 ALU opcode has a hand-written wrapper whose only variation is (fn name, addressing helper, perform_* operation, Acc::A | Acc::B). The wrappers exist as named functions only because the dispatch match in mod.rs references them by name (e.g. core/src/cpu/m6800/mod.rs:295, `0x90 => self.op_suba_dir(cycle, bus, master)`).

VERIFIED COUNTS (pub(crate) fn op_), which correct the design docs "~130 M6800 / ~70 M6809":
  m6800/alu/binary.rs  72     m6809/alu/binary.rs  73
  m6800/alu/unary.rs   24     m6809/alu/unary.rs   34
  m6800/alu/shift.rs   20     m6809/alu/shift.rs   25
                              m6809/alu/word.rs    37
  M6800 total 116             M6809 total 169
Real total ~285 wrappers, not ~200 — M6809 is undercounted by ~2.4x in the doc. The ~1,200 LOC saving is therefore conservative.

Add two macro_rules! generators alongside the code they expand (new core/src/cpu/m68xx_alu_macros.rs, or inline in m68xx.rs). Declarative macros suffice — no need for the phosphor-macros proc-macro crate.

Macro A (bus-addressed): one row per opcode — doc text, fn name, addressing helper, perform_* method, accumulator — expanding to the exact generic signature in use today (`pub(crate) fn $name<B: Bus<Address = u16, Data = u8> + ?Sized>(&mut self, cycle: u8, bus: &mut B, master: BusMaster)` forwarding to `self.$addr(cycle, bus, master, |cpu, op| cpu.$perform(Acc::$acc, op))`).

Macro B (inherent register): doc, fn name, register field, perform_* — expanding to `if cycle == 0 { self.$reg = self.$perform(self.$reg); self.state = ExecState::Fetch; }`.

Dispatch match arms are UNCHANGED — the macros emit the same function names mod.rs already calls.

Constraints:
- Doc comments are mandatory. core/CLAUDE.md requires every instructions doc comment to document flag behavior. Carry the doc text as the first column of each macro row and emit via #[doc = $doc]. Do not drop it during transcription.
- CLR special-case: perform_clr() takes no operand (m6800/alu/unary.rs:41-46). Macro B needs a no-operand variant arm, or a separate one-row form for op_clra/op_clrb.
- M6809 extras: word.rs (16-bit, 37 wrappers) and any DP/indexed-postbyte variants may not fit Macro As shape. Keep those hand-written if they do not — cover the common 8-bit cases and stop. Do not force a fit.

Zero risk to timing — the wrappers contain no cycle logic, they only forward to perform_*/alu_*. The only real hazard is mis-transcribing the opcode->op table, which the test suite and cross-validation catch directly.

Sequencing: M6800 first (no DP/Y/U registers, no multi-byte prefixes), confirm green, then apply the same macros to M6809.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-core m6800 && cargo test -p phosphor-core m6809 && cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation, then cross-validation (cd cross-validation && make && ./bin/validate_m6809 ../cpu-validation/test_data/m6809/*.json && ./bin/validate_m6800 ../cpu-validation/test_data/m6800/*.json). CPU changes require the cross-validation run per CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: M6800 (116 ops) and M6809 (127 ops) ALU wrappers now generated from m68xx_alu_acc!/m68xx_alu_rmw!/m68xx_alu_inherent! tables in core/src/cpu/m68xx_alu_macros.rs; ~2500 lines down to ~700, dispatch untouched. word.rs and the cycle-state-machine ops (MUL/DAA/ABX/NOP/SEX) left hand-written per the issue's guidance. Verified by full core suite, m6800 single-step (192k cases, all pass), m6800 cross-validation (192k, 0 failed), and a byte-identical per-opcode digest over all 266k m6809 vectors before vs after.

title: DRY 5a: register_machine! — collapse factory + inventory::submit boilerplate
description:
Every front-end machine ends with a byte-identical factory + registration varying only by type, CLI name and rom_names (joust.rs:435-445 verified exact):

  fn create_machine(rom_set: &RomSet) -> Result<Box<dyn FrontendMachine>, RomLoadError> {
      let mut sys = JoustSystem::new();
      sys.load_rom_set(rom_set)?;
      Ok(Box::new(sys))
  }
  inventory::submit! { MachineEntry::new("joust", &["joust"], create_machine) }

Every wrapper already has Type::new() + load_rom_set(&RomSet), so: register_machine!(JoustSystem, "joust", &["joust"]); with a second arm for the multi-config loader (digdug.rs:1435-1455 loops over ALL_CONFIGS): register_machine!(DigDugSystem, "digdug", &[...], with_loader = load_digdug).

VERIFIED SCALE — the doc says "~18 copies". Actual: ~40 MachineEntry::new registrations across 35 files (several files register 2-3 variants). The ~180 LOC estimate should be roughly doubled. Removes a real copy-paste footgun too (wrong type in Box::new).

CROSS-EPIC INTERACTION — coordinate with phosphor-emulator-control-handling-dyvs.4 (MachineEntry::controls + input contract test). If that lands, register_machine! needs a FOURTH argument naming the controls const: register_machine!(JoustSystem, "joust", &["joust"], JOUST_CONTROLS). It cannot derive that name, and this was verified:
- The macro only receives type, CLI name and rom_names.
- The const name does not track the type or the CLI name: JOUST_CONTROLS, but also CONGO_CONTROLS (congo_bongo.rs:1426) and DKONG_CONTROLS (donkey_kong.rs:255). paste!-style ident derivation would be wrong in at least those two cases.
- An associated const on InputConfigurable is NOT an option: it is a supertrait of FrontendMachine (core/src/core/machine.rs:687-695), used as Box<dyn FrontendMachine> in registry.rs:19. Associated consts make a trait non-dyn-compatible and there is no `where Self: Sized` escape hatch for consts as there is for methods — it would break the registry.
The consts are mostly private, but register_machine! expands in the same module so visibility is fine.

Do these together if possible — one pass over ~35-40 sites instead of two. But do NOT block dyvs.4 on this macro: it does not eliminate the per-site hand-work, only the duplicated factory body.

New macro goes alongside the existing delegation layer in machines/src/lib.rs (impl_board_delegation!, machine_save_state!, et al). Respects machines/CLAUDE.md:52 — this is obvious delegation, not machine-specific behavior.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-machines; confirm the machine list / registry is unchanged (registry::all() count and names identical before/after).
close_reason: register_machine! added to machines/src/lib.rs; 36 of 40 registrations collapsed to one line across 33 files (-164 net lines, -254 at the sites). Three arms: standard Type::new()+load_rom_set, 'new =' for variant constructors (pisces x2, docastle x3), 'configs =' for the ALL_CONFIGS retry loop (digdug, galaga). Four left hand-written because they do more than construct-and-load: starwars, esb, quantum. Takes the controls const as a fourth argument as dyvs.4 predicted. Verified: registry digest (name, rom_names, full stable_name list for all 40 entries) byte-identical before and after; machines/frontend/harness/core tests, clippy --all-features --all-targets, and fmt --check all clean.

title: DRY 5b: impl_dip_switches! — collapse DipSwitches impl bodies
close_reason: impl_dip_switches! added to machines/src/lib.rs; 22 of 26 DipSwitches impls collapsed across 22 files (-478 lines at the sites, +91 for the macro). Four arms: 1-bank, 2-bank, and masked 2-/3-bank for machines whose DIPs share an input port with live signals (reads mask, writes merge) — the issue only scoped the plain forms, but frogger/scramble/scobra/galaxian/mooncresta were the same duplication and are now covered. title: DRY 5c: migrate pacman/digdug onto assert_dip_banks_valid + dip_test_suite! macro
description:
A shared helper crate::assert_dip_banks_valid(...) already exists at machines/src/lib.rs:437-469 and donkey_kong*.rs use it, but pacman.rs and digdug.rs predate it and inline near-verbatim validity / decompose / round-trip checks.

Two steps:
1. Migrate pacman + digdug onto assert_dip_banks_valid. Deletes ~60 LOC with no new abstraction — do this half even if step 2 is skipped.
2. Add dip_test_suite!(Type, &[expected_bank0, ...]) generating the default-byte assertion + assert_dip_banks_valid + the mask/round-trip tests.

NOTE ON LINE REFERENCES: the doc cites pacman.rs:352-425 and digdug.rs:1457-1539 for the inline test blocks, but Area 5s refs have drifted ~10-20 lines against the current tree. Re-verify before editing.

close_reason: Both steps done. Step 1: pacman/digdug migrated onto assert_dip_banks_valid (-64 lines). Assertions were diffed, not regenerated — two the helper does not cover were kept explicitly (digdug's banks-cover-all-8-bits, both machines' out-of-range read), and the explicit bank-count asserts dropped as redundant since the helper asserts banks.len() == defaults.len(). Step 2: dip_test_suite!(Type, &[power-on bytes]) generating three tests that derive everything else from the machine's own DIP table, so adopting it ADDS coverage: set_dip_option is now checked for every choice of every option (the hand-written version picked one), and round-trip for 4 probes per bank incl. cross-bank and out-of-range. Round-trip is scoped to the union of the bank's option masks so the port-sharing machines (galaxian et al) can adopt it later. Teeth verified by 5 mutations across both steps, each caught and restored: overlapping option mask, drifted power-on byte, DIP accessor dropping a bit, two banks aliased to one field. Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-machines, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt --check all clean. NOT DONE (deliberate, out of scope): rolling dip_test_suite! out to the other ~20 DIP machines, which would add the exhaustive per-choice coverage there too — worth a follow-up issue.

title: DRY 2: Z80 flag-building helpers + accumulator rotate unification
description:
Unlike the M68xx family the Z80 has no shared flag helper and builds its flag byte inline in ~20 places in core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs. Repeated fragments: S+Z computation from a result (~15x); the undocumented `f |= result & (Flag::X | Flag::Y)` line (~20x); the `self.f = f; self.q = self.f;` commit pair (~20x). The four accumulator rotates op_rlca/op_rrca/op_rla/op_rra (alu.rs:457-526) are near-identical, differing only in direction and carry handling.

Add private helpers on Z80, mirroring M68xxAlu:
  fn set_sz_from(f: &mut u8, result: u8);   // sets S and Z from result
  fn apply_xy(f: &mut u8, source: u8);      // undocumented X/Y bits from source
  fn commit_flags(&mut self, f: u8) { self.f = f; self.q = self.f; }
then collapse the four rotates into fn rotate_a(&mut self, left: bool, through_carry: bool) with four thin callers.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT — the X/Y SOURCE differs by operation and must be passed explicitly, never hardcoded to `result`:
- CP uses the OPERAND, not the result — VERIFIED at core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs:124, and the code already carries the comment "X/Y come from the operand for CP, not the result".
- SCF/CCF use A | F when q == 0 (alu.rs:604, :621).
apply_xy therefore takes `source` as a parameter and each call site supplies the correct value. Audit every call site before substituting.

Risk assessment differs slightly from the design doc: the doc rates this moderate because the Z80 has the most flag corner cases in the codebase, which is true — but the quirks are already commented AT their sites, so the audit has something concrete to grep for rather than relying on the refactorers memory. Still the most care-intensive area in this epic.

Also note core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs:7-9 already has `pub(super) fn get_parity` — see the sibling issue on the shared parity helper; do not duplicate that work here.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-core z80, plus Z80 cross-validation vectors if present. Per CLAUDE.md any CPU change runs the cross-validation script.
close_reason:
Both halves done in 2 commits on branch dry. Helpers sz_flags/sz_flags16/xy_flags/commit_flags added to core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs and all 16 non-rotate flag sites migrated; the four accumulator rotates collapsed into rotate_a(left, through_carry). Net -50/+36 on the rotates plus ~60 lines off the flag sites.

THE CRITICAL CONSTRAINT WAS HONOURED: xy_flags takes an explicit source, never defaults to the result. Audited all 20 sites — CP takes X/Y from the operand (comment retained), ADD/ADC/SBC HL,rr from the high byte of the 16-bit result, SCF/CCF from A or A|F per prev_q; the other 12 use the result. commit_flags exists because Q is what the SCF/CCF quirk reads via prev_q, so a bare self.f write would silently break those opcodes.

Deviation from the issue's suggested signatures: helpers RETURN flag bits rather than taking &mut u8, which composes with the existing  idiom and cannot be forgotten. Added sz_flags16 beyond the three named, for the two 16-bit ADC/SBC HL sites.

VERIFICATION (no Z80 vectors exist in cpu-validation and no Z80 validator in cross-validation, so I built one): an exhaustive differential FNV digest over (A,F,HL,(HL),MEMPTR) covering every 8-bit ALU op x 256x256 operands x carry, INC/DEC over all 8 register slots, DAA/CPL/NEG/SCF/CCF/rotates over all 256 A x 256 F, SCF/CCF after both a flag-writing and non-flag-writing lead (both Q paths), RRD/RLD over all A x all memory, and 16-bit adds over a carry-boundary+stride sweep. Byte-identical before and after both commits: b3aa138f1072f06f. The digest was validated by 3 mutations, each caught and reverted: CP X/Y source -> result (f2eaeea3), SCF prev_q test inverted (8048ce6b), RLCA wired as RLA (3ff16879). Temp harness deleted.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-core clean; clippy --all-features --all-targets and fmt --check clean; machines/frontend/harness clean; cpu-validation clean except the pre-existing m6809 TST failure tracked as phosphor-emulator-m6809-tst-vma-cycle-2kaj.

NOT DONE (out of scope, helpers are pub(super) so it is a drop-in follow-up): bit.rs (~6 sites), block.rs (~10) and load_store.rs (~3) still build flags inline. block.rs needs its own audit — the INI/OUTI/CPI family has its own X/Y and PV quirks.

title: DRY 3: frontend debug-UI widget helpers (hex input field + width-keyed hex formatter)
description:
File: frontend/src/debug_ui.rs.

3a. Hex input field. A $-prefixed monospace TextEdit + Enter detection + from_str_radix parse repeats at device register write (:594-624, two fields), PC breakpoint add (:695-712), watchpoint add (:775-805) and memory "Go" (:1099-1121). VERIFIED counts: the line `let enter = resp.lost_focus() && ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(egui::Key::Enter));` appears 6x (doc says 5) and from_str_radix 6x (doc says 4).

Add:
  /// A $-prefixed monospace hex field plus an Add/Go button (or Enter).
  /// Returns the parsed value once, on the frame the user commits.
  fn hex_input_field<T>(ui: &mut egui::Ui, label: &str, buf: &mut String,
                        width: f32, button: &str, parse: impl Fn(&str) -> Option<T>) -> Option<T>
The two-field device-write case reuses the primitive twice. Collapses ~15 lines per site to ~1.

3b. Width-keyed hex formatter. The `match width { 2 => "{:04X}", 4 => "{:08X}", _ => "{:02X}" }` formatting repeats at draw_register_grid (:411-415, keyed on BIT-width), watchpoint hit value (:848-852, BYTE-width) and format_trace_event (:916-920, byte-width). Add fn fmt_hex_value(value: u32, byte_width: u8) -> String plus a thin bit-width adapter for the register grid.

CAVEAT — 3b IS A BEHAVIOR CHANGE, contrary to the epics "no behavior change" framing. The design doc notes it in passing as "also fixes a latent inconsistency": the register grid falls back to {:X} while the other two fall back to {:02X}, so unifying them changes what the register grid renders for unexpected widths. It is a fix and it is UI-only, but it must be called out in the commit message rather than riding along silently inside a refactor: commit.

Watch the bit-width vs byte-width distinction when wiring the adapter — that is the one place a transcription slip produces wrong output rather than a compile error.

Gate: cargo build -p phosphor-frontend, then a manual run exercising breakpoint / watchpoint / memory-Go / device-write fields: cargo run -p phosphor-frontend -- <machine> <roms> --scale 3.
close_reason:
Done in 3 commits on branch dry (branch dry).

3a — entry_field(ui,label,buf,width)->bool and entry_commit(ui,label,buf,width,button,parse)->Option<T> in frontend/src/debug_ui.rs; all 6 sites migrated. Split into primitive + composed deliberately: the watchpoint row puts R/W checkboxes BETWEEN field and button and the device-write row has one button for two fields, so a single field+button helper would have reordered those widgets. Behaviour preserved in three details that are easy to tidy away by accident: parse stays per-site (cycle/frame are DECIMAL, not hex; hex sites differ on whitespace tolerance), clear-on-success stays per-site (memory Go deliberately keeps its text), and Enter still commits only from the device-write VALUE field.

3b — fmt_hex_value(value, byte_width) extracted, with a unit test. Split across 2 commits so the behaviour change is isolated and independently revertable.

THE CAVEAT WAS UNDERSTATED AND IS NOW CORRECTED. The issue (and design doc) described the register-grid unification as changing 'unexpected widths'. It does not: 32 is a LIVE width. Verified by grepping every DebugRegister construction in core — widths in use are exactly 8, 16, 32, and the 32-bit ones are the M68000's PC/D0-D7/A0-A7/USP/SSP (cpu/state.rs:237-265) and the i8088's CS:IP (cpu/i8088/mod.rs:364). So the fall-through {:X} arm is what renders EVERY 32-bit register today, and this changes the register display of foodf, marble, roadrunner, quantum, atari_system1 and gottlieb/qbert. Example: PC 0x1A2B3C was $1A2B3C, now $001A2B3C. Intended direction (fixed-width column matching 8/16-bit behaviour) but a real visible change, called out in its own commit title as BEHAVIOUR CHANGE.

Gate: cargo build/clippy --all-features --all-targets/fmt --check and the frontend test suite (58 tests, +2 added for fmt_hex_value and the bit->byte mapping) all clean.

GATE NOT FULLY MET — the issue asks for a manual interactive run exercising the breakpoint/watchpoint/memory-Go/device-write fields. I cannot drive an interactive GUI here. Substitutes done instead: a headless run of foodf (an M68000 machine, 120 frames, PNG+WAV written, no panic) proving the app path is intact, plus a line-by-line review that each migrated row emits its widgets in the original order. The interactive click-through of the four field types is still worth doing before this is considered signed off.

title: DRY 4: shared parity helper + hex_bytes join (4a dropped as already done)
description:
Two small cross-crate extractions. The design docs Area 4a is NOT part of this issue — see below.

4b. Shared parity helper. core/src/cpu/i8088/flags.rs:62-78 builds a table-backed parity(u8) -> bool; core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs:7-9 computes the same even-parity as `val.count_ones().is_multiple_of(2)`. Promote one core::cpu::flags::parity(u8) -> bool and reuse in both.

CORRECTION to the design doc: it describes the Z80 side as computing parity "inline". It does not — it is already a named `pub(super) fn get_parity` at alu.rs:7-9. So this is unifying two named helpers, not extracting an inline expression. Still worth doing; just a smaller and cleaner change than advertised. Decide which implementation wins (table lookup vs count_ones) on measurement or simplicity, not by default.

4c. hex_bytes join. tools/disasm/src/main.rs:308-313 and frontend/src/debug_ui.rs:1054-1060 independently build "addr + space-joined {:02X} bytes + mnemonic". The decode path is already shared via the Disassemble trait — only the LINE RENDERING is duplicated, and the two differ in column widths and breakpoint markers. Extract ONLY the trivially shared hex_bytes(&[u8]) -> String join (also used by the memory viewer at debug_ui.rs:1159-1165), next to DisassembledInstruction in core/src/cpu/disasm.rs. Do not attempt a full render_line unless the call sites converge — the doc is right to scope this down.

AREA 4a IS DROPPED — already done, and done better than the doc proposed. VERIFIED: frontend/src/rom_path.rs no longer exists; there is no load_rom_set/load_from_zip/zip_err anywhere under tools/; the canonical implementation lives at harness/src/rom_path.rs:13, matching what frontend/CLAUDE.md and the root CLAUDE.md describe. The docs proposed destination (machines/src/rom_loader.rs) was also the wrong layer — phosphor-machines should not own filesystem and ZIP I/O; phosphor-harness is the right home. Nothing to do.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-core (parity), cargo build -p phosphor-disasm and -p phosphor-frontend, plus a disasm smoke test: cargo run -p phosphor-disasm --bin disasm -- machine --machine mariobros --region sound <roms>. Since 4b touches CPU flag code, run cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation and the i8088/z80 suites.
close_reason:
Done in 2 commits on branch dry.

4b — cpu::flags::parity(u8)->bool added; the i8088's 256-entry const table and Z80::get_parity both removed. i8088/flags.rs re-exports the shared fn so its call sites and tests are untouched; the Z80's ten callers across alu/bit/block/load_store call it directly.

Winner picked on measurement as the issue asked, not by default: over 26M calls on a pseudo-random byte stream the table ran ~0.67 ns/call vs ~0.72 for count_ones, so the table is ~7% faster — a 0.05 ns absolute difference on an operation done a few times per emulated instruction. Not worth a 256-byte static plus twelve lines to memoise the very expression that generated it, so count_ones wins on simplicity. The measurement is recorded in the doc comment so the trade can be revisited. Equivalence was proved exhaustively (all 256 inputs asserted equal before timing), not spot-checked.

4c — cpu::disasm::hex_bytes extracted, used by the disasm CLI and the debug UI's disassembly pane. Scoped to the join only, per the issue: the surrounding line differs (CLI pads to 23 with a 6-digit address, debug UI pads to 12 with a breakpoint marker) and the doc comment says so.

CORRECTION to the issue: it lists the memory viewer as a third hex_bytes caller. It is not — verified. That code builds a 16-column grid with a gap after column 8, a trailing space per byte, --/.. markers for I/O and unmapped cells, and a parallel ASCII column. It shares the {:02X} token and nothing else, and is untouched. Two call sites, not three.

4a re-verified independently and confirmed already done: no frontend/src/rom_path.rs, and load_rom_set(path, rom_names)/load_from_zip/zip_err exist only at harness/src/rom_path.rs. (The ~35 load_rom_set(&mut self, rom_set: &RomSet) in machines are per-machine ROM decoders taking an already-loaded RomSet, not filesystem I/O.) Nothing to do.

title: Extend the Z80 flag helpers to bit.rs / block.rs / load_store.rs
description:
DRY 2 (phosphor-emulator-dry-refactors-0lhx.5) added sz_flags / sz_flags16 / xy_flags / commit_flags to core/src/cpu/z80/alu.rs and migrated that file. The helpers are pub(super), so the remaining Z80 files can adopt them, but they were left out of scope. Until they do, the crate has two idioms for the same thing.

VERIFIED SITE COUNTS (occurrences of the `self.f = f; self.q = self.f;` commit pair):
  bit.rs         6   lines 111, 129, 174, 207, 267, 287
  block.rs      10   lines 50, 98, 111, 180, 241, 255, 331, 401, 470, 536
  load_store.rs  3   lines 536, 563, 688

commit_flags applies to all 19 unconditionally — it is a pure mechanical
substitution and captures the Q-latch invariant the SCF/CCF quirk depends on.
sz_flags and xy_flags need a per-site audit, and block.rs is where the care is.

BLOCK.RS DOES NOT UNIFORMLY FIT xy_flags — VERIFIED, DO NOT BULK-SUBSTITUTE.
xy_flags(source) is `source & (X|Y)`, i.e. X = bit 3 (0x08) and Y = bit 5
(0x20) of the source. The LDI/LDD/LDIR/LDDR family does something different
(block.rs:42-48 and the parallel sites):

    // Undocumented: X = bit 3 of (val+A), Y = bit 1 of (val+A)
    if (n & 0x08) != 0 { f |= Flag::X as u8; }
    if (n & 0x02) != 0 { f |= Flag::Y as u8; }

Y comes from bit 1, not bit 5, so xy_flags is simply the wrong function there
and a naive substitution silently corrupts the Y flag. Either leave those
sites hand-written or add a separate helper (e.g. block_xy_flags(n)) that
states the bit-1 rule once.

The repeat path IS a plain fit: block.rs:107-110 takes X/Y from the high byte
of the rewound PC via the ordinary bit-3/bit-5 mask, so xy_flags((pc>>8) as u8)
is correct there.

Audit bit.rs and load_store.rs the same way before substituting; the DRY 2
audit found four X/Y sources in alu.rs alone that were not the result.

VERIFICATION APPROACH THAT WORKED FOR DRY 2 — reuse it. There are no Z80
vectors in cpu-validation and no Z80 validator in cross-validation, so DRY 2
built a temporary exhaustive differential digest as core/tests/tmp_z80_flag_digest.rs:
an FNV hash over (A, F, HL, (HL), MEMPTR) after running each opcode across its
full input space, captured before and after and required to be byte-identical
(it was: b3aa138f1072f06f). It was itself validated by mutation — three
deliberate breakages each changed the hash. See commit 3adddc3 for the harness
shape; extend the opcode list to cover the block/bit/load_store families
(LDI/LDD/LDIR/LDDR, CPI/CPD/CPIR/CPDR, INI/IND/INIR/INDR, OUTI/OUTD/OTIR/OTDR,
the CB-prefixed rotates/shifts, BIT/SET/RES, and LD A,I / LD A,R).

Note the CB-prefixed rotates take X/Y from the operand, unlike the accumulator
rotates DRY 2 unified, which take them from A after the rotate.

Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-core, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt
--check, plus the digest A/B above. Per CLAUDE.md a CPU change also runs the
cross-validation script, which has no Z80 target — the digest is the substitute.
close_reason:
Done in 2 commits on branch dry. All Z80 flag writes now go through the shared helpers; the only remaining 'self.q = self.f' in the CPU is inside commit_flags itself.

Commit 1 (bit.rs, load_store.rs): do_cb_rotate_shift onto sz_flags/xy_flags; BIT's three different X/Y sources (operand register, MEMPTR high byte, indexed EA high byte) each passed explicitly; LD A,I / LD A,R / IN r,(C) onto sz_flags/xy_flags/commit_flags.

Commit 2 (block.rs): added a block-local block_xy_flags(n) for the four LDI/LDD/CPI/CPD sites (X from bit 3, Y from bit 1, n derived), the two repeat paths onto the ordinary xy_flags(pc_h), the I/O group onto sz_flags(self.b)+xy_flags(self.b), and CPI/CPD S/Z onto sz_flags. The INIR/OTIR repeat paths keep their in-place mutation sequence — the H re-derivation and PV XNOR read self.f back between steps, so hoisting to a local would be a rewrite not a substitution — but now end in commit_flags(self.f).

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN ISSUE, both found by re-verifying at the start as the issue itself advises:
1. The site count was 19; it is 20. do_cb_rotate_shift (bit.rs) builds S/Z and X/Y but RETURNS the flag byte instead of committing, so it has no commit pair and the grep missed it.
2. The issue says the CB-prefixed rotates take X/Y from the operand. They do not — do_cb_rotate_shift takes them from the RESULT. It is BIT that uses the operand. The comment now states the distinction at the site.

VERIFICATION: extended the DRY 2 differential digest to cover CB rotates/shifts (every op x register x value x carry), BIT/RES/SET across all 192 opcodes, DD CB indexed variants, the full ED block family (LDI/LDD/LDIR/LDDR, CPI/CPD/CPIR/CPDR, INI/IND/INIR/INDR, OUTI/OUTD/OTIR/OTDR run 4 instructions deep so both the repeat and terminating paths execute), and LD A,I / LD A,R / IN r,(C) — while keeping the DRY 2 opcode set so alu.rs stays pinned. Byte-identical before and after both commits: 6169c3a522f6bf4f.

The digest was mutation-checked on BOTH sides: replacing LDI's bit-1 Y rule with the naive mask before the refactor, and swapping block_xy_flags for xy_flags after it, both yield 32e9113a36ab048f. Producing the SAME wrong hash is the useful part — it confirms xy_flags is precisely the naive substitution the issue warned about, and that block_xy_flags is load-bearing. Temp harness deleted.

title: M6809: DAA/EXG/TFR diverge from the reference core in cross-validation
description:
Found while doing phosphor-emulator-5dgc; unrelated to it and pre-existing
(reproduced on a clean tree at 966fee2, byte-identical counts).

`./bin/validate_m6809 ../cpu-validation/test_data/m6809/*.json` reports three
opcodes failing on REGISTER values, not cycle counts:

    0x19 DAA: 642/1000 failures  [cc expected=192 got=193]
    0x1e EXG: 471/1000 failures  [y expected=58741 got=255]
    0x1f TFR: 505/1000 failures  [y expected=65341 got=255]

That is 1,618 of the 1,900 total mismatches — the large majority.

Two things to sort out:

1. Which side is right. For EXG/TFR the reference yields 255 (0x00FF) where
   phosphor yields the wide value, which smells like the 8<->16-bit transfer
   rule: transferring an 8-bit register into a 16-bit one is documented to
   fill the other half with $FF. If phosphor is not doing that, it is a real
   bug in transfer.rs. For DAA the disagreement is one CC bit (C, given
   192 vs 193) on a case the datasheet may leave undefined.

2. README_m6809.md is stale either way. It claims "All 1,868 mismatches are
   the same known divergence" (the [n] extended-indirect +3 cycle case) and
   that "any mismatch in a register ... is a regression". Neither matches what
   the validator actually reports — the register mismatches above dominate and
   are not mentioned at all. The self-validation suite passes on these
   opcodes, so the vectors agree with phosphor; only the reference disagrees.
close_reason:
Both sides answered and fixed.

DAA (0x19): phosphor was wrong, twice. It recomputed C from the adjustment
alone, but the programming manual defines C as 'set if a carry is generated or
if the carry bit was set before the operation' — the carry of the whole BCD
add. It also left V alone where the reference clears it; V is documented
undefined for DAA, so clearing it is a free tie-break that costs nothing and
removes 511 unfixable mismatches. 0x19 now passes 1000/1000.

TFR/EXG (0x1e/0x1f): both sides were wrong. Phosphor silently did nothing on a
mixed-size postbyte; the reference drives the whole 16-bit transfer path with
$FF, losing the source. Real hardware transfers: a register drives only as
many of the 16 bits as it is wide and the rest read back as ones, so TFR A,X
gives X=$FF:A and TFR X,A gives A=X.low (6809.org.uk/dragon/illegal-opcodes).
Phosphor now does that, which also defines codes 6/7/12-15 as reading $FFFF
and latching nothing. The cross-validation gap moved rather than closed — ~1003
mismatches remain where the reference is the wrong side, now documented.

Full run: 264,723/266,000 (99.5%), 1,277 mismatches, all in the two documented
divergences. Both READMEs restated.

title: Epic: Frame-level regression testing
description:
Nothing in the repo pins what any machine is supposed to look like. A palette, sprite-priority or scroll regression in any of roughly 40 machines is currently detected by a human launching that specific game.

tools/script/tests/frameshot_parity.rs is the closest thing, and it is not this: it boots Mr. Do twice — once through Harness, once through DebugSession — and asserts the pixels match. That catches wiring drift between two of our own code paths. A change that breaks both paths identically still passes.

Every piece needed already exists and is unused for this purpose: Harness, DebugSession, screenshot/PNG, apply_orientation, and the frameshot/imgdiff tooling.

This epic must land before the structural refactors (concrete bus dispatch, cycle-accurate CPUs), which are exactly the changes most likely to move pixels.
close_reason: Both children landed. Every registered machine except dkongjr now has a reviewed, committed golden frame, enforced by a registry-driven guard that runs without ROMs. Design recorded in docs/designs/frame-regression.md. This unblocks phosphor-emulator-concrete-bus-dispatch-blzz and the cycle-accurate CPU epics, which now have a pixel-level tripwire. Two rendering bugs surfaced in the process: scobra's orientation (fixed here) and phosphor-emulator-iitc (Tempest, filed).

title: Golden-frame hash infrastructure, ROM-gated
description:
Build the mechanism: for a given machine and frame count, boot via Harness, run to the frame, render through the machine's declared orientation (the render_oriented helper in tools/script/tests/frameshot_parity.rs:29 already does exactly this), and hash the RGB buffer.

Requirements:
- Hashes committed in-repo as data, not embedded in test source, so refreshing a machine is a data change with a visible diff.
- ROM-gated: skip with an eprintln when roms_dir() is None, matching frameshot_parity.rs:66.
- On mismatch, write the actual frame as a PNG next to the expected hash so the failure is inspectable rather than just a hex diff.
- A guard so an empty or all-skipped hash set cannot pass vacuously.
- Frame counts must land past each machine's power-on self-test — galaga needs about 3000 frames, mrdo 3100.

Acceptance: deliberately perturbing a palette entry fails the test for the affected machine and no other.
close_reason: Built harness/tests/golden_frame_test.rs: boot via Harness, run to a pinned frame count, render through the declared orientation, compare a SHA-256 of the oriented RGB frame (plus the vector display list for vector machines). Pins are data in harness/tests/golden/frames.toml with a committed reference PNG per machine; PHOSPHOR_GOLDEN_UPDATE=1 recaptures. Mismatch writes the actual frame to golden/actual/ and prints the disasm imgdiff command. Guards: uniform frames refused even in update mode, undescribed or stale entries fail without ROMs, a ROM dir supplying nothing fails rather than passing on zero comparisons, and a ROM-less test proves each PNG decodes to its pinned hash. Acceptance verified: perturbing one constant in Mr. Do's palette weighting failed mrdo and no other machine (1 of 39).

title: Populate golden-frame hashes across the registered machines
description:
With the infrastructure in place, capture and commit a hash per machine, plus a scripted input sequence where a static attract-mode frame is not representative.

Per-machine work: choose a frame count past the self-test, verify by eye that the captured frame is correct before pinning it, and record what the frame is supposed to show. Pinning a wrong frame is worse than no test.

Vector machines (asteroids, tempest, starwars, llander, quantum, irobot) need thought: vector_display_list is the real output and the raster path is a fallback. Either hash the line list or accept the rasterised fallback — decide and document.

Blocked by the infrastructure sibling.
close_reason: 39 of 40 registered machines pinned, each frame reviewed by eye before pinning and described in its entry. Frame counts chosen per machine to land past the self-test on a representative picture. dkongjr recorded as [[unpinned]] with a reason: no ROM revision in the collection matches its table. frames_toml_covers_every_registered_machine now enforces the roster without ROMs. Vector decision: both hashes — the display list (what the frontend draws) and the rasterised frame (what the headless paths draw); documented in docs/designs/frame-regression.md. joust/robotron/sinistar use committed CMOS fixtures because a cold boot never leaves FACTORY SETTINGS RESTORED (phosphor-emulator-4waf). Two rendering bugs found: scobra's missing orientation (fixed) and tempest's double-applied ROT270 (phosphor-emulator-iitc, pinned as-is with the defect noted).

title: Galaxian/Scramble/Frogger arcade family
description:
Add the Galaxian -> Scramble -> Frogger hardware lineage to Phosphor (full family, both hardware tiers).

No new CPU required (Z80 exists); all sound chips already in-tree (Ay8910, i8255). The only genuinely new subsystem is the Galaxian-style video engine (tilemap + sprites + hardware starfield + bullet/shell RAM + PROM palette). Frogger is the requested anchor and lands on the more complex sound-CPU variant.

Reuse map and full scope in plan: ~/.claude/plans/soft-scribbling-planet.md
Key reuse: core/src/device/ssio.rs (embedded sound-CPU template = Frogger topology), core/src/device/ay8910.rs, core/src/device/i8255.rs, machines/src/mcr2.rs (two-CPU wiring), machines/src/namco_pac.rs + pacman.rs (tilemap+sprite+PROM board shape), machines/src/registry.rs.
close_reason: done

title: P0: Galaxian video engine + board skeleton
description:
New shared module machines/src/galaxian_video.rs: 8x8 2bpp tile decode, 32x28 background tilemap with per-column scroll, ~7-8 hardware sprites (flip bits), HARDWARE STARFIELD generator (LFSR), bullet/shell RAM (missile dots), 32-byte PROM palette decode + star/bullet color logic. Render into RGB24 via Renderable::render_frame. Plus a table-driven Galaxian board skeleton (machines/src/galaxian.rs) modeled on namco_pac.rs (no sound yet).

Critical path: the only piece with real reverse-eng risk (starfield + bullets have no in-tree analog). Validate pixel-exact vs MAME early. Watch bitplane LSB/MSB order and first-wins sprite compositing (see MAME-graphics-debugging memory).
close_reason: Delivered galaxian_video.rs (tile/sprite 2bpp decode, per-column-scroll tilemap, 8 sprites, LFSR starfield, bullet/shell dots, resnet PROM palette) and galaxian.rs board skeleton (Z80, galaxian_map address space, 74LS259 latch, VBLANK NMI, save-state). No sound yet; playable wrapper + ROM set follow in 355.3. Video pieces modeled directly on MAME galaxian sources.

title: Rebuild Galaxian sound as a port of galaxian_discrete
description:
Rewrite core/src/device/galaxian_sound.rs build_circuit as a component-level port of MAME's galaxian_discrete (~/ws/mame/src/mame/galaxian/galaxian_a.cpp), using the new 555/op-amp primitives with the real GAL_R*/GAL_C* schematic values. Keep the register interface (pitch_w/lfo_freq_w/sound_w), input nodes, TuneVoice, and Device/Debuggable/Saveable impls. Voice mapping:
- Background/wolf-whistle: bg_dac -> dac_weighted(R18/17/16/15) -> ne555_cc(R21,C15 cap out) -> gain/add mult-add -> clamp(0,5) -> 3x ne555_astable FS1/2/3 (R22/R23/C17, R25/R26/C18, R28/R29/C19, gated by fs enables) -> resistor_mixer(R24/R27/R30,C20).
- Pitch/tune: keep TuneVoice.
- HIT: rc_disc5(noise, hit, R35+R36, C21) -> op_amp_band_pass([R35,R36], R37, C22, C23).
- FIRE: noise mix -> ne555_astable fire VCO (R44/R45/C27) -> rc_disc5(R41,C25).
- Final mix: pre-mixer (tune+bg, VOL1/VOL2 switched R49/R51/R50/R52/R34) -> resistor_mixer(R34/R40/R43, load R91) -> output ~32767/5.
Remove the approximation tuning (triangle FS, cascaded-LP hit, noise-FM fire) + the APPROXIMATION doc caveat. Keep the 10 existing device tests green. Validate end-to-end with the tools/sound-reference rig (analyze_wav.py --galaxian + spectrograms) against MAME and the recorded shot.wav/death.wav samples.
close_reason: Rewrote galaxian_sound build as a component-level port of MAME galaxian_discrete: R-1 DAC -> 555 CC wolf-whistle VCO -> 3 CV-modulated 555 astables; noise-gated op-amp band-pass HIT; noise-jittered 555 VCO + RCDISC5 FIRE; faithful two-stage resistor mix with C26/C46 coupling. Real GAL_R*/GAL_C* values. Also added op-amp rail clipping (faithful + bounds power-on transient) and out_high param to ne555_astable. 10 device tests + 34 primitive tests green.

title: Migrate Donkey Kong / Asteroids / Lunar Lander to the 555/op-amp primitives
description:
Deferred follow-up after the primitives land and Galaxian is validated. Replace the hand-rolled square-wave VCO approximations with the new first-class primitives, one separately-committable change per game, each re-validated with its existing drive_*_sound.lua + *_capture example:
- Donkey Kong (machines/src/dkong_sound.rs): vco_freq() + DkongWalk/DkongJump/DkongStomp square VCOs -> ne555_astable; per-effect 2nd-order LPs reviewed.
- Asteroids (machines/src/asteroids_sound.rs): FireChirp linear-ramp VCO -> ne555_astable/cc; thrust Q=4 band-pass -> op_amp_band_pass.
- Lunar Lander (machines/src/llander_sound.rs): high-Q thrust band-pass -> op_amp_band_pass.
Goal: drop bespoke per-game oscillator math and improve fidelity. These devices are already 'good enough', so this is lower priority and must be re-validated per game with the sound-reference rig before/after.
close_reason: Migrated all three games to the 555/op-amp primitives, each validated against an isolated MAME capture: DK walk/jump -> ne555_astable (+DAC Sallen-Key reconstruction filter); Asteroids thrust -> op_amp_band_pass, thump + ship/saucer fire -> ne555_cc; Lunar Lander thrust -> op_amp_band_pass. Bespoke vco_freq()/FireChirp phase-accumulator math removed. Also added frontend --record-wav for live gameplay capture.

title: P1: Galaxian discrete sound device
description: New core/src/device/galaxian_sound.rs Tier-1 sound path: background tone, shoot/noise, hit, lfo 'wolf-whistle'. Prefer expressing with existing core/src/device/discrete/ netlist framework. Standalone device, can be built in parallel with the video engine. If the netlist proves heavy, an interim sample/approximation keeps the Galaxian anchor unblocked (flag any shortcut in code).
close_reason: Delivered core/src/device/galaxian_sound.rs on the discrete netlist framework: background-tone (pitch note clock + QA/QC/QD taps), wolf-whistle LFO (4-bit DAC sweeping 3 gated FS oscillators), FIRE shoot (descending noisy zap), HIT (enveloped 17-bit LFSR noise through band-pass), VOL switches, passive resistor final mix. Register interface (pitch_w/lfo_freq_w/sound_w 74LS259) matches MAME galaxian_sound_device. Device/Debuggable/Saveable + 9 tests; clippy/fmt green. Flagged approximation: framework has no 555/op-amp primitives, so oscillators/envelopes/band-pass are framework primitives tuned to schematic R/C; voicing to be A/B'd against a recording when 355.3 wires it.

title: P2: Konami Scramble sound board
description: New core/src/device/konami_sound.rs: near re-skin of core/src/device/ssio.rs -- embedded Z80 + 1-2x Ay8910 + 8255 (i8255.rs) command latch + timer IRQ + AudioResampler. Standalone; build in parallel with Tier-1. Unit-test command latching in isolation (cargo test -p phosphor-core).

The Scramble-family cousins (Amidar, The End, Calipso) were never implemented — the tree registers only 'scramble' and 'scobra' on this board; the 'The End' references in scramble.rs are the protection-PAL, not the game. Closing as won't-do rather than done. Can be reopened if these per-game maps/PROMs/DIPs are pursued later.

title: Discrete sound: faithful NE555 + op-amp primitives
description:
Add first-class, reusable analog primitives to core/src/device/discrete/ (node.rs + mod.rs), ported from MAME's BSD discrete core (~/ws/mame/src/devices/sound/disc_dev.hxx, disc_flt.hxx, discrete.h):
- Ne555Astable (with CV): port dsd_555_astable. Builder ne555_astable(name, cv_src, r1, r2, c, vcc, output). Precompute exp_charge=1-exp(-dt/((r1+r2)c)), exp_discharge=exp(-dt/(r2*c)) in the builder using self.sim_rate; state cap_v + flip_flop; CV modulates threshold/trigger. Square + Capacitor output modes. Drop MAME's sub-sample x_time loop (faithful at 192kHz sim rate; documented).
- Ne555Cc (constant-current VCO): port the simple type of dsd_555_cc; output capacitor voltage.
- OpAmpBandPass: port dst_op_amp_filt IS_BAND_PASS_1M + calculate_filter2_coefficients (biquad via pre-warped bilinear transform; fc/d/gain from r_in/rF/c1/c2). Precompute a1,a2,b0,b1,b2 in the builder from self.sim_rate.
- RcDisc5: port dst_rcdisc5 (gated diode RC discharge, 0.7V drop).
Follow the 6-step NodeKind pattern (enum variant, builder, eval, reset_runtime, save_runtime/load_runtime, deps). Reuse dac_weighted for R-1 DACs and gain/add/clamp for op-amp mult/add. Add per-primitive unit tests in discrete/tests.rs (555 oscillates near FREQ_OF_555=1.49/((R1+2R2)C); band-pass peaks near fc; rc_disc5 decays with tau=RC). No behavior change to existing devices. First commit of the 555/op-amp effort. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-for-the-555-op-amp-resilient-abelson.md
close_reason: Added Ne555Astable, Ne555Cc, OpAmpBandPass, RcDisc5 NodeKind primitives (faithful ports of MAME dsd_555_astable/dsd_555_cc/dst_op_amp_filt IS_BAND_PASS_1M/dst_rcdisc5) with builder methods and 10 unit tests. No behavior change to existing devices.

title: Add gfxview: charset & sprite ROM viewer (CLI, palette from PROM)
description: Standalone 'gfxview' subcommand in the disasm tool that decodes a machine's charset/sprite GFX ROMs offline (no running machine) and exports PNG tile/sprite sheets, applying the color-PROM palette where the machine has one. Isolates GFX bit-plane layout + PROM palette correctness from the scanline renderer during machine bring-up (current target: Congo Bongo), and produces PNGs diffable against MAME GFX dumps. Reuses existing core/src/gfx (decode_gfx/GfxLayout/GfxCache), the per-machine resistor-net palette models, and the png crate. Modeled directly on the existing disasm_registry/disasm subcommand pattern. Initial coverage: Congo Bongo + Donkey Kong + Mario Bros (DK/Mario are known-good references that validate the decoder).
close_reason: gfxview delivered across 6 children (all closed): z34.1 GfxRegion inventory registry; z34.2 disasm gfxview CLI (region listing + decode + PNG sheet export, compositing later moved to phosphor_core::gfx::sheet); z34.3 DK+Mario GfxRegions (shared layout/palette extraction); z34.4 Congo Bongo fg/bg/sprites GfxRegions, validated vs real ROMs (plane order + PROM palette confirmed); z34.5 interactive SDL viewer in the frontend; z34.6 MachineCore::gfx_sheets — free --gfxview coverage for ~18 tile/sprite machines (boots the machine first so RAM-palette games color correctly). Two paths sharing one compositor: offline GfxRegion PNG export = bring-up validation (diff vs MAME dump before the renderer works); frontend --gfxview = everyday viewing from the running machine's caches. Documented exceptions: Crystal Castles (color code 0 = black) and Atari System 1 (banked/lazy GFX + per-frame RAM palette) skipped, recorded in z34.6 with how to add System 1 later. All on branch feat/gfx-registry; core+machines+frontend+disasm tests pass, clippy/fmt clean, README documents both paths.

title: gfxview CLI subcommand: region listing + decode + PNG sheet export

Add png 0.17 to tools/disasm/Cargo.toml. Unit-test gfxsheet on a synthetic GfxCache.

title: Frontend gfxview mode: interactive SDL charset/sprite viewer
description:
Interactive charset/sprite viewer in phosphor-frontend (which already owns SDL2/egui/GL), rather than adding a C dependency to the deliberately dependency-light phosphor-disasm CLI. Decided over feature-gating disasm: the frontend already has all the window/texture/event plumbing to reuse.

Scope:
- New frontend mode (subcommand or F-key/settings toggle) that renders a machine's registered GfxRegions as an on-screen tile/sprite sheet.
- Reuse gfx_registry::{regions_for,find} (z34.1) + per-machine GfxRegion layout/palette (z34.3 DK+Mario, z34.4 Congo Bongo). Decode via phosphor_core::gfx::decode_gfx.
- UX beyond the CLI's static PNG: cycle regions, select color code (offline CLI defaults to pen group 0 since tile color attrs aren't known without VRAM), zoom/scale, maybe grid overlay.

Design note — share the compositing, don't duplicate it:
- The grid-layout + integer-scale + palette-map logic currently lives in tools/disasm/src/gfxsheet.rs (render_sheet/grayscale_ramp), local to the disasm bin crate so the frontend can't import it.
- Promote that compositing (GfxCache -> RGB grid) into a shared home (e.g. phosphor_core::gfx) so BOTH the CLI PNG export and the frontend viewer use one implementation. Follow the z34.3 precedent of no-duplicated logic.

Keep disasm's PNG export as-is: dependency-light, CI/headless/cross-compile friendly, and already diffable against MAME GFX dumps.

title: gfxview: free frontend coverage via MachineCore::gfx_sheets
description:
Make --gfxview work for any working tile/sprite machine without per-machine GfxRegion registration, by reading the caches the machine already decoded.

- frontend --gfxview now runs AFTER machine construction, boots ~180 frames (so palette-RAM machines populate their palette; BurgerTime's inverted format decoded zeroed RAM to all-white otherwise), and drives gfxview::run off machine.gfx_sheets(). Compositing shared via phosphor_core::gfx::render_sheet (moved to core in the prior commit).
- gfx_sheets implemented for: dkong/mario/congobongo (references), pacman, mspacman, galaga, digdug, galaxian, pisces, mooncresta, scramble, scobra, frogger, satans_hollow, qbert, dkongjr, burgertime, foodf, gridlee, irobot. Intentionally NOT covered:
- Crystal Castles: lone sprite cache colors from palette code 0 = black (all-black at pen group 0). Left out; revisit with color-code selection.
- Atari System 1 (roadrunner, marble): does not fit the fixed-cache model — GFX is a lazily-decoded Vec<GfxBank> shared between playfield+sprites, palette is a per-frame local 1024-entry IRGB-4444 RAM snapshot (no persistent array; GfxSheet.palette is a borrow), layer-sub-banked with per-tile color from PROM lookups. To add later: relax GfxSheet.palette to Cow/owned so a snapshot can be built, then expose the alpha/text layer cleanly (playfield/MO banks remain partial/ambiguous). Decision: skip for now (per user).
