title: Headless emulation benchmark harness
description:
There are no benchmarks anywhere in the workspace: no benches/ directory, no criterion dependency, no #[bench]. The in-app profiler (frontend/src/profile.rs) is good — per-phase timings and Chrome Trace export — but it measures one interactive session and produces nothing comparable across commits.

This blocks every performance item: none of them can be justified or refuted today.

Shape: 'run N frames of machine X headless, report frames/sec and ms/frame'. phosphor-harness is SDL-free, so the bench target needs no system dependencies and can live in harness/ or machines/.

Representative boards to cover:
- pacman   — single Z80, one address space (cleanest signal)
- galaga   — 3x Z80 sharing one board (multi-CPU dispatch cost)
- tempest  — M6502 + AVG + Mathbox (vector path)
- marble   — MC68010 + M6502 sound (68000 path)
- joust    — M6809 + M6800 + blitter (two address spaces, second bus master)

ROM-gated: skip cleanly when PHOSPHOR_ROMS is unset, same convention as tools/script/tests/frameshot_parity.rs.

Acceptance: a single command that prints a stable frames/sec figure per board, repeatable within a few percent run to run.
close_reason:
Implemented in 9f0198f as the tools/bench crate (phosphor-bench). Boots via the shared Harness, runs N frames headless with no throttle, reports per-frame emulation/render/audio cost plus fps and a realtime multiple. Defaults to pacman, galaga, tempest, marble, joust. ROM-gated through roms_dir(); exits 0 with a hint when ROMs are absent.

Acceptance ('a stable frames/sec figure per board, repeatable within a few percent') met and measured, not assumed: three consecutive full runs agreed within 1.7% (pacman 0.17%, marble 1.0%, joust 1.0%, tempest 1.1%, galaga 1.7%). Getting there required changing the estimator — reporting the median repeated only within 4.3%. The workload is deterministic (no RNG, no wall clock in the tick path), so all variation is host noise and noise only adds time; the minimum is therefore both the more accurate and the more stable estimator. The trailing +/- now reports how far the slowest rep lagged, so noise is visible rather than hidden.

Baseline (release, 600 frames, 120 warmup, 5 reps):
  pacman  emul 0.823 ms/f  total 0.829  1206.6 fps  19.91x realtime
  galaga  emul 1.011 ms/f  total 1.085   921.6 fps  15.21x
  tempest emul 1.135 ms/f  total 1.183   845.2 fps  14.09x
  marble  emul 2.455 ms/f  total 3.151   317.4 fps   5.30x
  joust   emul 0.751 ms/f  total 0.757  1320.6 fps  21.97x

Notable for the epics that depend on this: emulation is ~99% of frame cost on the raster boards (render 0.006 ms/f on pacman and joust), so concrete-bus-dispatch is aimed at the right place. Marble is the outlier at 0.697 ms/f render — the playfield/motion-object priority compositor — and is the slowest board overall at 5.3x realtime.

Caveat recorded in the tool's --help: the 120-frame default warmup is far short of most machines' power-on self-test, so the default numbers measure self-test code rather than gameplay. Fine for A/B (both sides measure the same thing); raise --warmup for in-game figures.

Unblocks ci-build-foundation-xnk5.3 (release profile) and concrete-bus-dispatch-blzz.

title: Epic: Headless CPU/bus debugging & trace tooling
description:
Surface the mature interactive-debugger machinery (MachineDebug/DebugCpu/BusDebug/DebugTrace/Watchpoints) to headless workflows, plus the two small core features recurring bug hunts keep needing. Design: docs/designs/headless-debugging.md.

Verified against code: all trait surfaces, run_frameshot harness, parse_u32_auto, and the #[debug_map] derive exist as the doc describes; check_read/check_write already carry value+width so conditional watchpoints are a localized change. Instruction trace + hang detection are pure harness code (zero per-board work). Lowest-risk / highest-leverage of the three design docs; unblocks the mid-frame raster audit and directly serves the open ESB reset bug (j63p).

Phases: (1) trace harness + event/watchpoint logging [frame loop]; (2) instruction trace + break-pc [cycle loop]; (3) conditional/value-match watchpoints [only core-type change]; (4) hang/idle-loop detection; (5) interactive debugger UX + CLI polish. Phases 1-4 and 5 are independently shippable.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Atari DVG/AVG family
description: Convert the M6502 vector boards -- Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe, Lunar Lander, Quantum, Star Wars (seven bus_split! sites) -- per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Blocked by the generic Cpu::reset task (the M6502 fetches its reset vector through the bus). Measure tempest/asteroids before/after; golden frames here also pin the vector display list, so a reordered tick shows up.
close_reason:
Partially done, remainder split out.

Converted in 6cfbd9b: Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe and Lunar Lander -- the three machines that actually share AtariDvgBoard.

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  llander  0.361 -> 0.336 ms/f  -6.9%
  astdelux 0.624 -> 0.591       -5.3%
  asteroid 0.430 -> 0.422       -1.9%
Small for the usual reason: 1.512 MHz, 25,200 cycles/frame, and a large share of each frame is vector rendering and discrete-sound simulation that this change doesn't touch. Asteroids gains least -- its emulation cost is already the smallest in the bench set, and its discrete sound advances once per frame rather than per cycle.

First real 6502 users of the generic Cpu::reset (bek7): the 6502 fetches its reset vector through the bus, so these could not have been converted before it.

Shape: board + per-game view, since each game puts real I/O in front of the board (input muxes, DIPs, discrete sound, POKEY, EAROM, analog thrust pedal). Added a begin_cycle hook to AtariDvgBus for per-cycle game work -- Asteroids Deluxe clocks its POKEY there, which also let its debug_tick_pre go: the debugger's single-step now clocks the POKEY exactly as run_frame does, because both go through the same tick. No frame-loop inversion: this board has no scanline structure, only a per-cycle NMI counter.

NOT done, split out to v5gm: Quantum and Star Wars. Neither uses AtariDvgBoard -- Quantum is a standalone M68000 + AVG machine (~1200 lines, 'u32 word' bus_split arm) and Star Wars is a standalone two-6502 board (~2700 lines, seven bus_split! sites). Both need a different shape (nesting the bus state rather than a board-plus-view), and each is a conversion in its own right rather than a variation on this one. The issue's premise that this family was five M6502 machines on one board was wrong in the same way the TKG-04 issue's was.

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines; machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Galaxian (Moon Cresta, Pisces) and MCR II (Satan's Hollow)
description: Convert the two single-Z80 shared boards per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Mechanical: the Pac-Man shape applies directly. Watch for game-specific decoding that is really board behaviour (move it to the board so the board can be the bus, avoiding a view struct). Measure and run golden frames.
close_reason:
Done in beb4ef8 (galaxian + mooncresta + pisces/uniwars + satans_hollow).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  galaxian 1.517 -> 1.317 ms/f  -13.2%
  pisces   1.541 -> 1.378       -10.6%
  mooncrst 1.528 -> 1.376        -9.9%
  shollow  3.408 -> 3.266        -4.2%

Satan's Hollow gains least for the usual reason: 2.496 MHz, a heavy compositor, and an SSIO sound board whose Z80 runs *inside the device* rather than through this bus -- so comparatively little of its frame is main-bus dispatch.

Shapes: both boards became the bus outright. GalaxianBoard serves Galaxian, Moon Cresta and UniWar S unchanged (they differ only in the map-layout flag and GFX-bank mode the board already carries); Mcr2Board serves Satan's Hollow, its only machine. Three system-level 'impl Bus' blocks deleted outright.

Pisces was the one exception: it re-wires 0x6002 (GFX bank instead of coin lockout), so it keeps a newtype view. Deliberately not folded into bus_write_common -- that would charge every other Galaxian game a comparison on every write.

Useful measurement fell out of that pairing: pisces (newtype view) and mooncrst (board direct) land within 0.002 ms/f of each other on identical hardware. So a single-pointer view hoisted out of the loop costs nothing; the Galaga regression was specifically about multi-pointer views rebuilt per cycle. Recorded in the design doc.

Also inverted both frame loops (Galaxian: starfield advance + line render + VBLANK NMI; MCR II: the CTC's two scanline-triggered channels), renamed GalaxianBoard::check_interrupts to interrupt_state, and preserved save-state layout (both boards wrote their CPU first).

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines (galaxian, mooncrst, pisces, uniwars, shollow); machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

26 files still reference bus_split!.

title: Inlinable fast path for backed-memory bus reads
description:
Now that converted boards dispatch to a concrete bus, the remaining per-access cost is the work inside bus_read_common/bus_write_common: a page lookup, a watchpoint check and a trace-enabled check on every access. Those functions are too large to inline, so each access is still a direct call with the register pressure that implies -- the Pac-Man codegen shows 29 call sites to bus_read_common in one Z80 cycle instantiation.

Idea: an #[inline] fast path for the common case (address lands in a backed ReadWrite/ReadOnly region, no watchpoints armed, tracing off) that reads the backing store directly, falling out to the existing function for I/O, unmapped addresses, and any debug observability. A trait object could never inline this; a concrete bus can.

Measure with phosphor-bench on pacman and galaga (both converted). Verify golden frames -- a fast path that skips a watchpoint check when one IS armed would be a silent debugger regression, so the fallback condition needs a test.

Depends on concrete bus dispatch reaching the boards being measured.

title: Debugger shows a stale image for machines that render in run_frame
description:
Machines that render once at the end of run_frame into a cached framebuffer (rather than per-scanline during tick()) show a frozen image while running under the debugger. The debugger advances the machine via MachineDebug::debug_tick() (frontend/src/debug_ui.rs execute_frame), which calls the board's tick() but never run_frame(), so the cached framebuffer is not refreshed. The frontend still copies that stale framebuffer via render_frame().

Affects Continue-in-debug, the new Step Frame, and frame breakpoints. Known-affected machines: Burgertime (machines/src/burgertime.rs run_frame calls board.render() after the tick loop), Dig Dug, and likely other render-in-run_frame machines. Per-scanline renderers (Williams/Joust, Missile Command, Gridlee, ...) update correctly because their scanline buffer is written during tick().

Note: CPU register / memory / device inspection and all breakpoints work correctly; only the displayed picture is stale.

Fix options: (a) have affected boards render at frame boundaries inside tick() (e.g. when clock crosses cycles_per_frame) so both run_frame and debug_tick refresh the framebuffer, removing the redundant explicit render() in run_frame; or (b) add a way for the debug path to request a render once per completed frame. Option (a) is localized per machine and keeps a single render site.

Audit all machines for the render-in-run_frame pattern when fixing.
close_reason: Fixed by Phase 1 (commit e9380a3) and confirmed by pjl in the real frontend debugger. Machines that cached a render in run_frame now render at a frame-boundary hook shared by run_frame and debug_tick, so the picture stays live under Continue-in-debug, Step Frame, and frame breakpoints. Audited all machines for the render-in-run_frame pattern as the issue asked: exactly six were affected (galaga, xevious, digdug, burgertime, qbert, shollow); mrdo, foodf, marble and roadrunner render on demand from live state and were never stale. Took fix option (a) — render at frame boundaries inside the tick path, single render site, redundant run_frame render removed. Output byte-identical (frameshot 12/12) and guarded by the ROM-gated acceptance test debug_tick_advances_picture_like_run_frame.

title: Tempest's headless render_frame double-applies ROT270
description:
Captured while pinning golden frames (phosphor-emulator-frame-regression-w1pi.2). harness/tests/golden/tempest.png shows every string running bottom-to-top: the picture is 90 degrees off upright.

AtariAvgBoard::render_frame calls rasterize_vectors(.., flip_y = false), and that branch is documented as 'ROT270: Y already maps to screen-Y directly' — i.e. the rasterised buffer is already in screen space. Every caller of render_frame then applies the machine's declared orientation centrally (Orientation::ROT270 for TempestSystem), which rotates it a second time.

The frontend does not hit this: for vector machines it feeds vector_display_list to GL, and the shader's 'rotation == 270' branch only negates Y (frontend/src/vector_gl.rs) rather than rotating, so the live game looks right. The two paths therefore disagree, and the disagreement is invisible to frameshot_parity.rs because both of its sides go through render_frame.

Affects: disasm frameshot, phosphor-script screenshot, the debug UI's texture fallback, and the golden frame pinned for tempest.

Fix needs a decision on where the AVG's screen mapping belongs — in rasterize_vectors, in the declared orientation, or in the GL shader — and the three should then agree. The golden hash for tempest must be recaptured with the fix.

title: ESB: mid-game watchdog reset (~19s) from RAM buffer overrun into the stack
description:
Empire Strikes Back (esb) boots and plays, but ~19s into an actual game (start a game, e.g. Free Play + fire) the main CPU derails and the watchdog resets the board.

Reproduced headless at ~frame 934 (deterministic, input-independent). The boot-check does not catch it because a reboot still yields a stable non-empty vector list.

Failure mechanism (traced instruction-by-instruction):
- Bank-2 ROM code (~0xea00-0xed00) runs a RAM write loop with X in the MathRamLo region ($4800-$4FFF), around 0x4829.
- The write overruns into the CPU stack (S ~ 0x4fed, same $4800 region) and clobbers a stacked return address with 0x4e5f.
- A later RTS at 0x91c1 pops 0x4e5f and jumps into RAM -> garbage -> watchdog reset. (RTS/6809 are correct; they faithfully return the corrupted value.)

Ruled out:
- Not the 6809 / shared board logic (base Star Wars is unaffected).
- Not the slapstic alt/bitwise sequences (direct-banking-only reproduces identically).
- Not a bank-switch-mid-loop (slapstic bank stable at 1, bit4/bank2 at entry 0 throughout).
- Not input-driven (occurs with zero yoke input).
- Bank/ROM layout is byte-correct (CRC-validated load; interleaving matches MAME esb image).

Leading suspect: the overrun length/pointer derives from a value that is wrong only on ESB. Since ROM content and banking check out and the CPU is fine, the most ESB-specific compute path is the Matrix Processor running ESB's distinct mathbox PROMs (136031-107..110); a value it produces (read from $5000) may be feeding the bad write count/pointer.

Repro (headless): create the esb machine, set dsw1=0x00 (Free Play), press fire ~frame 100, run ~1000 frames; watch board.clock restart (watchdog) or cpu.pc return to the ~0xEExx boot entry.

Next step: disassemble the 0xea00-0xed00 write loop and trace the count/pointer back to its source (matrix output vs. a banked table).
notes:
2026-08-08 (see j63p.1 for the full trace): the "RAM buffer overrun into the
stack" framing in this issue's title/description is WRONG and should be retired.

There is no overrun. The failure is a cross-bank return landing in the wrong
slapstic bank: bank2:$9171 JSR $8295 -> bank1:$8298 -> bank1:$829B `JMP $8090`
(stay in bank 1) instead of bank2:$829B `JMP $80A0` (return to bank 2), so
execution resumes mid-routine at bank1:$9174 holding bank 2's X. The $4E5F that
the RTS at $91C1 pops is a stale-but-legitimate object pointer, not a clobbered
return address.

Also retire the leading suspect recorded here: it is not the mathbox. The
Matrix Processor output is not involved in the diverging path, and the ESB
mathbox PROMs were already confirmed to load in MAME order.

Our slapstic device model is byte-for-byte equivalent to MAME's for chip 101,
so the remaining suspect is the ADDRESS STREAM the M6809 presents to it -
specifically don't-care/VMA cycles. Next steps in j63p.1.
close_reason: Fixed in c08770a: M6809 don't-care cycles now drive the bus, so the ESB slapstic alt-banking sequence completes. Verified no derail over 4000 frames and zero watchdog expiries over 6000 frames of gameplay.

title: j63p: interrupt recognised one instruction late (frame 55, cycle 2045954)
description:
Investigation notes for j63p. Superseded the earlier "corrupting write" reading:
the derail is a WRONG-SLAPSTIC-BANK RETURN, not stack corruption.

REPRODUCTION (no source patch needed; DIPs are now exposed):
  disasm trace --machine esb --dip 'Coinage=Free Play' --press fire1@300:16 \
    --break-pc 0:0x4E5F --frames 3000 <roms>
  -> stops on --break-pc at frame 1129, cycle 41649243. Deterministic.
  Works from any --from-frame now that the cycle loop applies scheduled presses.
  Rhai equivalent: set_dip("Coinage","Free Play"); run_frames; step() + pc(0).

MECHANISM (traced instruction-by-instruction, frame 1129):
1. bank2:$9171 `JSR $8295` is a cross-bank trampoline. bank2:$8295 = `JSR $8090`;
   the opcode fetch at $8090 is a slapstic DIRECT bank select to bank 1, so the
   RTS at $8093 returns to $8298 read from bank 1.
2. Each bank carries its own copy of the return trampoline, and they differ:
     bank 1 $829B = `JMP $8090`  (stay in bank 1)
     bank 2 $829B = `JMP $80A0`  (return to bank 2)
   We execute bank 1's copy, so we never come back to bank 2.
3. Execution resumes at bank1:$9174 (`STA 6,X`) - the MIDDLE of bank 1's
   $9168 routine - carrying bank 2's X = $91C5, a ROM byte-table pointer that
   bank2:$91B1 `LDX #$91C3` / `ABX` had legitimately loaded.
4. That runs bank 1's $9156/$915E rotate chain, whose `RTS` at $91C1 (S=$4FED)
   pops a stale word - $4E5F - and jumps into RAM. Watchdog resets the board.

CORRECTIONS to the earlier notes:
- X = $4E5F is NOT garbage. It is a legitimate live object pointer in CPU RAM
  ($4800-$4FFF is plain RAM in MAME's map too), pushed and popped correctly
  many times per frame (10+ times over frames 1117-1129 with no derail). The
  PSHS at $9125/$B4CA are innocent.
- There is no RAM write-loop overrun into the stack. Conditional watchpoints
  on $4FED/$4FEE (=4E/=5F) show only ordinary PSHS traffic.
- "Slapstic bank stable at 1" was an artifact of looking at too small a window.
  The bank moves constantly: 1<->3 alternation early, with bank 2 appearing
  from frame 1025 on. First bank-2 entry is frame 1025 cyc 37801889.

RULED OUT (this pass):
- The slapstic DEVICE MODEL. Every chip-101 constant (bankstart 3; bank selects
  0080/0090/00A0/00B0; alt 1f00/1e00, 1fff/1fff, 1ffc/1b5c, 1fcf/0080, shift 0;
  bitwise 1ff0/1540 ... 1ff8/1550), the geometry (0x8000-0x9FFF, 8-bit bus,
  13 decoded lines -> shift 0), and all five state handlers are equivalent to
  MAME's atari_slapstic_device (src/mame/atari/slapstic.cpp). Idle, active_101_102
  and alt_valid_101_102 were compared line-by-line; test_in/test_any/test_bank/
  test_reset/test_inside build identical masks.
- Feeding the chip every CPU address (not just window accesses) is correct -
  MAME installs its tap over the whole address space too.
- The alt sequence being unreachable. It IS reachable: alt_valid needs
  (addr & 0x1FFF) == 0x1FFF outside the window, and $BFFF is executed from
  7 times in the run, most recently frame 1129 cyc 41647541 - 1700 cycles
  before the derail.

NEXT STEP: the divergence is in the ADDRESS STREAM fed to the chip, not the
chip. Two concrete leads, in order:
1. Instrument slapstic STATE transitions (not just committed bank changes) and
   check whether an alt/bitwise sequence is being started or broken at a
   different point than on hardware - especially around the $BFFF access at
   cyc 41647541 and the $9E00-$9EFF fetches (which match alt_start,
   test_in 0x1F00/0x1E00) at cyc 41648848-41648855.
2. Audit our M6809's bus cycles against MAME's for don't-care/VMA behaviour.
   Ours drives no address on don't-care cycles (the only $FFFF read left is the
   reset vector, mod.rs:618) after the TST fix in 9706bbc. Chip 101's alt step 2
   is documented as landing outside the window "in practice a 6809 dummy VMA
   access", so a missing or extra dummy access shifts the state machine by one.

TOOLING SHIPPED THIS PASS (all were blocking or actively misleading):
- StarWars/ESB DIP banks exposed (DSW0 is variant-specific, DSW1 shared), so
  Free Play no longer needs a source patch. `--dip` on `disasm trace`.
- `disasm trace` stop conditions now report where and why the run ended. They
  used to stop silently while the summary still advertised the full frame
  range, which reads exactly like "never fired" - this cost hours.
- The cycle loop now applies scheduled `--press`/`--move` edges (Harness gained
  apply_scheduled_input/advance_frame). Previously any press aimed past
  --from-frame was silently dropped in --cpu/--break-pc mode.
- starwars now emits debug events at all: slapstic BankSwitch (with the address
  that tipped it), LS259 bit-4 bank line, and watchdog pet/expire.
- StarWarsSystem::debug_pre_tick services the pending sound-CPU reset, which
  run_frame did and debug_tick did not - the machine behaved differently under
  the debugger than at full speed.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — see phosphor-emulator-vy6l. The M6809 does not drive $FFFF on don't-care/VMA cycles, so ESB's slapstic alt-banking sequence can never complete its 'valid' step, the game never reaches bank 2 by that path, and the cross-bank return lands in bank 1 where $9174 is 'STA 6,X' instead of bank 2's 'RTS'. Established by tracing MAME 0.287 in actual gameplay (Lua harness; the notifier subscription must be stored in a global or it is garbage-collected) and finding it executes bank 1's $829B then bank 2's $9174 — a 1->2 bank change with no access to $80A0, which only the alt sequence can produce. j63p is now blocked on vy6l.
close_reason: Investigation complete; j63p fixed in c08770a. Notes retain the full path, including three wrong root-cause claims and the two tooling bugs that caused them.

title: phosphor-disasm tests do not compile: run_trace() call sites are one argument short
description:
Pre-existing on main (confirmed by stashing unrelated work and rebuilding), not
caused by any current change — noticed while running `cargo test --workspace`
for phosphor-emulator-vy6l.

`cargo test -p phosphor-disasm` fails to build with 8 x E0061: `run_trace` takes
19 arguments, the test call sites in tools/disasm/src/trace.rs (~line 1585
onwards) supply 18. Argument #13, `Option<&str>`, is missing — a parameter was
added to `run_trace` without updating its own test module.

`cargo build` is unaffected, which is why it went unnoticed: only the test
target breaks. Consequence is that the whole phosphor-disasm test suite has
been silently not running.
close_reason: Fixed in two commits. (1) The 8 run_trace call sites in trace::tests were missing the entropy_file argument added by e4d39d9; passing None at each restores the build and all 42 disasm tests pass, with no pre-existing failures hiding behind the break. (2) Removed the root cause: run_trace now takes a named TraceOptions struct (Default + new(machine, path)) instead of 19 positional args, so a future parameter cannot silently shift or omit an argument at a call site. Verified cargo test --workspace --no-run builds every target; clippy and fmt clean.

title: M6809 TST memory ops: dummy VMA cycle disagrees with test vectors, aborting the validation suite
description:
`cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation` fails on the very first M6809 mismatch and, because `test_all_opcodes` panics on first failure, every opcode after 0x0D goes unchecked. Pre-existing on main; found while verifying the DRY 1 macro refactor (phosphor-emulator-dry-refactors-0lhx.1), which is not the cause.

SYMPTOM
  m6809_single_step_test: `0d 4b: cycle 5 (bus 3) addr  left: 65535  right: 59211`
  (0xFFFF vs 0xE74B, the DP:addr effective address)

SCOPE — all 3000 cases of the three TST memory forms fail, and only these:
  test_data/m6809/0d.json  1000/1000  TST direct    (bus3 addr/data/op)
  test_data/m6809/6d.json  1000/1000  TST indexed   (bus3 addr/data/op)
  test_data/m6809/7d.json  1000/1000  TST extended  (bus4 addr/data/op)
  The other 263 opcode files pass 1000/1000.

CAUSE
TST shares RMW timing but must not write back, so `rmw_direct`/`rmw_indexed`/`rmw_extended` in core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs special-case it into a dummy read at 0xFFFF (see rmw_direct cycle 4, core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs:650-659). The checked-in vectors still encode the older behaviour — a read of the effective address on that cycle. Vectors are self-generated (cpu-validation/src/bin/gen_m6809_tests.rs drives our own M6809), so they went stale when the dummy-cycle address changed and were never regenerated.

WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT
The stale vectors PASS cross-validation against the reference emulator (0d 1000/1000, 7d 1000/1000, 6d 998/1000), i.e. the reference also re-reads the EA on that cycle. On real hardware a /VMA cycle drives 0xFFFF on the address bus, so the current emulator matches the datasheet and the reference does not. Per CLAUDE.md (\"if cross-validation differs from datasheet for timings, use the datasheet values\") the emulator behaviour looks correct and the vectors should be regenerated — but confirm against the 6809 datasheet cycle-by-cycle table before regenerating, since this permanently forks these three opcodes from the reference.

SUGGESTED FIX
1. Confirm the datasheet lists the final TST cycle as VMA/0xFFFF.
2. Regenerate: cargo run -p phosphor-cpu-validation --bin gen_m6809_tests -- all (or just 0d/6d/7d).
3. Re-run cross-validation and record the expected 0d/6d/7d divergence so it is not mistaken for a regression later.
4. Consider whether the dummy cycle should be emitted as BusOp::Internal rather than a real read, so the vector format distinguishes VMA cycles from genuine bus reads.

ALSO WORTH FIXING
`test_all_opcodes` aborting on the first bad case hides all later coverage. Collecting failures and reporting a per-opcode summary would have caught this being masked.
notes:
CORRECTION to the original report: the M6809 vectors are NOT checked in.
.gitignore line 3 ignores cpu-validation/test_data/, so test_data/m6809/*.json
are locally-generated artifacts (the test panics with a 'run gen_m6809_tests'
message if the directory is absent). The stale vectors were therefore a stale
LOCAL working copy predating the TST dummy-cycle change, not committed data --
a fresh checkout regenerating from scratch would have passed on main.

That does not change the fix, which stands on its own merits:
  - the three TST /VMA cycles were the only don't-care cycles in the M6809 that
    drove a real bus transaction, and that inconsistency is now gone;
  - the datasheet confirmation above is unaffected;
  - the test-harness summary and the README corrections are unaffected.

It does mean nothing needs committing under cpu-validation/test_data/.
close_reason:
Confirmed against the MC6809E datasheet and fixed.

DATASHEET CONFIRMATION (step 1)
Figure 17, Cycle-by-Cycle Performance, sheet 5 of 5 lists the two groups side
by side:
  ASL/ASR/CLR/COM/DEC/INC/LSL/LSR/NEG/ROL/ROR (all except immediate):
    Data(EA) / Don't Care(FFFF) / Data Write(EA)
  TST (all except immediate):
    Data(EA) / Don't Care(FFFF) / Don't Care(FFFF)
So TST's final cycle is a don't-care /VMA cycle, not a store and not an EA
re-read. The emulator was right; the vectors were stale.
Table 9 also confirms the counts: 0D=6, 6D=6+, 7D=7 -- unchanged.

FIX
- core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs: the three TST special cases in rmw_direct /
  rmw_indexed / rmw_extended now emit a true internal cycle instead of
  'bus.read(master, 0xFFFF)'. This resolves step 4 of the issue: they were the
  only three /VMA cycles in the whole M6809 that drove a real bus transaction,
  so a dummy read could disturb memory-mapped I/O at 0xFFFF while every other
  don't-care cycle stayed silent. The vector format now distinguishes them as
  "internal". Cycle counts are unchanged.
- Regenerated 0d/6d/7d vectors (step 2). cargo test -p phosphor-cpu-validation
  passes; full workspace test, clippy and fmt are clean.

CROSS-VALIDATION (step 3) -- no fork, contrary to the issue's expectation
The concern about permanently forking these three opcodes from the reference
does not apply: the cross-validator does not compare bus traces at all (it
checks registers, final memory at accessed addresses, and total cycle count),
and the cycle count is identical either way. Post-fix numbers are exactly the
pre-existing baseline: 0d 1000/1000, 7d 1000/1000, 6d 998/1000.

The residual 6d 2/1000 is NOT TST-related. A full sweep gives 264,090/266,000
with 53 indexed opcodes failing, all one cause: postbyte 0x9F ([n] extended
indirect), where the datasheet's Table 2 says +5 cycles and the reference core
charges +8. Datasheet wins, so phosphor is correct. Filed as
phosphor-emulator-oyxg and documented in cpu-validation/README_m6809.md.

ALSO FIXED
- cpu-validation/tests/m6809_single_step_test.rs now collects failures and
  panics with a per-opcode summary (counts + up to 3 example cases) instead of
  aborting on the first bad assertion. This immediately showed the failure was
  confined to 0d/6d/7d with the other 263 opcodes passing.
- cpu-validation/README_m6809.md: recorded the known [n] divergence and the TST
  bus-trace note, and corrected two stale claims -- it advertised
  '266,000/266,000 (100%)' and credited elmerucr/MC6809, but the validator
  actually compiles mame0148/src/emu/cpu/m6809/m6809.c.

title: Marble Madness (Atari System 1)
description:
Add Marble Madness (1984), the project's first 16-bit multi-CPU arcade machine, on the Atari System 1 board (MC68010 main @ 7.15909 MHz + M6502 sound @ 1.789772 MHz).

Builds on the new M68000 core (first exercised by machines/src/foodf.rs, the closest end-to-end template). System 1 is the gateway to four more titles (Peter Packrat, Indiana Jones, Road Runner, RoadBlasters) that share this board.

User-chosen scope for this first cut:
- Audio: boot-first - POKEY only (reuse core/src/device/pokey.rs); YM2151 STUBBED (silent, but registers/IRQ wired so the sound CPU runs). Full FM synthesis is a tracked follow-up.
- Video: correct-but-staged - build the full alpha + playfield + motion-object compositor and palette first, then iterate the trickier PROM 4/5/6-bpp banking and SLIP scanline IRQs against MAME.

New components: Slapstic 137412-103 device, EEPROM 2804 (via Nvram), YM2151 stub, System 1 video (banked tilemaps + atarimo linked-list MO engine), machines/src/marble.rs.

Hardware verified against MAME atari/atarisy1.cpp, atarisy1_v.cpp, slapstic.cpp, atarimo.*.

Full plan: ~/.claude/plans/plan-for-marble-madness-goofy-rainbow.md
close_reason: done

title: P0: 68010 fidelity check (exception frame / VBR)
description:
Confirm the existing M68000 core with M68kVariant::M68010 is sufficient for Marble Madness before building on it. Risks: 68010 pushes an extra format/vector word on exception frames and has a VBR; MOVE from SR is privileged. Marble runs supervisor-mode with vectors at 0, so it almost certainly runs as-is.

Verify by reading core/src/cpu/m68000/exception.rs frame-build and confirming RTE/exception entry use a matching frame format. If a 68010 frame is needed, add it behind the existing variant gate.

Deliverable: a note plus any small gated frame fix - no behavior change expected. Cheap, do first.
close_reason: 68010 fidelity confirmed and gated. Implemented behind M68kVariant::M68010: the format $0 exception frame (vector-offset word + RTE consumption) and privileged MOVE from SR. Verified the M68000 path is byte-for-byte unchanged (full cpu-validation incl. SingleStepTests passes; new 68010 tests added). Documented the deferred 68010 deltas (VBR, MOVEC/MOVES/RTD, MOVE from CCR, format $8 fault frame) in the README for Phase 1 to watch. 3 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity.

title: Follow-up: real YM2151 FM synthesis core
description: Replace the YM2151 stub (core/src/device/ym2151.rs) with a real FM synthesis core, restoring Marble Madness music/SFX. The single largest follow-up; the stub keeps the sound CPU alive so the rest of the machine is testable meanwhile. Drops in behind the same register/IRQ API established in P4.
close_reason: Real YM2151 (OPM) FM synthesis done. Replaced the timer/IRQ stub with a faithful integer port of the OPM synthesis path from MAME's ymfm reference core (no SSG-EG/depress/reverb/rhythm): die-extracted log-sine/exponent/EG-increment/detune/phase-step tables generated verbatim from ymfm; per-operator phase generator (key-code->phase-step, detune-1/2, MUL, LFO PM), envelope generator (KS-scaled AR/D1R/D2R/RR, D1L sustain, EG-counter divider + attack/decay curves), the 8 channel algorithms with op-1 self-feedback, LFO (saw/square/triangle/noise AM+PM) and the ch-7 noise operator, 8-channel per-sample mix at the native FM rate (clock/64) resampled on drain. Wired into the sound board: POKEY (unipolar) + YM (bipolar) summed, one-pole DC blocker (~35Hz) before i16 output, tunable FM mix gain. Verified vs MAME: identical register stream, attract FM-silent in both (game primes frequencies but keys no notes 40s+), music keys notes once a game starts. Address/data/status ports + A/B timers preserved. Synthesis + timer unit tests; cargo fmt + clippy --all-features --all-targets clean. User confirmed in-game music sounds correct. 3 commits on marble-68010-fidelity.

title: P1: Machine skeleton + main CPU boots
description:
Create machines/src/marble.rs; add mod marble; to machines/src/lib.rs.

- Region enum + build_map() (AddressSpace32): Program ROM (000000-07FFFF), Slapstic ROM window (080000-087FFF), Work RAM (400000), Playfield/MO/Alpha RAM (A00000-A03FFF), Palette RAM (B00000).
- ROM manifest (RomRegion/RomEntry) from the MAME 'marble' set: even/odd interleaved program ROMs, banked ROM, alpha/PF/MO GFX ROMs, two GFX-select PROMs. Pull exact filenames/sizes/CRCs from ROM_START(marble) in atarisy1.cpp.
- M68000::new() with variant=M68010; tick() cycle loop and reset() via bus_split! (mirror foodf). Wire watchdog (8-VBLANK) and 8A0000 VBLANK-ack.
- Bus read/write dispatch for ROM/RAM/EEPROM/control regs; stub video RAM as plain memory.
- Register via inventory::submit! { MachineEntry::new("marble", &["marble"], create_machine) }; add DisasmRegion entries (M68000 main, M6502 sound).

Verify: unit tests for map decode + reset-from-vectors (mirror foodf tests); a boot-check example runs N frames without panicking and the CPU leaves the reset vector.
close_reason: Machine skeleton boots. machines/src/marble.rs: AddressSpace32 map (program ROM, slapstic window as plain ROM, work/cart/playfield/MO/alpha/palette RAM); ROM manifest from the MAME 'marble' set (motherboard BIOS holding the reset vectors at 0x000000 + 4 even/odd cartridge banks + slapstic chips, de-interleaved); M68000 core in M68010 mode with bus_split tick/reset; VBLANK IRQ4 + 8-VBLANK watchdog; control/IO dispatch (scroll/priority/bankselect latches, F60000 switch port with live VBLANK bit, stubbed EEPROM/trackball/ADC/sound); registered as 'marble'; disasm regions for 68010 main + M6502 sound. 13 unit tests incl. map decode, reset-from-BIOS-vectors, and a synthetic 68010 program that boots + services VBLANK IRQ (RTE through the Phase-0 frame). Plus a headless marble_boot_check example. Full workspace builds; all 411 phosphor-machines tests pass. 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. NOTE: GFX/PROM ROM manifest + decode deferred to Phase 3 (3a/3b/3c) where they are consumed and CRC-verified; Slapstic/EEPROM to Phase 2; sound CPU to Phase 4; trackball/coins to Phase 5 - all stubbed with TODO markers.

Alpha font ROM (136032.104.f5) added to the manifest and decoded as 512 8x8 2bpp tiles via the anlayout layout. Full-frame compositor renders the 64x32 alpha tilemap 1:1 from the screen origin: per pixel code=data&0x3FF, color=(data>>10)&7, opaque=data&0x2000; composites palette[color*4+pen]; pen 0 transparent unless the cell forces layer 0 (black background until Phase 3b playfield). 4 new tests (IRGB conversion vs MAME values, opaque-cell compositing, transparent-pen-0 black). marble_boot_check example extended with lit/distinct-colour stats + ASCII thumbnail per the verify step. All 417 phosphor-machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean. 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. title: P3b: Video - playfield tilemap + PROM GFX decode
description:
64x64 playfield tilemap with X/Y scroll (800000/820000). Implement the PROM-driven GFX decode (decode_gfx in atarisy1_v.cpp: PROM1/PROM2 -> bank, bpp 4/5/6, color, offset) and the runtime tile-bank select from 860000. Start with a single bank / fixed bpp, then generalize.

Least-standard part of the video; bring up incrementally against MAME, expect iteration.

Verify: playfield matches MAME attract-mode frames.
close_reason: Playfield + PROM GFX decode done. tiles (0x100000) + graphics PROMs (0x400) added to the manifest; tiles region handled as ROMREGION_INVERT|ROMREGION_ERASEFF by inverting the whole zero-filled buffer. build_playfield_gfx/get_pf_bank port MAME decode_gfx+get_bank: each of 256 remap entries -> tile bank (1-7), bpp (4/5/6), color, offset; banks decoded on demand at their bpp (planes 0x10000 apart, reversed to LSB-first). render: 64x64 playfield as opaque background with X/Y scroll (800000/820000), lookup ((data>>8)&0x7f | tile_bank<<7), code=(offset<<8)|(data&0xff), palette[0x100 + palcolor*2^bpp + pen]; alpha overlays on top; tile bank from 860001 bit 2. 3 new tests (PROM lookup decode, bpp select + unmapped remap, playfield pixel composites under alpha). All 420 phosphor-machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean. 1 commit on branch marble-68010-fidelity. CAVEATS (issue flagged iteration expected): visual attract-mode comparison vs MAME not done - marble ROM set not on this machine. The scroll sign/offset convention (src = screen + scroll) and bank2's missing-4th-plane edge case are the most likely things to need adjustment once ROMs are available.

Verify: marbles/sprites render and composite correctly vs MAME.
close_reason: Motion objects + priority/translucency done. PROM decode builds a sprite remap lookup (proms +0x100/+0x300, MO colour mask) sharing the playfield tile banks; render_motion_objects walks the active bank's linked list (split 4-word entries, timer entries skipped) and rasterises each sprite (h-flip, transparent pen 0, yscroll 256, 512x512 wrap) into a palette-index buffer merged over the playfield: high-priority pens blend through the translucent bank (0x300+pf<<4+mo), low-priority pens draw unless the playfield pixel is a colour-0 priority pen (0x840000 mask). Also fixed the tile ROM to true ROMREGION_ERASEFF (load_erased(0xFF)+invert) so bank 2's absent plane 3 reads 0 — without it sprites rendered all black (pen bit 3 forced). render() refactored to index-based compositing first. Verified vs MAME (palette/PF/sprite pens); attract sprites now render in colour. 3 commits on marble-68010-fidelity. Follow-up: SLIP/IRQ3 (iv0.7).

title: P3d: Video - SLIP / IRQ3 scanline motion-object interrupts
description:
Scanline-position motion-object interrupts (the int3_callback timer) and the 2E0000 sprite-interrupt-state read (bit 7). Add once static rendering is correct.

SLIP timing affects both visuals and game logic; verify cadence against MAME traces.
close_reason: SLIP / IRQ3 scanline motion-object interrupts done. A motion-object timer entry (0xFFFF in word[1]) asserts IRQ3 for the one scanline at the top of its band (ypos = 256 - (word0>>5) - vsize*8 - 1, per MAME update_timers), recomputed each scanline boundary from the active sprite bank; drives the IRQ3 line (priority below IRQ4/IRQ6) and the 0x2E0000 status read bit 7 (was stubbed 0). State-saved; unit test covers the firing scanline + status/level wiring. Verified vs MAME: SLIP is negligible in attract (MAME fires it 2x at boot frame 6 then never; VBLANK ~1/frame). Our attract writes no timer entries so IRQ3 stays idle there — mechanism matches MAME's algorithm for gameplay and is unit-tested. 1 commit on marble-68010-fidelity. Note: the 2 MAME boot-frame-6 firings aren't replicated (boot-state timing diverges via the EEPROM/sound path); not a SLIP bug.

title: P4: Sound CPU (M6502) + inter-CPU comms, YM2151 stubbed
description:
Add M6502 sound CPU with its own AddressSpace16 map and a Bresenham ClockDivider (1.789772 vs 7.15909 MHz ~= 1/4) like machines/src/tkg04.rs.

Latches: main FE0000 write -> sound NMI (command); sound 1810 write -> main IRQ6 (response); FC0000/1810 reads; status bits at 1820/F60000 (buffer-full flags); 860000 bit drives sound-CPU reset.

POKEY at 1870-187F (reuse Pokey), mixed to stereo in run_frame. YM2151 stub (core/src/device/ym2151.rs) at 1800-1801: accept register writes, return not-busy status, raise the IRQ line on its timers so the 6502 IRQ handler executes - but emit silence from drain_audio. Structured so the real FM core drops in behind the same API.

Verify: command/response handshake in a unit test (write command -> NMI taken -> response latched -> main IRQ6). POKEY audio path produces output without underruns.
close_reason: Sound CPU done — and it unblocks boot. core/src/device/ym2151.rs: timer/IRQ stub (timer A/B overflow -> status flag -> IRQ; register writes stored; silent audio; 6 tests). machines/src/marble_sound.rs: MarbleSound = M6502 @ 1.789772 MHz with its own Bus<u16> (RAM/ROM/YM2151/POKEY/output-latch), inter-CPU latches (main FE0000->sound NMI command; sound 1810->main IRQ6 response; FC0000/1810 reads; F60000/1820 buffer flags; 860001 bit7 = sound reset, held at power-on until released), driven at 1/4 main via ClockDivider; POKEY mixed in run_frame, YM silent; IRQ6 in the main interrupt priority; save/load; 4 tests incl. the full command->NMI->response->IRQ6 handshake. VERIFIED against the real ROM set (~/ws/mame-runtime/roms/marble.zip): marble now boots through self-test — the EEPROM self-initialises (195 byte writes), the sound CPU runs once released, and the frame renders attract content (alpha HUD text + playfield visibly working, 1379 lit px / 20 colours). All 805 core+machines tests pass; clippy/fmt clean; 2 commits on branch marble-68010-fidelity. Follow-up iv0.10 (real YM2151 FM) remains; exact attract-mode pixel match vs MAME (scroll sign, bank-2 plane, MO) is Phase 3c/polish.

title: Epic: Mid-frame raster fidelity
description:
Correctness: several machines render the whole frame once from final video state, losing mid-frame palette/scroll/bank/flip changes. Decide which machines actually need per-scanline rendering by MEASUREMENT (via the headless trace tool), migrate the ones that do, and cheaply fix the rest. Subsumes the ifs0 debugger-stale-image bug for every machine it touches. Design: ~/mid-frame-raster-fidelity.md.

Verified against code: per-scanline vs render-once split is real and broad; galaga run_frame is the render-once pattern; atari_system1 already records per-scanline mo_bank_changes while compositing once (proof at least one machine needs this today); mcr2/atari_system1 use indexed+priority buffers. Main correctness risk (doc-flagged): must NOT re-sample vblank-latched state (galaga starfield) per scanline.

Depends on: Epic headless-debugging (Phase 0 audit uses the trace tool) and Epic graphics-consolidation (Tier A migrations use the enriched 2a / indexed 2b scanline helpers). Sequence LAST of the three.

Phases: (0) trace-based Tier A/B audit; (1) Tier B frame-boundary fix [closes ifs0, zero output change]; (2) Tier A non-priority per-scanline; (3) Tier A priority-compositing [after graphics 2b].
close_reason:
Epic complete. Goal was: decide by MEASUREMENT which machines need per-scanline rendering, migrate those that do, cheaply fix the rest.

Decided (Phase 0): all 37 registered machines classified; evidence in docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md. Of 10 render-once boards, 9 measured Tier B; the one Tier A case (atari_system1 via Road Runner's mid-frame MO-bank switch) already implements per-scanline band rendering and pjl verified it renders correctly. Per-scanline boards (williams/namco_pac/tkg04/mario_bros/congo_bongo/galaxian_video + gridlee/ccastles/missile/irobot) were already mid-frame-correct; DVG/AVG vector games (incl. esb, which runs on Star Wars hardware) are not raster.

Migrated (Phases 2/3): nothing needed — both closed as not-needed, with reasons. The audit's whole point was to avoid needless per-scanline cost, and it did.

Fixed cheaply (Phase 1): the six machines that cached a render in run_frame now render at a frame-boundary hook shared with debug_tick. Byte-identical output (frameshot 12/12), guarded by a ROM-gated acceptance test proven to fail when the bug is reintroduced. Closed phosphor-emulator-ifs0 (open since 2026-07-03), verified by pjl in the real frontend debugger.

Also built the missing instrument the audit depended on: CPU-agnostic, region-tagged bus write-event tracing for every AddressSpace16/32 board (previously only the 3 hand-wired Namco boards emitted events), plus io_write capture.

Follow-ups filed: nx2p (framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle consolidation), j55q (unify Namco boards onto AddressSpace16), pvmf (Marble Madness MOB rendering bug). Note graphics-consolidation.md Feature 2b lost its only consumer from this epic and should now be justified on its own merits.

comments.author: pjl
comments.text: Correction to the close reason: it stated graphics-consolidation.md Feature 2b 'lost its only consumer and should now be justified on its own merits'. That is wrong. 2b is already implemented (render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline_indexed in core/src/gfx/tilemap.rs; draw_sprite_row_indexed in core/src/gfx/sprite.rs) and is in production use by gottlieb/qbert. mcr2 and atari_system1 were deliberately not migrated to it for structural reasons (mcr2: 2x tile upscale vs the helper's 1:1 loop, plus dirty-tile incremental redraw vs unconditional per-scanline; atari_system1: u16 1024-entry index space vs the helper's &mut [u8], plus a priority_pens/translucency merge rather than a per-pixel prio_buf). So Phase 3 was never 2b's motivation and no 2b action is needed. graphics-consolidation.md's table listing mcr2 as a 2b target is stale.

title: raster: Phase 0 — trace-based Tier A/B classification audit
description: Phase 0, do first — first concrete consumer of the headless trace tool. For each render-once machine (digdug, galaga, xevious, btime, mrdo, foodf, gottlieb, mcr2/satans_hollow, atari_system1): enumerate its video registers (palette latch, scroll, bank latches, flip), set write-watchpoints / DebugTrace filtered to writes via 'disasm trace', run representative gameplay, and flag any write landing inside active display (cycle % cycles_per_frame < VISIBLE_LINES*cycles_per_scanline). Any active-display write => Tier A candidate (confirm visually vs a MAME per-scanline reference); none => Tier B. Record the result + evidence per machine so the decision is auditable. Initial hypotheses (must be measured): atari_system1=A confirmed; xevious/mcr2 likely A; galaga/digdug/btime/mrdo/foodf/gottlieb likely B.
close_reason: Phase 0 audit complete. Method + per-machine evidence in docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md. Result: of 9 render-once boards, only atari_system1 (Road Runner MO-bank) is Tier A and already implements per-band rendering; digdug/galaga/xevious/mrdo/burgertime/foodf/qbert/shollow/marble are all Tier B (measured: video registers written only in vblank, at init, sporadically at transitions, or as IRQ-acks with constant video bits). Also classified the full roster (per-scanline boards already correct; DVG/AVG vector N/A). Built the missing instrument: CPU-agnostic bus write-event tracing for all AddressSpace16/32 boards. Follow-ups: pvmf (marble MOB bug), j55q (Namco AddressSpace consolidation).

title: raster: Phase 1 — Tier B frame-boundary render fix (closes ifs0)
description: Phase 1 — low risk, high value, closes phosphor-emulator-ifs0. For each measured Tier B machine, move the single render out of run_frame() into a frame-boundary hook in tick() (render on the last visible-line boundary, or share a 'frame just completed' signal between run_frame and debug_tick); delete the redundant run_frame render call. Output must be byte-identical (same state, same frame boundary) — verify with disasm frameshot --compare vs pre-change. Add the ifs0 acceptance check: under debug_tick the framebuffer now changes across frames (was frozen). Zero runtime cost beyond today.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete (commit e9380a3). Moved the render into a frame-boundary hook shared by run_frame and debug_tick for the six machines that cached a render in run_frame: galaga, xevious, digdug (system-level hook) and burgertime/btime, qbert/gottlieb, shollow/mcr2 (board-level hook in tick). Audit found only these six were affected; mrdo, foodf, marble and roadrunner render on demand from live state and were never stale. Hook fires on the frame's last cycle, not the vblank boundary, because Phase 0 measured these boards writing video registers during vblank. Output byte-identical (frameshot 12/12 at frames 300 and 1200). ROM-gated acceptance test debug_tick_advances_picture_like_run_frame added and verified to fail when the bug is reintroduced. Also filed nx2p (framebuffer consolidation) from inconsistencies found while doing this.

title: raster: Phase 2 — Tier A non-priority per-scanline migration
description: Phase 2 — only for measured Tier A direct-RGB machines (e.g. xevious bg). Follow the namco_pac template: persistent scanline_buffer; in tick() at each cycles_per_scanline boundary with scanline<VISIBLE_LINES call render_scanline reading LIVE video state; render_frame becomes rotate/copy; delete end-of-frame render_video(). Sampling convention: render scanline N from state at the START of scanline N (scanline-quantized, standard MAME granularity) — document it. CRITICAL: keep vblank-latched state end-of-frame (galaga starfield update_starfield_at_vblank, double-buffered sprite RAM) — do NOT re-sample per line. Uses graphics Feature 2a enriched helpers. Validate the split-frame case vs a MAME per-scanline reference (not attract mode); confirm no vblank regression.
close_reason: Not needed — the Phase 0 audit found no Tier A non-priority machine to migrate. This phase's presumed target was xevious ('A? scrolling bg'); it measured Tier B: bg scroll X/Y are written exactly once per frame (from the sub-CPU, cpu 1) at a stable scanline ~8, which is VBLANK-IRQ-handler latency, not a mid-screen split. fg scroll is never written and flip is vblank-only. digdug, galaga, mrdo, burgertime and foodf likewise measured Tier B. Evidence: docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md. Reopen if a future machine measures Tier A with direct-RGB rendering.

title: raster: Phase 3 — Tier A priority-compositing per-scanline migration
description: Phase 3 — hardest tier, last. mcr2/atari_system1 (and gottlieb if measured Tier A) composite tiles+sprites through an indexed+priority buffer in separate full-frame passes; per-scanline priority compositing depends on graphics Feature 2b (indexed+priority scanline helpers). Migrate confirmed Tier A priority machines to per-scanline compositing after 2b lands; validate vs MAME references at the exact frames where the effect appears. If measurement shows a machine is actually Tier B, prefer the Phase 1 cheap fix and skip the compositing rework.
close_reason: Not needed — neither priority-compositing target requires migration. mcr2/shollow measured Tier B: its palette (0xEF80-0xEFFF, written via the 0xFF80 VRAM mirror) is rewritten in only 4 of 2400 frames, as bulk screen-transition reloads, with no repeating per-frame raster color-bar. atari_system1 IS Tier A via Road Runner's mid-frame motion-object bank switch, but the board already implements the fix: bankselect_w logs (scanline, mo_bank) and render_motion_objects renders each scanline band with its live bank, clipping sprites at the boundary (tests bankselect_logs_midframe_mo_bank_changes, motion_objects_follow_midframe_bank_switch). pjl verified Road Runner renders correctly; an input-driven automated test is impractical to build. Note: this phase was the only consumer of graphics-consolidation.md Feature 2b (indexed+priority scanline helpers) from this epic — that dependency is now unmotivated by raster fidelity and should be justified on its own merits. Evidence: docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md.

title: Audit increment-before-compare in periodic-interrupt dividers
description: starwars.rs asserted its periodic IRQ one cycle early because the divider incremented its counter before comparing (fixed in 219ccde; it reached the period on cycle N-1). The same idiom appears at atari_avg.rs:110, congo_bongo.rs:872 (sound_irq_counter) and quantum.rs:479, and the starwars watchdog had it too. Each is probably one cycle early. Not changed blind: a one-cycle shift is only observable when an instruction boundary falls in that window, so each needs its own check against a reference before touching it. On starwars the symptom was that a boundary at cycle 2095103 took an interrupt whose assert belongs at 2095104.

title: Consolidate framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle into a shared component
description:
Framebuffer definition and handling is inconsistent across machines; consolidate into shared infrastructure. Evidence gathered while doing mid-frame-raster Phase 1 (touched all of these):

  machine                 buffer name      owner   format    refresh trigger
  galaga/xevious/digdug   native_buffer    system  indexed8  frame boundary
  qbert (gottlieb)        pixel_buffer     board   indexed8  frame boundary
  shollow (mcr2)          pixel_buffer     board   indexed8  frame boundary
  burgertime (btime)      framebuffer      board   RGB24     frame boundary
  mrdo, foodf, marble     (none)           -       -         on-demand in render_frame
  williams/namco_pac/...  scanline_buffer  board   RGB24     per-scanline in tick

Four names, two formats, two owners (system vs board), three refresh triggers. The indexed -> palette -> RGB24 conversion loop in render_frame is hand-rolled ~5 times (galaga.rs:890, xevious.rs:941, digdug.rs:1011, gottlieb.rs:832, mcr2.rs:465).

Index width is NOT uniform, so the format enum needs at least Indexed8 / Indexed16 / Rgb24:
  - galaga 96 entries, gottlieb 16/32, mcr2 64  -> fit u8
  - atari_system1 uses a 1024-entry (10-bit) palette index space (alpha 0x000 /
    motion 0x100 / playfield 0x200 / translucent 0x300, masked & 0x3FF;
    atari_system1.rs:665-668, 675, 705) -> needs u16. An Indexed8-only design
    would silently truncate it.
Note atari_system1 already composites into an index buffer and converts to RGB only at the end - it just builds that buffer per render call instead of persisting it, so it is a natural adopter of the component (with the wider index).

Proposed shared component (core/src/gfx): a Framebuffer owning native dims + storage with a declared format (Indexed8{palette} | Indexed16{palette} | Rgb24), a single present(&self, out) doing the conversion (retires the duplicated loops), and a uniform frame-boundary/scanline refresh hook. Phase 1 had to hand-write the same frame-boundary render hook 6 times in 2 different shapes (3 system-level, 3 board-level) - that duplication is itself the argument for the component. Prefer board-level ownership to match the Board Wrapper Pattern.

Complementary to graphics-consolidation.md, which covers the scanline RENDER helpers (tilemap/sprite/bitmap, indexed+priority) but not framebuffer ownership/format/lifecycle. Must preserve byte-identical output per machine (frameshot compare).

Shared root cause worth exploiting: the u8-index assumption is baked into the EXISTING Feature 2b helpers too — render_tilemap_scanline_indexed / render_scrolled_tilemap_scanline_indexed (core/src/gfx/tilemap.rs:107,216) and draw_sprite_row_indexed (core/src/gfx/sprite.rs:108) all take index_buf: &mut [u8]. That is precisely why atari_system1 cannot use them: it composites into vec![0u16; w*h] for its 1024-entry palette (atari_system1.rs:682) and a u8 buffer would truncate the 10-bit index. So introducing Indexed16 here should come with u16 variants of those helpers; that removes one of atari_system1's two blockers (the other is its priority model - a priority_pens mask + translucency applied during the motion-object merge, not a per-pixel u8 prio_buf - which is not addressed by widening the index).

For reference, Feature 2b IS implemented and in production use by gottlieb/qbert (3 call sites). mcr2 does not adopt it for unrelated structural reasons: 2x tile upscale (helper is 1:1) and dirty-tile incremental redraw (helper renders every scanline unconditionally). graphics-consolidation.md's table still lists mcr2 as a 2b target; that table is stale.

title: Star Wars AVG busy window too short; VG_HALT clears early
description:
IN1 bit 6 is VG_HALT, the AVG done flag. We report done essentially always,
because trigger_avg() rasterises the entire vector list synchronously on the
$4600 GO write and the AVG is halted again by the time the CPU can look.
MAME models the AVG as taking real time (avg_starwars_device, done_r).

Caught under instruction-level lockstep against MAME 0.287: the two runs are
identical for 498,252 instructions and then

  idx 498252  EABA  LDA $4320     <- IN1
  idx 498253  ours A=$74   mame A=$34      (bit 6 differs)

Consequence: a game that spins waiting for VG_HALT exits the wait
immediately here, so it completes more work per frame than the hardware
would. That matches the measured symptom in phosphor-emulator-j63p — our
attract-mode slapstic bank switches run at 38/106/270 over 82/123/205 frames
against MAME's 39/87/187 — and it is the leading candidate for the state
divergence that eventually walks ESB into the frame-1129 failure path.

To reproduce the comparison:
  disasm trace --machine esb --frames 90 --cpu 0:regs \
    --entropy-file <mame LCG stream> -o ours.txt <roms>
  (MAME side: -debug -debugscript with `trace f,maincpu,noloop,{tracelog "%d %04X ",totalcycles,d}`
   under SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy)

Fix direction: give the AVG a duration. MAME derives it from the vector list
it walks; the cheapest faithful approach here is probably to count the AVG's
own cycles while rasterising and hold `halted` false for that many machine
cycles, rather than completing on the GO write.
notes:
2026-08-15 — the restructure this issue called for has landed (f184a12,
ea9c9c2), and the lockstep now verifies it (tooling in 75b5a92).

WHAT CHANGED

Avg::execute is now the sequencer loop itself rather than a per-instruction
decoder: it addresses the PROM with (halt ^ 1) | op | state, latches the next
state, dispatches handlers 0-7 when ST3 is set, and charges 8 master cycles
per state plus the beam time strobe3 consumes. states_for_op and its
"walk until a state repeats" construction are gone. The old decode_* bodies
now live in latch0-latch3 / strobe0-strobe3.

Two further sources of missing time came out of the restructure: CNTR now runs
the vector timer down before re-centering, and a run picks up the idle state
the sequencer parks in after a halt. run_cycles is sampled on the state that
raises the halt rather than summed to the end of the list.

Tempest and Quantum now load 136002-125, their own copy of the PROM. Quantum's
factory was calling load_program directly and bypassing load_rom_set, so
anything added there was dead code.

VERIFICATION (esb, 90 frames, MAME 0.287, instruction-level)

  before:  first divergence at instruction 507357
             ours cyc=2280017 pc=EABA D=74DF
             mame cyc=2280017 pc=EABA D=34DF     <- bit 6, VG_HALT
  after:   no divergence in 755843 instructions
             pc, D and cycle delta agree for the whole run

The "before" number is a control run of f184a12~1 against the same captured
reference, so the divergence this issue records reproduces on demand and it is
this change that closes it, not the harness.

Confirmed the entropy replay is not masking anything: re-running with 400 junk
values appended produces a byte-identical trace, so the recording never ran
out and the LFSR never silently took over.

Also measured, esb attract over 300 frames: the VG_HALT busy window grows from
a mean of 48,404 to 55,243 CPU cycles per GO, and the game issues 149 GO writes
instead of 165.

Frameshots at frames 400/900/1800: tempest and quantum pixel-identical across
the change; starwars and esb differ only in attract-sequence phase.

REPRO, corrected

The recipe in the description above does not work as written. `-debugscript`
is inert under `-debugger none` — that front-end resumes without ever pumping
the debugger's command loop — and the entropy stream had no recorded capture
method. Both are now checked in; see the header of
tools/mame_esb_lockstep.lua for the full command line, then
tools/lockstep_diff.py ours.txt mame_raw.txt.

Two traps worth repeating: clear MAME's -nvram_directory before each capture
(it writes NVRAM at exit, so run 2 is not a cold boot and splits from us at the
first $4500 read), and only the common prefix is comparable, since MAME
overruns the frame limit by a scheduler boundary.
close_reason: Fixed in f184a12: Avg::execute is now the PROM state sequencer rather than a per-instruction decoder, so the VG_HALT window comes from the real state sequence plus beam time. Verified by instruction-level lockstep against MAME 0.287 — esb now matches for all 755,843 instructions of a 90-frame run (pc, D, cycle delta), where a control run of the previous commit still diverges at instruction 507,357 on the LDA $4320 that reads VG_HALT.

title: M6809 indexed [n] extended indirect: reference core charges +8 cycles, datasheet says +5
description:
Documenting a KNOWN, EXPECTED cross-validation divergence so it is not re-investigated as a regression. No phosphor-side change is believed necessary.

SYMPTOM
  ./cross-validation/bin/validate_m6809 cpu-validation/test_data/m6809/*.json
  -> 264,090/266,000 pass. 53 opcodes fail a few cases each, always
     'cycles expected=N got=N+3' (expected = phosphor, got = reference).

CAUSE
Every failing case uses indexed postbyte 0x9F -- [n], extended indirect.
Verified by counting: a4.json has 8 failures and exactly 8 cases whose name
starts 'a4 9f'. All 53 affected opcodes are indexed; the deficit is uniformly 3.

WHICH SIDE IS RIGHT
MC6809E datasheet Table 2 (Indexed Addressing Mode) lists Extended Indirect,
16-Bit Address, [n], postbyte 10011111, as +5 cycles / +2 bytes. phosphor
charges 5 (core/src/cpu/m6809/alu.rs indexed_mode_internal: 0x0F => 0, plus
4 bus cycles). The reference core (cross-validation/mame0148/.../m6809.c)
charges 8. Per CLAUDE.md ('if cross-validation differs from datasheet for
timings, use the datasheet values') phosphor is correct.

NOTES
- Pre-existing, unrelated to phosphor-emulator-m6809-tst-vma-cycle-2kaj; the
  '6d 998/1000' figure quoted in that issue is this, not a TST problem.
- Per-opcode counts shift on every regeneration since they depend on how often
  a random postbyte lands on 0x9F (~4/1000 per indexed opcode).
- Recorded in cpu-validation/README_m6809.md under 'Known divergence'.

ACTION
Confirm the reading of Table 2 independently, then either close as
working-as-intended or, if the reference turns out to match real silicon,
reopen the timing question.
notes:
2026-08-09 — RETRACTION. I raised this to P1 and made it block j63p on the
theory that this cycle discrepancy was the source of j63p's timing drift.
That theory is DISPROVEN; priority is back to P3 and the dependency is
removed. j63p's cause is the CPU reset sequence costing 0 emulated cycles,
not instruction timing.

What the j63p side-by-side against MAME 0.287 does and does not say here:

DOES: over the first 454,189 instructions of ESB boot, our M6809 matches
modern MAME's cycle-stepped core EXACTLY — a constant offset and zero
per-instruction discrepancies. Many indexed modes are exercised (postbyte
modes 0x0-0x9, 0xC-0xE non-indirect, and 0x1/0x2/0x3/0x4/0x6/0x8/0x9
indirect). Our indexed timing is right for all of them.

DOES NOT: that workload never executes postbyte 0x9F ([n] extended
indirect), so it does not settle THIS issue either way. I briefly thought
it did — that was a decoding bug in my analysis script, which treated the
second byte of every instruction as a postbyte and so counted `LDA #$FF`
(86 FF) as postbyte 0xFF. Corrected: zero occurrences.

NEW EVIDENCE, static, still needs an empirical check:
Modern MAME (src/devices/cpu/m6809/m6809.lst, cycle-stepped, generated) is
a different core from the cross-validation reference (mame0148, 2013,
table-driven). Counting its cycle markers for the INDEXED routine, noting
that `dummy_vma(n)` is n cycles (m6809.h:217, it reads $FFFF n times):
  postbyte 0x84 (,R):   postbyte + dummy_read_opcode_arg + set_ea      = 3
  postbyte 0x9F ([n]):  postbyte + 2 offset reads + dummy_vma(1)
                        + 2 indirect reads + dummy_vma(1) + set_ea     = 8
  delta = +5
So MODERN MAME agrees with the datasheet and with phosphor; only the 2013
reference core charges +8. That is consistent with closing this as
working-as-intended, but it is a static reading of generated source, not a
measurement.

TO CLOSE: measure it. `mame esb ... -debug -debugscript` with
SDL_VIDEODRIVER=dummy works headlessly; inject `A6 9F nn nn` (LDA [n]) and
`A6 84` (LDA ,X) into RAM, trace with {tracelog "%d ",totalcycles}, and
diff the deltas. My first attempt at this failed — only the trailing NOPs
were traced and the injected LDAs produced no usable line — so the
injection/step sequencing needs work.

title: Conditional DIP options: bonus-life tables depend on Lives (Galaga/Dig Dug/Xevious)
description:
The DIP framework (DipOption/DipChoice in core machine.rs) has no support for options whose valid choices depend on another option's value. On real Namco Galaga-family hardware the Bonus Life bits are interpreted differently based on the Lives/fighters setting (MAME models this with PORT_CONDITION):
- Galaga: Bonus Life (DSWB 0x38) conditioned on fighters (DSWB 0xc0).
- Xevious: Bonus Life (DSWA 0x1c) conditioned on Lives (DSWA 0x60).
- Dig Dug: similar.

Today all three flatten it to one non-conditional table, so the labels shown are only correct for one Lives setting (and Galaga's current labels don't even match MAME's conditional tables). The DIP bits still reach the game; only the UI labels are wrong.

Fix: add an optional condition to DipOption (e.g. {other_mask, equals/not-equals, value} + per-condition choice lists), teach assert_dip_banks_valid + the frontend rebinding UI to honor it, then make the Galaga/Dig Dug/Xevious bonus-life tables conditional and correct against MAME.

A seam is documented in the xevious.rs module header.

Depends on the Galaga 54XX issue (phosphor-emulator-uxi9), which builds the reusable LLE 54XX device + discrete DAC/filter primitives. This issue then:
- Fits the 54XX on the Xevious board (54xx.bin ships in xevious.zip) and routes its output into the Xevious audio mix.
- Supplies Xevious's DAC/filter network values (per MAME xevious/galaga audio) if they differ from Galaga's bosco_54xx_dac ladder.
- Updates the xevious.rs header note + README bullet to drop 'explosion channel stubbed'.
- Tests: machine-level check that an in-game explosion command produces non-silent output.

Timings/datasheet take precedence over MAME per project convention; keep MAME refs in commit/PR, not source comments.

title: Per-game settings: per-machine config overrides + unify DIP/binding persistence
description:
Make all config.toml settings overridable per game and restructure persistence so a machine's config overrides, DIP switch state, and input bindings live together under one per-machine section.

Today: config.toml (config.rs Config: rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale) is entirely global. state.toml (state.rs State) already persists input_bindings and dip_switches as separate top-level maps keyed by machine_id. So bindings + DIPs are per-game but config is not, and the three per-machine concerns are scattered.

Goal:
- Per-game config overrides for every Config field (rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, scale), keyed by machine_id. Resolution order: CLI arg > per-game override > global config.toml > built-in default. Global config.toml stays the user-edited default source.
- Restructure DIP + binding storage into a single per-machine settings section instead of separate top-level input_bindings / dip_switches maps. Sketch: State { window_position, machines: HashMap<String, MachineSettings> } where MachineSettings { scale, rom_path, nvram_path, save_path, dip_switches: Vec<u8>, input_bindings: Vec<SerializedBinding> } (all optional / diff-only — omit fields equal to the resolved default, drop the whole entry when empty, preserving the current no-redundant-defaults behavior).

Touch points: frontend/src/config.rs (Config), frontend/src/state.rs (State + save/load), frontend/src/main.rs (load/resolve/persist: lines ~98-150 build bindings, dips, scale; lines ~134-150 persist diffs).

Considerations:
- Backward-compat / migration for existing state.toml (top-level input_bindings + dip_switches). Decide: one-time migration on load vs. accept a clean break (state.toml is auto-generated, low stakes) — document the choice.
- Keep the diff-only persistence (bindings_eq pattern, DIP-vs-default compare) so unchanged games leave no entry.
- Likely warrants splitting into subtasks (config.rs/state.rs schema + resolution; main.rs wiring + migration; tests) when picked up.
close_reason: Unified per-machine settings into a single [machines.<name>] section in state.toml (MachineSettings with diff-only config overrides + DIP/binding state), with one-time migration from legacy top-level maps; wired CLI > per-game > config > default resolution for scale/rom_path/nvram_path/save_path in main.rs. Keyed by registry/CLI name (rather than machine_id) so per-game rom_path can resolve before machine creation.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Do Castle family
description: Convert docastle.rs (two Z80s, five registered variants, eight bus_split! sites, board and machines in one file) per docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md. Follow the Galaga shape: group the CPUs into one field beside the bus, one generic per-cycle tick. Measure docastle before/after; run golden frames for all five variants.
close_reason:
Done in f38e13a.

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  docastle 2.506 -> 2.403 ms/f  -4.1%
  dorunrun 3.202 -> 3.095       -3.3%

Modest, and diagnosed rather than shrugged at: these are the slowest boards in the bench set and most of a frame is not bus dispatch. Four SN76489A PSGs are serviced every cycle, and every main-CPU T-state clones the whole Z80 for the WAIT rewind. Filed the clone as its own issue.

Shape: simplest possible -- the board already decodes through variant.map(), so DocastleBoard implements Bus and IS the bus for all five registered variants. No view, no trait, no per-game wrapper. Both Z80s moved to DocastleSystem; tick/step_main/run_scanlines/run_frame became free functions over (main, sub, board).

Why the split has to be real here: step_main rewinds the main Z80 when a latch read asserts WAIT -- the board sets main_retry from *inside* a bus read and the caller restores a snapshot afterwards. That handshake only works if the CPU is reachable independently of the bus it is reading, which is exactly what this refactor provides (previously it worked through the aliased raw pointer).

Also inverted the frame loop to scanline-outer / cycle-inner (VBLANK IRQ + the sub CPU's periodic raster IRQ were the only per-scanline work), renamed DocastleBoard::check_interrupts to interrupt_state to avoid Bus-method recursion, and preserved the save-state layout (machine writes both CPUs before the board, the order the board used).

Six of the eight bus_split! sites were in tests; they became sys.step_cycle() loops with bus_read/bus_write for direct bus pokes.

Golden frames unchanged for all three pinned variants (docastle, dorunrun, dowild); machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.
