title: Epic: Rhai scripting / debugging interface
description:
A lightweight, pure-Rust programmable interface for driving and inspecting machines — the phosphor analogue of MAME's Lua, built on the debug traits and the headless boot harness that already exist. Design: ~/rhai-scripting.md.

WHY: today the only options are hand-writing a throwaway Rust example (machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs hard-codes an input/register timeline in a fn), generating references out-of-tree with MAME Lua, or the flag-driven disasm trace/frameshot CLI. A script closes the "boot machine, drive inputs on a timeline, read memory, snapshot a frame, branch on a value" gap that flags cannot express.

LANGUAGE: Rhai, not Lua. Pure Rust (CLAUDE.md forbids C deps in core/machines; mlua is a C library), deterministic and sandboxed (no ambient time/RNG, built-in operation limits), first-class Rust binding. MAME-script portability is knowingly sacrificed.

SCOPE — v1 is a headless runner with a READ-FIRST API: a phosphor-script crate (lib + bin), a DebugSession over the existing Harness, and Rhai bindings for memory read, CPU pc/regs, disassemble, run_frames/step, inputs by stable name, and screenshot PNG. Read-only keeps replay honesty trivially intact and minimizes the binding surface.

v1 NON-GOALS (specified in the doc, deferred to v2): pokes, watchpoints + callbacks, event-trace access, save/load state, DIP editing, and the interactive in-frontend console.

KEY DECISIONS (from the doc):
  1. Rhai, not Lua.
  2. Headless first; the lib/bin split keeps the deferred frontend console cheap later.
  3. Read-first v1.
  4. Build on the shared Harness — promote it (and the ROM-path resolver) rather than forking a third boot path.
  5. Machine handle is Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>>; rhai without the sync feature (single-threaded).
  6. Global open() plus a pre-bound m, so single- and multi-machine scripts fall out of one design.
  7. No core/machines edits — read-first needs none; the crate is purely additive.

SEQUENCING: children 1-6 are the v1 build order; 1 is the only prerequisite refactor and blocks the rest. Children 7-12 are the deferred v2 surface and the packaging decision.

NOTE ON A CORRECTED CLAIM: an earlier revision of the design doc said this interface would be "a convenient harness for the trace-based Tier A/B classification audit" that mid-frame-raster Phase 0 called for. That is NOT true of v1 as scoped — the audit's core operation is timestamping video-register writes within a frame, which needs watchpoints or event-trace, and both are v1 non-goals. Only the v2 surface could express it. Phase 0 was completed against the disasm trace CLI instead (see docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md); the doc has been corrected. The audit remains a good worked example of what a v2 script should express, and the two capabilities it actually needed are the strongest argument for which v2 items to land first.
close_reason:
Epic complete. All 12 children (.1-.12) plus the poke Frontend-tagging follow-up (phosphor-emulator-ryqt) are closed, verified, and committed on the rhai branch (13 commits).

v1 (headless, read-first): .1 promoted Harness + ROM-resolver into phosphor-harness; .2 phosphor-script crate skeleton (lib+bin); .3 DebugSession read-first API; .4 Rhai engine bindings (Machine type, open(), limits, print hooks); .5 CLI run subcommand + examples + README; .6 end-to-end frameshot parity (byte-exact on mrdo).

v2: .7 memory pokes; .8 watchpoints (all-CPU watch + drained hit list, proven on galaga's sub-CPU trap); .9 event-trace + hang detection (region-tagged capture on shollow); .10 save/load state + DIP editing (exact round-trip on galaga); .11 interactive in-frontend console (Ctrl+backtick, shared Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>>, human-smoke-tested and confirmed working); .12 packaging decision (keep separate binary, recorded with reversal recipe). Follow-up ryqt: pokes tagged DebugAccessSource::Frontend in the trace (verified on derived + Namco boards).

Design decisions held: pure-Rust Rhai (no C dep), one shared boot path, lib/bin split enabling the console, all v2 work additive except the poke-tagging (derive + 3 Namco boards). Every capability validated end-to-end on real ROMs or by human smoke-test; clippy + fmt clean throughout.

title: rhai: promote Harness + ROM-path resolver into a shared crate
description:
Harness (boot + coin/press scheduling + frame stepping) lives at tools/disasm/src/harness.rs and is crate-private to tools/disasm; it is shared today by frameshot and trace. The ROM-path resolver (load_rom_set / load_from_zip in tools/disasm/src/main.rs) is duplicated in frontend/src/rom_path.rs. phosphor-script must reuse both rather than forking a third machine-construction sequence (epic decision 4).

WORK: promote Harness plus the ROM-path resolver into a shared location - either a small phosphor-harness library crate or a shared module both tools depend on - and re-point tools/disasm at it. This also retires the existing ROM-resolver duplication rather than adding a third copy.

API to preserve: Harness::build(machine, path, nvram, coin_at, presses), run_frame(), machine_mut() -> &mut dyn FrontendMachine, and PressSpec { control, at, hold }.

ACCEPTANCE: tools/disasm builds and all its tests pass unchanged, including the ROM-gated ones; no behavior change to frameshot or trace; clippy and fmt clean.

If promotion is deferred, phosphor-script would need a temporary copy - acceptable but a known debt, so prefer doing this first. Blocks the rest of v1.
close_reason: Promoted Harness + ROM-path resolver into new phosphor-harness crate; re-pointed disasm (harness.rs/load_rom_set/load_from_zip removed) and frontend (rom_path.rs removed) at it, dropping duplicate ROM resolver and direct zip deps. API preserved (Harness::build/run_frame/machine_mut, PressSpec). Workspace builds; disasm 39 tests incl. ROM-gated pass; frontend 21 + harness 3 pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: rhai v2: save/load state + DIP editing
description:
Deferred from v1. Bind SaveState save_state/load_state and DIP switch editing to the Machine type.

Useful for scripted regression work: snapshot at a known point, branch, and restore - which also makes long scripted runs cheap to re-enter without replaying from reset. DIP editing lets a script sweep machine configurations (coinage, lives, bonus thresholds) without recompiling or hand-editing NVRAM.

Extends the Machine type without reshaping the v1 surface.
close_reason:
Bound save/load state and DIP editing into the script surface. Additive — SaveState (save_state/load_state) and DipSwitches (dip_banks/dip_bank_value/set_dip_bank_value/set_dip_option) are on the machine bundle; the only core change is a new additive Harness::reset() (machine.reset + zero the frame counter).

DebugSession: save_state()->Option<Vec<u8>>, load_state()->Result, reset() (also clears watchpoint/event/hang accumulators + resets the hang detector), dip_banks()/dip_bank_value/set_dip_bank_value/set_dip_option, plus set_dip_by_name(option,choice) resolving names from the metadata (the ergonomic sweep path; honors OnReset timing via reset). rhai: save_state (returns a Blob) / load_state(blob) / reset; dip_banks (array of nested maps name/options/mask/apply/choices) / dip_bank / set_dip_bank / set_dip_option / set_dip(name,label)->bool.

Tests: stub now supports save_state over its poke store (5-byte records) and a 2-option DIP bank (Immediate Lives + OnReset Bonus, exercising the mask-merge + by-name paths). 6 stub unit tests. Gated integration test on real galaga: save at attract, run 90 frames (guard asserts the sprite RAM animates: 301 bytes change), load_state restores the exact RAM signature; DSWA metadata reads back, set_dip('Difficulty','Hard') sets the low bits. Skips cleanly w/o ROMs. clippy+fmt clean; 36 unit + 4 integration green; disasm regression (39) green for the Harness::reset change.

Use: snapshot/branch/restore for cheap re-entry of long runs; DIP sweeps of coinage/lives/difficulty without recompiling or hand-editing NVRAM.

title: rhai v2: interactive in-frontend console
description:
Deferred by choice (epic decision 2), but confirmed feasible: a near-clone of the existing DIP side panel.

SHAPE: a new frontend/src/console_ui.rs plus roughly 5 wiring sites in frontend/src/emulator.rs - a ConsoleState, a panels_width term, a toggle key, the draw call and its gate inside present_with_debug, and a post-frame command drain.

KEYMAP CONSTRAINT: F-keys are already taken and letters collide with game input, so the toggle is likely a modifier combo. This is the same constraint that deferred the debugger step-key remap in headless-debugging.md Feature 5 - solve it once for both.

REUSE: embeds this crate's LIB (which is why v1 ships a lib/bin split rather than burying the engine builder in a binary), binding the engine to the LIVE machine rather than a headless session. Pokes are applied with the queue-then-apply pattern already used by DeviceAction in frontend/src/debug_ui.rs, so script writes land at a safe point in the frame rather than mid-tick.

Depends on the v1 crate existing and, for anything that writes, on the pokes child.
close_reason:
Implemented the interactive in-frontend Rhai console. Shared-session approach (per user decision): the emulator now owns its machine as Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>> and reaches it each frame via sess.machine_mut(); the console holds a clone of the SAME Rc, so it reuses phosphor-script's engine and bindings UNCHANGED against the live machine (what the epic's lib/bin split was for).

CHANGES: new frontend/src/console_ui.rs (egui side panel: scrollback + single-line input, a near-clone of the DIP panel). emulator.rs: run() now takes+returns Box<dyn FrontendMachine>; the loop binds machine = sess.machine_mut() at the top and drop(sess) before evaluating any submitted command (snapshot-before / act-after, so the machine isn't borrowed during eval, no RefCell double-borrow). Toggle is Ctrl+backtick (modifier combo; plain backtick stays DIP); while visible the loop routes keyboard to egui and suppresses game input + other hotkeys (Esc/Ctrl+backtick close it). panels_width includes the console; present gate + draw wired. Console print/debug rerouted from stdout into the scrollback via on_print/on_debug over an Rc buffer. At shutdown the machine is reclaimed via Rc::try_unwrap + DebugSession::into_machine and handed back to main.rs. Added Harness::into_machine and DebugSession::from_machine/into_machine/machine/machine_mut (all additive).

TESTING: builds clean first try (borrow scoping, Mod combo, Rc ownership, try_unwrap all compile); clippy + fmt clean; 25 frontend tests (incl. 4 new ConsoleState unit tests: toggle/focus, one-shot take_pending, newline split, bounded scrollback); phosphor-script 36 + disasm regression green. CAVEAT: the egui interaction (focus, keystroke routing, panel layout) CANNOT be verified in CI, it needs a real SDL/GL window. State logic is unit-tested and the UI mirrors existing patterns (debug_ui hex input, DIP panel), but a human should smoke-test the window.

KEYMAP NOTE: only the console toggle was solved; the deferred debugger step-key remap is left as-is to keep scope bounded.

title: rhai: decide packaging - separate binary vs disasm script subcommand
description:
Packaging decision, deliberately deferred to build time (the design doc lists it as a follow-up, not a fixed choice).

Once the Harness is shared (first child), a script subcommand on the EXISTING disasm binary could delegate to this crate instead of shipping a second binary:
  disasm script run <script.rhai> --machine <name> <rompath>

TRADE-OFF: one binary is fewer artifacts and puts scripting next to trace/frameshot/imgdiff where a user already is; a separate phosphor-script binary keeps the tool boundary clean and avoids growing disasm's CLI surface further. Either way the engine lives in the phosphor-script LIB, so this is purely about how it is exposed - the decision is cheap to defer and cheap to reverse.

Revisit after the v1 CLI child lands and there is real usage to judge by.
close_reason:
DECISION: keep phosphor-script as its own binary; do NOT add a disasm script subcommand.

Rationale (recorded in tools/script/README.md Packaging section, with a reversal recipe):
- Scripting is a distinct capability (programmatically DRIVING a machine) vs what disasm does (disassembly + one-shot analysis/capture: frameshot/trace/imgdiff/gfxview/rom). A tool named for what it does is more discoverable than a 9th disasm subcommand.
- disasm already carries 8 subcommands; folding scripting in grows an already-broad CLI.
- The real reuse point is the LIBRARY, not the binary: the in-frontend console (.11) embeds the engine builder directly, so a second binary entry point adds no leverage.
- Cheap to reverse: a delegating disasm script run subcommand is ~6 lines over phosphor_script::{build_engine, open_machine} + run_with_scope if usage later favors it; the recipe is in the README.

CHANGE: docs-only. Added the Packaging section; brought the README intro up to date (the console is no longer future; watchpoints/event-trace/hang/save-state/DIP are implemented, not deferred to v2); removed a stray content-tag artifact left in the file from its original write.

Last epic child (.1-.12 all done). Remaining epic follow-up: the poke Frontend-tagging issue phosphor-emulator-ryqt.

title: rhai: DebugSession read-first inspection API
description:
src/session.rs - wrap the shared Harness and add the read-first accessors that the trace subcommand currently calls inline on machine_mut(). This is the only genuinely new code in v1; everything else is binding.

STRUCT: DebugSession { harness, input_ids: HashMap<String, InputId> built once from input_controls(), fb: Vec<u8> reused RGB24 render buffer }.

METHODS: open(machine_name, rom_path); run_frames(n); step() -> u32 boundary mask; read(cpu, addr) -> Option<u8>; pc(cpu) -> Option<u32>; regs(cpu) -> Vec<(String, u64)>; disasm(cpu, addr) -> Option<String>; input(name, pressed); input_axis(name, value); screenshot(path); frame_count(); machine_id(); display_size().

BINDING NOTES (verified trait surface in core/src/core/machine.rs and debug.rs): reads route through MachineDebug::debug_bus then BusDebug::read; pc/regs/disasm use BusDebug::cpus then DebugCpu::debug_pc / debug_disassemble and Debuggable::debug_registers - exactly as the trace cycle loop and the frontend debug_ui disassemble_from already do. Machines without debug support yield None or empty, and scripts can check.

input is IMPERATIVE (apply an edge now) and is deliberately distinct from the Harness's SCHEDULED PressSpec (fire at frame N). It resolves the stable control name to an InputId via the input_ids map and calls handle_input with an InputEvent::Button, so a script can drive a timeline imperatively: input(coin,true); run_frames(8); input(coin,false).

screenshot mirrors frameshot: display_size then render_frame then RGB24 PNG via the png crate. Raster-only - vector machines render through vector_display_list, the same limitation frameshot has.

step() uses debug_tick() and needs cycles_per_frame > 0; run_frames always works via the harness.

ACCEPTANCE: unit-tested against a stub FrontendMachine with NO ROMs - a trivial run_frame bumping a counter and a tiny BusDebug returning seeded bytes. ROM-free and fully unit-testable.
close_reason: Implemented DebugSession read-first inspection API in tools/script/src/session.rs: open/run_frames/step/read/pc/regs/disasm/input/input_axis/screenshot/frame_count/machine_id/display_size, all routing through the machine debug traits (debug_bus->read, cpus->debug_pc/debug_disassemble/debug_registers) exactly as trace/debug_ui do; imperative input by stable name; frameshot-style RGB24 PNG screenshot with central orientation. Added three additive accessors to phosphor-harness (machine(), frame_count(), from_machine()) so DebugSession can wrap a Harness with &self reads and tests can inject a stub. 9 ROM-free unit tests against a stub FrontendMachine (seeded BusDebug + StubCpu + input recorder) all pass; clippy + fmt clean; disasm/frontend/harness regression green.

title: rhai: engine bindings (Machine type, open(), limits, print hooks)
description:
src/rhai_api.rs - build the Engine and register the v1 surface.

TYPE: register a custom type Machine = Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>>. Rhai requires registered types be Clone; the Rc handle is cheap to clone and, without the sync feature, needs no Send/Sync.

METHODS map 1:1 to DebugSession: m.run_frames(n); m.step() -> i64 boundary mask; m.read(cpu, addr) -> i64 (-1 if unmapped); m.pc(cpu) -> i64 (-1 if none); m.regs(cpu) -> Map of name to value; m.disasm(cpu, addr) -> String; m.input(name, on); m.input_axis(name, v); m.screenshot(path) throwing on error; m.frame_count() -> i64; m.id() -> String; m.display_size() -> array of 2.

GLOBAL: register open(machine_name, rom_path) -> Machine so a script can open one or SEVERAL machines - this is what enables in-repo A/B comparisons across two builds or ROM sets. The CLI pre-binds m in the Scope when the machine and rompath args are supplied, so single-machine scripts stay terse.

OUTPUT: route Rhai print and debug to stdout via Engine::on_print / on_debug.

GUARDS: Engine::set_max_operations and set_max_call_levels to bound runaway scripts - important for CI scripts and the future interactive console. Rhai's default engine exposes no time or RNG, so determinism holds; do NOT add packages that would introduce either (the emulator has no wall-clock or RNG in the tick path today, and replay honesty depends on keeping it that way).

ACCEPTANCE: unit tests drive Rhai scripts against the stub machine - run_frames(3) advances frame_count, read returns the seed, input reaches handle_input, and set_max_operations aborts an infinite loop. Covers the whole binding path without ROM files.
close_reason: Implemented Rhai engine bindings in tools/script/src/rhai_api.rs: pub type Machine = Rc<RefCell<DebugSession>>; build_engine() registers the Machine type, global open(), and the v1 method surface 1:1 with DebugSession (run_frames/step/read(-1 if unmapped)/pc(-1 if none)/regs(Map)/disasm(String)/input/input_axis/screenshot(throws)/frame_count/id/display_size([w,h])); print+debug routed to stdout via on_print/on_debug; runaway guards set_max_operations(1e9)+set_max_call_levels(64); no time/RNG packages added. Added pub open_machine() Rust helper for the CLI to pre-bind m. Extracted the session stub into a shared #[cfg(test)] test_support module (stub_session/stub_machine/COIN_ID) reused by both session and rhai_api tests. 7 rhai_api tests (run_frames advances frame_count, read seed, read -1 unmapped, input reaches handle_input, pc/regs/disasm/display_size/id/step bindings, max_operations aborts infinite loop, open unknown-machine throws) + 9 session tests all pass; clippy + fmt clean.

title: rhai: CLI run subcommand + examples + README
description:
src/main.rs - clap CLI mirroring the disasm style.

USAGE:
  phosphor-script run <script.rhai> --machine <name> <rompath>
  phosphor-script run <script.rhai>          (no pre-bound m; the script calls open(...) itself)

Reads the script, builds the engine via rhai_api, pushes m into the Scope when the args provide it, evals, prints errors to stderr, and returns an ExitCode - the same Ok-to-stdout / Err-to-stderr convention as disasm's run_command.

EXAMPLES to ship:
  examples/capture.rhai     - frameshot equivalent, used for the end-to-end validation:
                              m.run_frames(3100); m.screenshot(out.png); print pc.
  examples/coin_start.rhai  - imperative input timeline, generalizing the hard-coded
                              machines/examples/asteroid_capture.rs: run_frames, coin edge,
                              start edge, run_frames, screenshot.

README with the API table (the Rhai method to DebugSession mapping and return types), so the surface is documented where a script author will look.

ACCEPTANCE: both examples run end to end against a real ROM set; clippy and fmt clean.

Validated end-to-end against galaga ROMs: capture.rhai produced a correct attract-screen PNG (verified visually), coin_start.rhai (warms up past galaga's ~3000-frame self-test, since open() loads no factory NVRAM, then coins+starts) produced a PLAYER 1/STAGE 1 gameplay PNG; both exit 0. title: rhai: end-to-end validation against frameshot
description:
Prove the scripted path produces exactly what the existing rig produces.

CHECK: run examples/capture.rhai for mrdo, then capture the same frame with the existing tool and diff:
  cargo run -p phosphor-script -- run examples/capture.rhai --machine mrdo <roms>
  disasm frameshot --machine mrdo --frames 3100 -o ref.png <roms>
  disasm imgdiff out.png ref.png     ->  expect 0%
Both call render_frame after the same frame count, so they MUST match exactly; any difference is a real bug in the session or harness wiring.

ROM GATING: gate any committed ROM-dependent test behind an env var, following the pattern already used in tools/disasm/src/trace.rs - a roms_dir() helper that reads PHOSPHOR_ROMS (falling back to the conventional local ROM dir) and makes the test skip with an eprintln when absent, so CI without ROMs stays green.

Note the harness promotion in the first child means a shared roms_dir helper may be the natural home for this rather than a third copy.

ACCEPTANCE: imgdiff reports 0% for at least one raster machine; the gated test skips cleanly with no ROM dir present.
close_reason: Added gated end-to-end parity test tools/script/tests/frameshot_parity.rs: renders mrdo at frame 3100 via the scripted path (DebugSession::open -> run_frames -> screenshot PNG, decoded back to RGB) and via the frameshot path (Harness::build -> run_frame x N -> render_frame + central orientation), and asserts byte-exact RGB equality (== imgdiff 0%). Passes for mrdo; guard-the-guard rejects a uniform frame. ROM-gated via the shared roms_dir helper; skips cleanly with an eprintln when no ROM dir (verified with PHOSPHOR_ROMS=/nonexistent -> skipped, 0.00s). Promoted roms_dir() into phosphor-harness (pub) and re-pointed trace.rs at it, retiring the local copy rather than adding a third. Also corrected a factual error introduced in .5: galaga has NO NVRAM (nothing in machines/src implements it) - fixed the coin_start.rhai comment that wrongly attributed galaga's ~3000-frame cold-boot warmup to missing NVRAM; the warmup is just galaga's normal power-on self-test. clippy + fmt clean; disasm regression (39 tests) + phosphor-script (16 + 1) green.

title: rhai v2: memory/register pokes
description:
Deferred from v1 by design decision 3 (read-first). Adds write access: poke memory and CPU registers from a script.

REPLAY HONESTY: pokes must be tagged DebugAccessSource::Frontend, which already exists in core/src/core/watchpoint.rs, so they surface in traces and do NOT masquerade as hardware state. This is the reason v1 was scoped read-only - with no pokes, a script can only observe and drive legitimate machine input, so replay honesty is free by construction. Once pokes land, that property is maintained by the tagging rather than by absence.

Extends the Machine type without reshaping the v1 surface.
close_reason:
Landed the memory-poke CAPABILITY (scoped down from the original memory+register goal per discussion). Added BusDebug::poke default (forwards to write) as a board-agnostic seam in core; DebugSession::poke(cpu,addr,data)->bool via debug_bus_mut; rhai m.poke(cpu,addr,value)->bool. Read-first surface is now read-first + one poke. Tests: stub bus stores pokes so read-after-poke round-trips (4 new tests across session + rhai_api, incl. no-debug->false); end-to-end on real galaga (read 0x24 at 0x8000, poke 0xAA, read 0xAA). Docs updated. All green: phosphor-script 20+1, core/machines/frontend regression, clippy+fmt.

DEFERRED (filed as phosphor-emulator-ryqt): DebugAccessSource::Frontend trace-tagging of pokes. NOT contained (BusDebug is hand-written per board or derived; galaga's write shares the CPU hot-path write_backing) and NOT observable until a script/console can record+read a trace (v2 .9/.11). BusDebug::poke is the override seam for it. Register pokes also deferred (need a per-CPU debug_set_register across ~8 CPUs + a mutable-CPU accessor).

title: rhai v2: watchpoints + script callbacks
description:
Deferred from v1. Bind the real WatchpointCondition and set_watchpoint_cond (core/src/core/watchpoint.rs) plus a way for a script to react to hits (callback or drained hit list).

API DESIGN WARNING, learned the hard way during the mid-frame-raster Phase 0 audit: watchpoints are scoped PER CPU. set_watchpoint_cond(cpu, addr, kind, cond) only fires for accesses by THAT cpu. On multi-CPU boards the video registers are frequently written by a sub-CPU rather than the main one - on the Namco boards (galaga/xevious/digdug) the scroll registers are written by CPU 1, not CPU 0. A script that watches CPU 0 therefore gets ZERO hits and no diagnostic, which reads as a broken emulator rather than a mis-scoped watch. This cost real debugging time.

Mitigations to consider when binding: default to watching all CPUs; and/or return an assertable hit count so a script can fail loudly on zero; and/or expose the CPU index on each hit. Event-trace does not have this problem because it is CPU-agnostic, which is exactly why it was the better instrument for that audit.

Together with the event-trace child, this is what would let a script express the Tier A/B classification audit that v1 cannot.
close_reason:
Bound watchpoints into the script surface. PURELY ADDITIVE (no core/board edits) — the watchpoint API (set_watchpoint_cond/take_watchpoint_hit/clear_all_watchpoints) already exists on MachineDebug and is implemented per board.

DebugSession: watch(addr,kind,cond)->cpu count (sets on ALL cpus), watch_cpu(cpu,...), clear_watchpoints, cpu_count, take_hits()->Vec<WatchpointHit>; run_frames/step now drain the machine's 64-entry hit queue into a session accumulator each frame/tick. rhai: watch/watch_value/watch_changed/watch_bits/watch_cpu/clear_watchpoints/hits/cpu_count, binding the real WatchpointCondition (Always/Equals/Bits/Changed); hits() returns an array of maps {cpu,addr,kind,value,width,pc,cycle,source,region} and drains.

PER-CPU-SCOPING TRAP (the API-design warning) addressed all three ways: watch() defaults to ALL cpus; each hit carries cpu_index; hit count is assertable (m.hits().len()) so a script fails loudly on zero. Gated integration test proves it on real galaga: watching 0x9100/0x9800 across all 3 CPUs over 600 attract frames yields deterministic hits split cpu0=152, cpu1=403 — i.e. a sub-CPU writes the MAJORITY, which a cpu-0-only watch would have silently missed. 5 stub unit tests + gated test (skips cleanly w/o ROMs). clippy+fmt clean; 25 unit + 2 integration green.

Callback model NOT used: a drained hit list is simpler, deterministic, and avoids re-entering rhai from Rust mid-frame.

title: rhai v2: event-trace + hang-detection access
description:
Deferred from v1. Bind the DebugTrace event stream and the real HangDetector (core/src/core/debug_hang.rs) so a script can drain bus events and detect stuck CPUs.

SUBSTRATE NOTE: this binding is now worth having, where before it would have looked broken. DebugTrace used to be an EMPTY no-op impl on most machines, so trace_events() would have returned nothing - silently, with no error. Bus write-event tracing is now wired for every AddressSpace16/32 board (region-tagged and CPU-agnostic, recorded via watch_write plus an explicit trace_bus_io_write for the separate I/O space); only the Namco boards still use their older hand-rolled path. See the mid-frame-raster work and the follow-up j55q for unifying Namco onto AddressSpace16.

WHY IT MATTERS: event-trace is CPU-agnostic and region-tagged, which makes it strictly better than watchpoints for questions like which video registers are written and WHEN within a frame. It is also mirror-resolving - the Satan's Hollow palette is written through a VRAM mirror at 0xFF80 that an address-exact watchpoint on the 0xEF80 base simply misses.

Together with the watchpoint child, this is what would let a script express the Tier A/B classification audit (docs/designs/mid-frame-raster-audit.md) that v1 cannot.
close_reason:
Bound the event-trace stream and the hang detector into the script surface. Purely additive (no core/board edits) — DebugTrace (set_trace_enabled/trace_events/clear_trace_events) is on the machine bundle, HangDetector is a standalone PC-sampling util.

DebugSession: set_trace/trace_enabled/take_events (events drained from the machine's finite ring into a session accumulator after each frame/step); detect_hangs(window,threshold)/take_hangs (run_frames samples each CPU's PC once per frame and feeds HangDetector). rhai: trace/trace_enabled/events, detect_hangs (Dig Dug defaults or explicit)/hangs. events() returns an array of maps {cycle,kind,source,cpu,pc,addr,value,width,region,device,detail}; hangs() {cpu,pc,window_lo,window_hi,frames_stuck}.

Tests: stub now emits one bus event per frame while tracing, and its fixed PC makes a perpetual hang — 5 stub unit tests cover events-across-frames, trace-disabled-silent, and the hang report. Gated integration test on real Satan's Hollow (shollow, a fully-traced AS16 board — NOT Namco) proves region-tagged CPU-agnostic capture: 1 attract frame yields ~1495 events tagged mem wr/io wr with regions NVRAM/Sprite RAM/Video RAM; asserts region-tagged + write events present, drains, and stops when disabled. Skips cleanly w/o ROMs. clippy+fmt clean; 30 unit + 3 integration green.

With .8 (watchpoints), this is the surface the epic said would let a script express the Tier A/B raster audit v1 couldn't. NOTE: Namco boards (galaga/xevious/digdug) still use the older hand-rolled trace path (see j55q) — event trace is thin there; use a fully-AS16 board for register-timing work.

title: disasm trace --cpu logs a phantom instruction when an interrupt is taken
description:
At an instruction boundary where the CPU takes an interrupt instead of
executing, the cycle loop still emits an instruction line for the PC it was
sitting on. The instruction never executes, but the trace claims it did.

Measured on esb: 405 phantom lines in 123 frames. Example (frame 55):

  cyc 2045946  pc=A366  STD ,U++      <- executes, 8 cycles
  cyc 2045954  pc=A368  CMPU #$3000   <- PHANTOM, never executes
  cyc 2045973  pc=6005  LEAU ,S       <- IRQ handler

2045973 - 2045954 = 19, exactly the 6809 IRQ sequence, so no CMPU ran.

Why it matters beyond cosmetics: it makes the trace unusable for
index-aligned diffs against another emulator, because every interrupt
shifts the index by one. This corrupted the whole j63p investigation --
"first divergence at instruction 454,189" was this artifact, not a real
divergence, and the conclusion drawn from it (that the reset-cycle fix was
inert) was wrong. With phantoms filtered the same fix moves the first
divergence from 454,189 to 462,362.

The cycle loop emits a line whenever `debug_tick()` reports an instruction
boundary, and our M6809 is still at a boundary (ExecState::Fetch) on the
cycle it decides to take an interrupt. The tracer needs to distinguish
"boundary, about to execute" from "boundary, about to vector".

A workaround while this is open: drop any line whose successor is the
interrupt vector target exactly 19 cycles later (6809). That is a heuristic,
not a fix.
close_reason: Fixed in c0c23d6. Added DebugCpu::debug_servicing_interrupt (default false, implemented for M6809); the trace cycle loop now treats an instruction boundary as provisional and confirms it on the next cycle, dropping anything that vectored. --break-pc is confirmed the same way and still reports the boundary's cycle. Verified: esb 123-frame trace drops 1017412 -> 1017006 lines (-406 phantoms), the legitimate CMPU at the frame-55 interrupt survives (24 cycles = 5 + 19) while the phantom (19) is gone, and --break-pc still stops at 41649243. 2 regression tests in core/tests/m6809_interrupt_test.rs cover both directions.

title: rhai: tag script/frontend memory pokes as DebugAccessSource::Frontend in the event trace
description:
Follow-up from phosphor-emulator-rhai-scripting-yrwn.7 (which landed the memory-poke CAPABILITY only). Pokes currently forward to BusDebug::write and are NOT tagged in the event trace, so they can't be distinguished from hardware writes when a trace is recorded.

WORK: record a DebugAccessSource::Frontend event when a poke happens, so pokes surface in the event trace instead of masquerading as hardware state. BusDebug::poke (added in .7 as a default forwarding to write) is the override seam.

SCOPE NOTE (learned in .7): this is NOT a contained change. BusDebug is hand-written per board (e.g. galaga's write calls map.write_backing, the same method the CPU hot-path uses) or derived via #[derive(BusDebug)]. Tagging requires: an AddressSpace16/32 poke that records the Frontend event, changing the derive's write/poke arm centrally, and fixing each hand-written board (galaga, standalone simple* machines). Only observable once a script/console can record+read a trace, so best done WITH .9 (event-trace access) and/or .11 (interactive console).
close_reason:
Pokes are now tagged DebugAccessSource::Frontend in the event trace. Turned out MORE tractable than .7's scope note feared.

CORE: AddressSpace16::poke and AddressSpace32::poke record a Frontend-tagged MemoryWrite event (region-tagged, detail 'frontend poke') into the trace ring when tracing is on, then do the backing write; watchpoints are intentionally not fired (a poke is a debugger action, not machine execution).

DERIVE: #[derive(BusDebug)] now generates fn poke routing each CPU's write to the address space's tagged poke (mirrors the write arm). No board uses explicit debug_cpu write methods, so this covers ALL 21 derived boards centrally (williams/namco_pac/mcr2/mrdo/gottlieb/atari*/... — including shollow via mcr2).

NAMCO: galaga/digdug/xevious hand-write BusDebug; added a matching fn poke override routing RAM ranges to board.map.poke. Their DebugTrace surfaces the SAME map ring, so pokes tag+surface there too (the scope note worried they might not — verified they do).

BusDebug::poke default still forwards to write untagged, for machines with no address space (minimal test rigs).

VERIFIED end-to-end on real ROMs: m.trace(true); m.poke(0,0x8000,0xAA); m.events() yields exactly one source=='frontend' mem-wr event at 0x8000=0xAA — on mrdo (derived, region 'BG Video RAM') AND galaga (Namco, region 'Video RAM'). Gated integration test frontend_poke_is_tagged_in_the_trace (mrdo) asserts this. Docs updated (core BusDebug::poke doc + script README no longer call the tagging a pending follow-up). fmt+clippy clean; core/macros/machines + phosphor-script (36 unit + gated) + frontend (25) all green.

Closes the last open work in the Rhai scripting epic.

title: phosphor-script: inline script source (-e) so one-off runs need no temp file
description:
phosphor-script run requires `script: PathBuf` (tools/script/src/main.rs:31-39) and run_script reads it with fs::read_to_string (:74). There is no way to pass source inline, so any one-off — take a screenshot, poke an address, check a PC — costs a temp file plus a second command. That friction is the only real argument left for growing the CLI surface of `disasm frameshot` (it has --coin-at but no --press/--move). We decided NOT to add input flags there: script + `disasm imgdiff` already covers the whole capture-and-compare regression workflow, and a flag mini-language can express "move for 60 frames from frame 200" but never "move until the ball reaches the ramp". Making the script path frictionless is the higher-leverage version of the same fix — it improves every script use, not just captures. Target: phosphor-script run -e $(printf %s "m.run_frames(300); m.input_relative(\"p1_trackball_x\", 4.0); m.screenshot(\"x.png\")") --machine marble ~/ws/mame-runtime/roms Work: - Accept inline source alongside the file path; exactly one of the two must be given. - run_script currently formats errors as `{script.display()}: {e}` (:96). Inline source needs a stand-in label (e.g. ``) so the message still reads sensibly. - Consider `-` as a third form (read source from stdin), which composes with heredocs and pipes. DESIGN DECISION TO MAKE FIRST — positional ambiguity. `Run` currently has TWO positionals in order: `script` (:33) then `rompath` (:38). If `script` merely becomes optional, clap binds the first positional to it, so `run -e "..." --machine marble ROMS` puts ROMS in `script` and leaves rompath empty. Options: (a) add a named `--rompath` alongside the positional (keeps existing invocations working; the positional stays for the file form), (b) require `--rompath` when `-e` is used, (c) make it a separate subcommand — `phosphor-script eval "" --machine --rompath

` — leaving `run` untouched. (c) is the least invasive and has no ambiguity; (a) is friendlier if inline becomes the common path. Decide before writing code — this is the whole design risk in the issue. Also update tools/script/README.md, which documents the runner invocation. Not part of the control-handling or dry-refactors epics; it belongs with the Rhai scripting work (~/rhai-scripting.md). Gate: cargo test -p phosphor-script, plus a manual one-liner run against a real ROM set confirming both forms (file and inline) still work and that a missing/both-supplied source errors cleanly.
close_reason: phosphor-script run now takes source from a file, -e <SOURCE>, or - (stdin). Chose context-sensitive positionals over a separate eval subcommand: with -e the sole positional is the rompath, without it the first is the script and the second the rompath, and --rompath names it explicitly either way. Existing invocations unchanged. Errors label the source <inline>/<stdin>; both-supplied and missing-source cases error cleanly. Verified against marble/galaga ROMs.

title: Epic: Make the existing test suite bite
description:
3,165 tests pass, but several of the highest-value guarantees are either vacuous or opt-in. This epic fixes the tests that exist rather than adding new categories (golden frames are a separate epic).

Theme: the registry-wide input contract test (machines/tests/input_contract_test.rs) is the pattern to copy — it iterates registry::all(), so a new machine cannot silently skip it. Two of the three children are about applying that same idea elsewhere.
close_reason: All three children done. The registry-driven pattern from input_contract_test now also covers live-machine contracts, save-state round trips, and ROM-gated boot verdicts, via a ROM-less MachineEntry::create_bare. Fixed 5 real defects the new tests found: three crashes on garbage execution (MB88xx PA overflow, Galaxian unmapped-decode hole, Crystal Castles scanline underflow) and two Gottlieb save-state omissions. Design doc: docs/designs/test-suite-depth.md.

title: Save-state round-trip tests are vacuous — exercise a machine that has run
description:
machines/tests/save_state_tests.rs:19-29 saves a machine, loads into a fresh instance, re-saves and compares bytes — on a machine that has never run a frame. Both sides sit at power-on defaults, so any field that only diverges after execution serializes identically in both directions.

The suite therefore cannot detect the bug it exists for: a device runtime counter missing from save_state passes all 19 machines today.

Fix: run N frames -> save -> run M more -> load the save -> run M more -> assert the two post-load framebuffers and CPU states match. That form catches omitted fields.

Machines whose new() boots without ROMs can do this with no ROM dependency; the rest become ROM-gated.

Acceptance: deliberately deleting a field from a board's Saveable impl makes the test fail.
close_reason: Replaced the vacuous round trip with a differential test: several instances with different pre-load histories load the same snapshot, replay frames, and must agree on frame, audio and state. Registry-driven over all 40 machines; harness/tests/save_state_rom_test.rs runs the same protocol on machines booted from real ROMs. Verified by hand-breaking Saveable impls (dropping GalaxianSound fails the ROM-less test, dropping GalaxianVideo fails the ROM-gated one). Found and fixed two real omissions in the Gottlieb board.

title: Registry-driven machine contract tests via a ROM-less constructor
description:
machines/tests/save_state_tests.rs:64-103 is a hand-maintained list: 19 machines out of roughly 40 registered. Star Wars, Tempest, Quantum, Marble Madness, Road Runner, I Robot, Mr. Do, Congo Bongo, Mario Bros. and the Galaxian family are absent — not by decision, but because adding a machine does not add a row.

MachineEntry::create needs a RomSet, which is why contract tests currently either hand-list machines or (input_contract_test) restrict themselves to the static control table.

Fix: add a ROM-less constructor to MachineEntry so registry-driven tests can instantiate every machine, then move onto it:
- save-state round trip (sibling issue)
- DIP bank validity (assert_dip_banks_valid — today invoked per machine via dip_test_suite!)
- orientation/display_size sanity (non-zero, aspect consistent with the declared orientation)

Acceptance: a newly registered machine is covered by all of the above without touching a test file. Add a guard like input_contract_test's the_registry_is_not_empty so the suite cannot pass vacuously.
close_reason: Added MachineEntry::create_bare plus RomSet::blank() so every registered machine can be built with no ROMs; machines/tests/machine_contract_test.rs now drives 14 identity/display/timing/DIP/execution checks off registry::all() with a the_registry_is_not_empty guard. assert_dip_banks_valid is public so DIP validity covers all 40 machines rather than only those invoking dip_test_suite!.

title: Promote the examples/ boot checks into ROM-gated tests
description:
Ten programs under machines/examples/ (starwars, esb, marble, roadrunner, xevious, galaxian, asteroids, dkong, llander, plus captures) encode real knowledge — e.g. xevious_boot_check reports whether the sub/sound CPUs were released, which is how you know the 50XX protection handshake succeeded. They print their verdict rather than asserting it, and nothing runs them.

Fix: move the assertions into ROM-gated #[test]s that skip without ROMs (roms_dir() from phosphor-harness), keeping the examples as the interactive/diagnostic front end.

Acceptance: with ROMs present, cargo test catches a regression that stops any of these machines reaching its game loop.
close_reason: harness/tests/boot_check_test.rs asserts the six boot-check examples' verdicts (starwars, esb, xevious, marble, roadrunner, the Galaxian family) plus a registry-driven check that every machine with ROMs draws and moves a CPU off its reset PC — 39 of 40 locally. Examples stay as the interactive front end and cross-reference their test. The five capture programs are not promoted: they dump a WAV/PNG for an external analyzer and carry no verdict.

title: Verify dorunrun + dowild against real ROMs
description: dorunrun.zip and dowild.zip are not in ~/ws/mame-runtime/roms, so both variants shipped implemented-but-unverified. Once the ROM sets are available: boot each, check attract mode, colours (256B PROM vs docastle's 512B), ROT0 orientation, the 0xFF00 front-tilemap transmask, the split 0000-1FFF + 4000-9FFF map, sub latch at E000, SN ports at A000-AC00, and the per-variant DIP tables. dorunrun's attract-mode demo sequence is the sensitive timing check — the driver documents the expected first 12 rounds for the dorunrun2 set.
close_reason: Verified both against real ROMs (dorunrun.zip / dowild.zip). Both boot, run attract, accept coin+start and play. Checked: ROT0 landscape, 256-byte PROM colours, the split 0000-1FFF + 4000-9FFF map, sub latch at E000, all four SN ports at A000-AC00 driven by the sub CPU (~20k writes over 6000 frames), the 0xFF00 front-tilemap transmask (A/B'd against docastle's 0x00FF, which makes every sprite vanish behind the tilemap), per-variant DIP tables (dowild title coinage line follows Coin A/B; dorunrun bit-7 Lives shows 2 vs 4 spare-life icons for 3 vs 5), main+sub disassembly, and tile-sheet decode. 6000-frame soak on each with no hang. No code changes were needed. Note: dorunrun's power-on graphics test runs ~2500 frames and looks like broken video - it is not.

Per repo 'no MAME in code comments' rule, describe as TMS5220 tables; cite MAME only in the commit. Unit-test sizes + spot values.

title: TMS5220 device core: variant + FIFO + command decode + host-agnostic handshake
description: Rewrite core/src/device/tms5220.rs preserving the existing public API. Add Tms52xxVariant {Tms5220, Tms5220C}; constructors new() (=5220C @650.8kHz nominal) and with_variant(v, clock_hz). data_w command decode by bits 6-4: SPEAK EXTERNAL (0x60) clears FIFO + arms speak-external; RESET (0x70) stops + clears; SET RATE stored only when 5220C; VSM commands (LA/SPK/RDBY/RB) decoded and no-op'd; else push a data byte. 16-byte FIFO + head/tail/count/bits_taken + read_bits(n). status_r (TS/BL/BE), ready()/int_asserted() from FIFO fullness/stop. set_clock(hz) (retunes resampler input=clk/80). Saveable (#[save_skip] tables/clock/resampler) + Device + Debuggable. Host-agnostic: no 6522/RIOT knowledge, no Atari PB4 math in the device. Silent handshake only; synthesis is the next child. Tests: FIFO fullness->ready/BL/BE, command decode, SET RATE variant-gated, save/load.
close_reason: Rewrote the TMS5220 stub into a host-agnostic device core: Tms52xxVariant {Tms5220, Tms5220C} + new()/with_variant(v, clock_hz); data_w command decode (SPEAK EXTERNAL/RESET/SET-RATE gated to 5220C/VSM inert), 16-byte FIFO with BL-edge SPEN start, BL/BE status + /INT edges, status_r (clears /INT), ready()/int_asserted(), set_clock(hz) retuning the resampler (clock/80). #[derive(Saveable)] runtime state (variant/clock/resampler skipped) + Device + Debuggable. Silent until synthesis (child .3): drain_audio empty, tick no-op. Handshake ported from MAME tms5220.cpp. 11 device tests + tables pass; clippy/fmt clean; machines builds. One commit on branch tms5220.

title: TMS5220 LPC synthesis (parse/interp/lattice/excitation/audio)
description: Port MAME tms5220.cpp synthesis into the device: parse_frame (4-bit energy, repeat bit, 6-bit pitch, K1-K10 by bit width; stop on energy 0/15; unvoiced when pitch 0), interpolation via INTERP_SHIFT[IP] unless inhibited, excitation (chirp table when voiced / 20x-per-sample 16-bit LFSR when unvoiced), unrolled 10-pole lattice_filter with clamped matrix_multiply, clip. tick() = one master clock with a /80 prescaler stepping one synthesis sample into AudioResampler<f32> (->44100); consume FIFO bits as frames parse; assert/clear talk. Real drain_audio(). Tests: known LPC frame -> non-empty non-DC audio; silence/stop frame stays quiet.
close_reason: LPC synthesis complete (2 commits on branch tms5220). (A) FIFO bit-reader (read_bits, LSB/MSB order) + parse_frame (energy/rep/pitch/K1-K4/K5-K10 with silence/stop/repeat/unvoiced early-outs) + full synthesizer state (save_version 2) + idle-frame/zpar/OLDE/OLDP setup on speak-external and SPEN start; TALK separated from TALKD. (B) process_one_sample state machine (frame parse at cycle boundary, interpolation-inhibit, INTERP_SHIFT B-cycle interpolation of energy/pitch/K, chirp/20x-LFSR excitation, unrolled 10-pole lattice_filter + matrix_multiply + clip_analog), advance_counters (RESETF3/RESETL4 TALKD+OLDE/OLDP latching, pitch counter), tick() ÷80 -> resampler, real drain_audio; Device::tick wired. Ported from MAME tms5220.cpp. Tests: bit order, voiced/unvoiced/stop parse round-trips, idle-silent, voiced-audible-varying; full core suite 833 pass; clippy/fmt clean.

title: Wire TMS5220 into Atari System 1 sound board (Road Runner speech)
description: machines/src/atari_system1_sound.rs (VIA6522 bridge kept). PB4 clock select computed board-side: on Port B write extract D4 and tms.set_clock(7_159_090/(16-(5|(bit4<<1)))) -> 650.8kHz (D4=0) or 795.5kHz (D4=1). Add a u64 fractional accumulator and, in tick(), step speech.tms.tick() for the (variable) TMS master clock vs SOUND_CLOCK_HZ (Bresenham). In drain_audio() drain speech and add to POKEY+YM mix (bipolar, gain ~1.0, tune vs MAME), guarded on speech.is_some(). Construct as 5220C via new(). Marble (speech off) byte-identical. Verify the via6522.rs stub suffices for a pure parallel-port bridge (confirm RR sound ROM doesn't need VIA timers/CA-CB); note any upgrade. Tests: streaming keeps /READY toggling without stalling, PB4 retunes, Marble parity.
close_reason: Wired the TMS5220 into AtariSystem1Sound (VIA6522 bridge kept). Port B bit4 clock-select retunes the TMS master clock (tms_clock_for_pb4: 650.8kHz nominal / 795.5kHz) via set_clock; Speech::tick steps the TMS at its variable clock vs the 6502 via a Bresenham accumulator; drain_audio mixes TMS output (SPEECH_MIX, tunable) with POKEY+YM. Marble (speech=None) byte-identical (no tick; +0.0 mix). Save state round-trips selected clock + accumulator and re-syncs the TMS resampler on load. 3 new tests (clock math, PB4 retune, ticks-drain-FIFO); 13 atari sound tests pass; full machines suite green; clippy --all-targets + fmt clean. 2 commits on branch tms5220 (+ isolated chore fixing a pre-existing galaxian_boot_check clippy identity_op). VIA6522 stub confirmed sufficient as a parallel-port bridge. End-to-end Road Runner audio verification is child .6/.5.

title: Road Runner speech end-to-end verification + docs
description: Run the frontend on roadrunn and listen for intelligible speech in attract/gameplay. Optional MAME diff: Lua-tap tms5220_device::data_w and diff the byte/command stream vs ours before chasing audio-quality differences (per the 'diff against MAME bus traffic' memory). Update README/roadmap. cargo test -p phosphor-core + -p phosphor-machines, clippy --all-features --all-targets, fmt clean. Relates to t9r.6.
close_reason: End-to-end verified: user confirms Road Runner speech now plays correctly. Root cause of the initially slow/choppy speech was NOT the TMS device but AudioResampler only supporting downsampling — the TMS at clock/80 (~8.1kHz) upsamples to 44.1kHz and the resampler degenerated to pass-through (~8135 samples/sec), airing ~1/5 of each frame then silence. Fixed AudioResampler::tick to emit one output per consumed input period (loop; sample-and-hold on upsampling), which also fixes Votrax's inaudible 1.1x error. README updated (Road Runner: TMS5220 LPC speech, not stub). Full core (835) + machines suites, clippy --all-targets, fmt clean. Optional MAME data_w Lua diff skipped — user-confirmed by ear. Commits on branch tms5220.

title: Galaga 54XX discrete explosion sound
description:
Model the Namco 54XX (MB8844) explosion-sound generator and its discrete analog output so Galaga's shooting/explosion effects are audible. Currently the 54XX is stubbed: commands sent via 06XX chip-select 3 are discarded at machines/src/namco_galaga.rs:771 and explosions are silent; only the WSG melodic/effect voices play.

Scope (this issue builds the SHARED 54XX component that Xevious also needs):
- LLE the 54XX on the existing mb88xx core (core/src/cpu/mb88xx). Model it after core/src/device/namco51_lle.rs: load 54xx.bin (ships in galaga.zip/xevious.zip), drive command bytes in via the 06XX write path, run the MCU on its machine-cycle divider.
- Convert the 54XX's ~3-bit output through the discrete DAC + op-amp filter network (MAME galaga.c/bosco audio: bosco_54xx_dac R-1 ladder + op-amp filters) into a 44.1 kHz signal. Build on core/src/device/discrete/ (see docs/designs/discrete-sound-framework.md) rather than hard-coding samples.
- Replace the discarded chip-select-3 seam in namco_galaga.rs with the real 54XX write path; add the 54XX channel to the board audio mix alongside the WSG.
- Tests: 54XX command->response/MCU-step (cross-validate against the mb88xx tooling), and a machine-level check that a Galaga explosion command produces non-silent output.

Timings/datasheet take precedence over MAME per project convention; keep MAME refs in commit/PR, not source comments.

title: Concrete bus dispatch: Quantum and Star Wars
description:
The two standalone machines left over from hv5p (the Atari DVG/AVG family). Neither uses AtariDvgBoard, so neither fits the board-plus-view shape the other three took; both need their own split.

Quantum (machines/src/quantum.rs, ~1200 lines): M68000 + AVG + 2x POKEY, all in one QuantumSystem struct with 'impl Bus for QuantumSystem' and two 'bus_split!(self, bus: u32 word)' sites. Its Bus impl touches ~10 fields (map, avg, pokey, nvram, color_ram, track_x/y, system_input, irq_pending, watchdog_count) plus helper methods (trigger_avg, led_w), so a per-field view would be wide. Prefer nesting the bus state into a QuantumBus field (the shape the design doc calls out for standalone machines) over a 10-borrow view.

Star Wars (machines/src/starwars.rs, ~2700 lines): two 6502s (main + sound) on its own StarWarsBoard, AVG, POKEY/RIOT/TMS5220, ADC0809 yoke, X2212 NVRAM. Seven bus_split! sites. Note debug_pre_tick services a pending sound-CPU reset and explicitly needs a bus for the reset-vector fetch -- with the generic Cpu::reset (bek7) that becomes straightforward, and the comment there about run_frame being 'where bus_split! yields a bus' should be updated.

Both are M6502/M68000, so both depend on bek7 (done). Follow the conventions in docs/designs/concrete-bus-dispatch.md: machines expose step_cycle/bus_read/bus_write, board-level device-index tests move up to the machine, and measure with phosphor-bench before and after (asteroids/tempest are the nearest comparables at 1.5 MHz).

Split out of hv5p, which converted Asteroids, Asteroids Deluxe and Lunar Lander in 6cfbd9b.
close_reason:
Done in 422ca0f (quantum + starwars/esb).

Numbers (phosphor-bench, release, 400f x 5 reps, best of 6 alternating runs, idle host):
  quantum  1.413 -> 1.145 ms/f  -19.0%
  starwars 3.968 -> 3.448       -13.1%
Quantum is the largest single gain of the rollout so far: a 68000 whose frame is almost entirely CPU cycles, previously dispatching every *word* access through a trait object. It is also the first user of the u32/u16 wide bus to convert -- and nothing about the conversion was width-specific, exactly as the design doc predicted the bus_split! arms would turn out.

Shapes:
- Quantum had no board at all (CPU, map, AVG, POKEYs, NVRAM, I/O in one struct). Introduced QuantumBoard for the bus state, leaving QuantumSystem { cpu, board }; the Bus impl moved to the board unchanged. ~120 field references rewritten to self.board.*, which is the churn the design doc warns standalone machines carry.
- Star Wars kept its board and moved both 6809s up. The board already carried the variant differences (Empire's slapstic window and bank), so it implements Bus and IS the bus for both registered machines.

Nice side effect: the deferred sound-CPU reset (E0) stops being awkward. It existed as a deferred flag because the reset fetches a vector through the bus, which only run_frame could produce via bus_split!, with debug_pre_tick mirroring it for the cycle-stepped paths. With the CPU beside the bus it is a plain call, and both paths now route through one function.

The ROM-gated boot check earned its keep: Star Wars' hand-written MachineDebug::debug_bus still returned the board, which no longer owns the CPUs, so Empire failed with 'exposes no CPUs through its debug bus'. Golden frames could not have caught it -- the picture is identical either way. Worth remembering for the remaining conversions: any hand-written MachineDebug needs its debug_bus repointed at the machine.

Golden frames unchanged for all pinned machines; machine, harness and ROM-gated suites pass; clippy and fmt clean.

22 files still reference bus_split!, all in the 3hnp (Atari System 1 + Gottlieb) and 642d (standalone) buckets.

title: Satan's Hollow: model the SSIO sound-board DIP (coinage)
description: Satan's Hollow's only user DIP is the SSIO sound board's 8 switches (set via ssio.set_dip_switches, read by the SSIO sound CPU at 0xF000; default 0x81). MAME treats this port as 8 IPT_UNKNOWN switches for every MCR game — the coin/option meaning is interpreted by the SSIO sound ROM, with no documented per-bit layout — so the DipSwitches impl is currently left empty (see comment in satans_hollow.rs). To expose it: derive the MCR SSIO coinage scheme (operator manual / SSIO firmware analysis) and add a DipSwitchBank, or expose the 8 raw switches as a fallback. Also consider the game-side IP3 DIPs (Coin Meters, Cabinet) which sit on a separate SSIO input port, not the persisted DIP byte.

title: M6809: don't-care cycles outside indexed addressing still drive nothing
description:
ROOT CAUSE of phosphor-emulator-j63p (ESB watchdog reset).

The MC6809E drives $FFFF on its don't-care (/VMA) cycles. Ours drives
nothing at all. ESB's slapstic depends on that address, so the dependency is
not academic.

HOW IT BREAKS ESB. The $829B trampoline re-selects the CURRENT bank -- each
bank holds its own copy:
    bank 0 JMP $8080   bank 1 JMP $8090   bank 2 JMP $80A0   bank 3 JMP $80B0
and $9174 differs per bank:
    bank 0 BITA #$10   bank 1 STA 6,X     bank 2 RTS         bank 3 BHI $9176

MAME (0.287, gameplay, traced) executes bank 1's `$829B JMP $8090` and then
lands on bank 2's `$9174 RTS` -- so the bank changes 1 -> 2 between them
WITHOUT any access to $80A0. The only mechanism that can do that is the
chip's ALT sequence committing bank 2, and the callee's `LDX #$9B5E` /
`LDA 0,X` reads $9B5E, which is exactly the alt_select range
(test_in 0x1FFC/0x1B5C) with the low bits encoding bank 2.

Our alt sequence never completes. Traced with the new state instrumentation:
    41750126  $9E00 -> alt-valid    (alt_start matched)
    41750128  $9E01 -> active       (BROKEN at the valid step)
The valid step needs an access with (addr & 0x1FFF) == 0x1FFF from OUTSIDE
the window -- i.e. $FFFF, a don't-care cycle. We never drive it, so the
sequence always breaks, the game never gets bank 2 by the alt path, and the
return lands in bank 1 where $9174 is `STA 6,X` instead of `RTS`.

MAME's 6809 does drive it: m6809.h:217
    inline void dummy_vma(int count) { for(...) { read_opcode_arg(0xffff); } }
and its .lst uses dummy_vma at 17 sites. Note this is DISTINCT from
dummy_read_opcode_arg(0), which reads at PC -- I conflated the two earlier
and tested the PC variant, which correctly changed nothing.

Our own slapstic doc comment already predicted this: "the alt sequence's 2nd
(valid) access must land *outside* the window (in practice a 6809 dummy VMA
access)".

SCOPE OF THE FIX. Every don't-care cycle in the M6809 should drive $FFFF,
not just the indexed ones. A partial experiment adding it only to the
indexed internal cycle did NOT fix ESB, because the break happens at $9E00's
ASLA, whose internal cycle is a different path. So this needs doing across
the instruction set.

Note commit 9706bbc moved us AWAY from this: it replaced TST's three
`bus.read(0xFFFF)` don't-care cycles with internal cycles, on the reading
that the datasheet's "don't-care($FFFF)" meant no bus activity. It means the
opposite -- the address bus IS driven to $FFFF. That commit should be
revisited as part of this.

Cross-validation impact: bus traces will gain these accesses, so the m6809
vectors need regenerating, and the reference core (mame0148) may model them
differently from the modern one.
notes:
2026-08-09 — retitled; the original claim is now only partly true.

Fixed in c08770a, and it fixed phosphor-emulator-j63p: the indexed
postbyte-resolution don't-cares read at PC, and `alu_indexed`'s base internal
cycle drives $FFFF. No cycle counts changed — these were existing silent
cycles.

STILL OPEN, and worth keeping for two reasons rather than one:

1. Every other don't-care cycle in the instruction set is still silent —
   inherent-mode internal cycles, the direct/extended address-computation
   cycles, RMW, the interrupt entry sequence, RTS/PULS. Any address-snooping
   device sees a bus the hardware would not present. The slapstic games on
   Atari System 1 (Marble Madness 103, Road Runner 108) are the obvious
   exposure, and neither is verified against a reference in this respect.

2. Commit 9706bbc is probably a regression and should be revisited on its
   own merits. It replaced TST's three `bus.read(0xFFFF)` don't-care cycles
   with silent internal cycles, reasoning that the datasheet's
   "don't-care($FFFF)" meant no bus activity. The ESB result is direct
   evidence it means the opposite: the address bus IS driven to $FFFF, and
   the slapstic depends on it. That commit made one machine's fidelity worse
   to satisfy a reading the hardware contradicts.

No known game currently depends on the remainder, so P2 rather than higher —
but (2) is a wrong-direction change sitting in the tree, not merely absent
work.
close_reason:
Every don't-care cycle in the M6809 now drives an address, and 9706bbc's
direction is reversed.

The reference is MAME's m6809.lst/base6x09.lst, which distinguishes two kinds of
don't-care cycle where the datasheet's blanket 'don't-care($FFFF)' does not:
dummy_vma() holds $FFFF, dummy_read_opcode_arg() re-drives PC. The ESB result
already showed the blanket reading was too coarse, so where the two disagree the
per-cycle split wins.

WHAT NOW DRIVES THE BUS
- Direct and extended address computation -> $FFFF
- The RMW modify cycle -> PC (TST -> $FFFF)
- TST direct/indexed/extended final cycle -> $FFFF, reversing 9706bbc
- Inherent register ops (NEG/COM/INC/DEC/CLR/shifts/rotates, NOP, DAA, SEX,
  ABX, MUL) -> PC; inherent TSTA/TSTB -> $FFFF
- The trailing cycle of every 16-bit ALU op -> PC
- TFR/EXG, branches and long branches, JMP, LEA -> $FFFF
- BSR/LBSR/JSR: their don't-cares now all precede the two pushes, as on the part
- Interrupt/SWI entry: PC, PC, $FFFF, and the vector fetch bracketed by $FFFF.
  The cycle that detects the interrupt is the first of those PC cycles
- Indexed: the leading don't-cares re-drive PC and the rest hold $FFFF, per
  mode. D,R is the one mode with two, at PC+0 then PC+1

Pull sequences (RTS, RTI, PULS/PULU) close on a real read at the settled stack
pointer and pushes (PSHS/PSHU) open on a real read at the stack top; those are
memory accesses, not don't-cares, and were silent before.

CYCLE COUNTS ARE UNCHANGED. Every one of the 266,000 single-step vectors reports
the same total cycle count as before across all 266 opcodes — nothing was added
or removed, only given an address, and the four instructions whose cycles were
reordered (rmw_indexed, indexed 16-bit ALU, BSR/LBSR/JSR) kept their length.

VERIFIED
- 4,150 workspace tests pass (phosphor-disasm's test target does not build on
  main either; filed as phosphor-emulator-kd9b)
- Cross-validation 264,132/266,000, all 1,868 failures the known extended-
  indirect +3 divergence and nothing else; baseline was 264,090 on a different
  random draw
- ESB 4,000 frames: same PC, zero hangs, same 405/405 slapstic bank switches as
  the pre-change build, cycle for cycle
- starwars/joust/robotron/gridlee/irobot 1,200 frames each: PC and hang counts
  identical to the pre-change build
- core/tests/m6809_dont_care_cycle_test.rs, 18 new tests, asserts the whole bus
  trace of representative instructions so a cycle that moves relative to a real
  access fails too

FOLLOW-UPS FILED (both out of this issue's scope — neither is a silent cycle)
- phosphor-emulator-ks1q: CWAI and the CWAI-wake vector path are short of cycles
- phosphor-emulator-5dgc: indexed indirect emits its don't-cares after the
  pointer read instead of before

title: Do Castle: the main Z80 is cloned every T-state for the WAIT rewind
description:
docastle::step_main takes a full Z80 snapshot (main.clone()) before every main-CPU T-state, so the latch-read rewind can undo it:

    let snapshot = main.clone();
    main.execute_cycle(board, BusMaster::Cpu(0));
    if board.main_retry { *main = snapshot; ... }

That is a ~100-byte struct copy on each of ~66,000 cycles per frame, and the rewind it exists for fires only on the handful of cycles that hit the shared latch window.

Found while converting the board to concrete bus dispatch (f38e13a). The conversion measured only -4.1% (docastle) / -3.3% (dorunrun) against 12-27% on comparable Z80 boards, because most of a Do Castle frame is not bus dispatch: this clone plus four SN76489A PSGs serviced every cycle.

Options worth measuring:
- Snapshot lazily: only clone when the cycle is about to touch the latch window. The board knows the window (MAIN_LATCH_BASE..+LATCH_WINDOW_LEN) but not the address before the CPU issues it, so this may need the CPU to expose 'about to read address X' or the board to set a flag from the read itself and rewind from a cheaper record.
- Snapshot only the fields the rewind restores, if that is a strict subset.
- Have the Z80 support an explicit 'retry this T-state' rather than a whole-state rollback.

Any change here must keep the LDIR handshake test passing (main_latch_read_stalls_then_samples_the_sub_cpu_value and the nine-byte boot handshake), and be measured with phosphor-bench on docastle.

title: Implement Xevious on the Namco Galaga platform
description:
Add Xevious (Namco, 1983) as a new game on the shared NamcoGalagaBoard (namco_galaga.rs), reusing the 3x Z80 + WSG + 06XX infrastructure alongside Galaga and Dig Dug.

Xevious differs from Galaga/Dig Dug in three confirmed ways:
1. Custom chips: drops the 53XX, adds the 50XX (MB8842 protection MCU, boot-critical) and 54XX (MB8844 explosion-sound MCU). DIPs are read directly at 0x6800 (bosco_dsw_r), not via a custom chip.
2. Three graphics layers: scrolling background tilemap + foreground text tilemap + 3bpp 16x16 sprites, with independent per-layer X/Y scroll (0xD000 latch).
3. Background tile data lives in ROM, addressed via a hardware lookup (xevious_bb_r/xevious_bs_w at 0xF000, 'schematic 9B').

De-risker: xevious.zip ships the 50xx/51xx/54xx MCU dumps, and the repo already has an mb88xx core + LLE example (namco51_lle.rs), so the 50XX protection can be done LLE with no reverse-engineering.

Delivery: staged milestones (M1 boot, M2 video, M3 input/sound/tests). 54XX explosion sound stubbed silent initially; WSG melodic/effect sound works from M1.

Full design: ~/.claude/plans/plan-to-implement-xevious-sleepy-teacup.md
close_reason: Xevious ships on the shared Namco Galaga board across all three milestones: M1 board plumbing + boot (50XX protection cleared — implemented as a behavioural HLE rather than the originally-scoped MB8842 LLE, since the LLE could not be synced to the 06XX handshake; see commit eeeea52), M2 three-layer scrolling video + 3bpp sprites + F000 ROM-lookup background, M3 input/DIPs/WSG sound/tests/docs. WSG melodic+effect audio works and is verified against the real ROM; the 54XX explosion channel is stubbed silent with a documented seam for a future discrete network + LLE. All descendant issues closed.

title: Xevious: sound CPU runs away and clears misc latch, stalling attract
description:
Xevious boots through the power-on RAM test and PASSES the 50XX start-up protection into its main game loop (~frame 635, main PC 0x0437). It then stalls: the sound CPU (Cpu 2) writes the LS259 misc latch Q0=0 and Q3=0 (observed via bus-master trace), which disables the main VBLANK IRQ and re-holds the sub/sound CPUs in reset. The main loop at 0x0437 then spins forever waiting for the IRQ handler to set the frame counter at mem[0x8000]=1.

The sound ROM (xvi_7) never writes 0x6820/0x6823 in its reset/init/NMI paths (only Q2 at 0x6822), so the sound CPU has run away and is executing garbage that decodes as those latch writes — likely stack/RAM corruption or wrong NMI timing in the 3-Z80 interleave.

Next step (per repo guidance): trace+diff actual bus/latch traffic against MAME Lua taps rather than reverse-engineering ROM control flow. Reproduce with: cargo run -p phosphor-machines --example xevious_boot_check -- <extracted-xevious-dir> 800. Blocks M1 boot sign-off.
close_reason: FIXED in 0715d05. Root cause (via MAME bus-diff): the board latched the sound CPU's scanline NMI while it was held in reset (LS259 Q3), then delivered it the instant the CPU was released — before it ran its reset vector to load SP. The push went to the reset SP=0xFFFF, which on Xevious maps to the 0xF000-0xFFFF background-ROM window (not RAM), wrecking the stack -> sound CPU runaway that stomped the misc latch. Fix: clear pending sub/sound IRQ/NMI on reset release and don't latch the sound NMI while the CPUs are in reset. Verified: sound CPU now boots cleanly and idles in its command loop; matches MAME (sub2 only ever writes Q2).

title: Xevious: 50XX LLE returns wrong value for periodic protection check -> main reboots
description:
PROGRESS. The reboot is a periodic 50XX score/protection query: main handler 0x3B9E writes commands to the 50XX (06XX ctrl 0x64) and reads a 4-byte response into 0x8060-0x8063 (ctrl 0x74), then at 0x3BBC does LD A,(0x8063)/CP 5/JP NZ,0x0000 -- reboot unless byte3==5. It is a BCD score query: MAME returns {0x80,0x00,0x00,0x05} (byte0=flags, bytes1-3=BCD score 000005).

FIXED so far (3599cb6): the 50XX MB8842 was clocked 6x too fast (namco50_divider was /2 = 1.536 MHz; the MB88xx machine cycle is external/6, and the 50XX external clock is MASTER_CLOCK/6/2 = 1.536 MHz, so the machine cycle is 256 kHz = board/12). At /2 the MCU sat in its output loop (0x0013-0x0023); at /12 it now runs the same command/dispatch loop as MAME (0x04C-0x05A + 0x080-0x081). Only Xevious fits a 50XX so Galaga/Dig Dug are unaffected; all machines tests pass. (Note: the 51XX LLE divider is also /2 and likely wants /12 for the same reason, but it only carries inputs (level signals) so it tolerates the wrong rate; left as-is to avoid Dig Dug regression risk.)

REMAINING: the 50XX response is still {0x00,0x00,0x00,0xFF} (byte3 0xFF = the 4th read finds chip 2 deselected; O=0 on the first three). Command DELIVERY is fine -- MAME sends 0x10 (reset), 0x80 (+5), 0xE5; my MCU receives K=1 (0x10) and K=8 (0x80). But the MCUs internal score RAM stays 0, so the received commands are not applied. So the remaining bug is the fine command-latch handshake timing: WHEN the MCU samples K/R0 relative to the Z80 command write, governed by the 06XX chip-select pulse and the namco06 chip_select_delay (base_divisor cycles), which was tuned for the 51XX at /2 and likely needs adjustment for the 50XX at /12.

Next steps: (1) cycle-level compare of the 50XX MB8842 execution (RAM/registers/O) against MAME during a single command, to see where the score update diverges; (2) tune/verify the 06XX chip_select_delay and the write->chip_select ordering for the 50XX; (3) verify the read handshake outputs all 4 bytes without deselecting on the 4th (the 0xFF). Repro: cargo run -p phosphor-machines --example xevious_boot_check -- <dir> 1600 shows Q3/main cycling. Blocks M1 boot sign-off.
close_reason: FIXED in ed91e91. The 50XX periodic protection check now passes. Root cause chain: (1) 50XX MB8842 was clocked 6x too fast (fixed 3599cb6, /2 -> /12); (2) even at the right rate the LLE MB8842<->06XX command/response handshake (chip-select pulse phase, external-IRQ delivery, read-byte count) could not be synchronised, so the score chip returned zeros. Resolved by replacing the LLE with a behavioural HLE 50XX that responds immediately via the proven 06XX read/write dispatch (like the 51XX/53XX HLE): models reset/player/mode/increment tables/multi-byte set-bonus+high-score and returns the 4-byte flags+BCD-score response. Verified: Xevious clears RAM test + 50XX protection, keeps sub/sound running and main IRQ on, and holds a stable attract loop for 3500+ frames (no reboot cycling).

title: foodf + gridlee: cocktail flip is addressing-entangled, not a clean framebuffer ROT180
close_reason: Deferred (not converting). foodf and gridlee are landscape (4:3) games with NO screen rotation, only a cocktail 180 flip. Unlike a clean post-render buffer reverse (mario_bros), their flip is baked into scanline/tile ADDRESSING: foodf mirrors source tile coords AND reflects intra-tile pixels (7-px) with a -8 scroll that does not reflect; gridlee reverses VRAM row+nibble order and remaps sprite Y via (271-scanline)+VBEND. Proven algebraically that foodf's flipped output != ROT180(native_unflipped), so a declarative NORMAL/COCKTAIL swap would change pixels. Correct conversion needs ROM-level pixel verification; out of scope for the rotation-standardization pass. All 9 baked-ROTATION machines are migrated.

title: Standalone CPU disassembler CLI

Helps debug sound/CPU ROMs (e.g. the Mario Bros 8049 sound program) without the full debug UI. Suggested: a bin in phosphor-cpu-validation or a small tool crate taking --cpu <name> --org <addr> <file>.
close_reason: Implemented standalone disasm CLI (tools/disasm) with raw/rom/machine modes over the shared Disassemble trait; machine mode backed by new disasm_registry in phosphor-machines (Mario Bros seeded). Docs in docs/disassembler.md.
